events.title: Last Call for Bay Beats Submissions (SF)
events.description: Last call for Bay Beats music submissions.
events.event_detail: Bay Beats is a free streaming music platform by San Francisco Public Library featuring Bay Area artists. This is a last call for music submission deadline - artists must submit their music recordings before May 31, 2026 (7:00 am to 11:00 pm). Selected artists receive $300 and get featured on the platform, reaching thousands of new listeners for free. The event is virtual and hosted by San Francisco Main Library. Artists interested in submitting should visit baybeats.sfpl.org for more information and submission guidelines.

events.title: Dirtybird Social Club
events.description: Through Jul 11 - Free event at San Francisco
events.event_detail: Dirtybird Social Club is a community-driven series by the iconic house/techno label Dirtybird, running May 2 - July 11, 2026 at various San Francisco venues. The free RSVP event features diverse activities including pickleball at Bay Padel, evening runs with Midnight Runners, open decks and art gallery at The Faight, workout classes with LuxFit, beach cleanup at Ocean Beach, bar trivia at O'Reilly's, outdoor yoga at Baker Beach, and the annual Back To Baysics day party at Embarcadero Plaza. Events happen at 8:00AM and span movement, music, fitness, games, food, and community programming. The series rewards participation with a physical punchcard system offering chances to win a golden ticket to Dirtybird Campout x Northern Nights. Originally inspired by DIY events and pop-up BBQs, this returns to Dirtybird's roots while celebrating their diverse Bay Area fanbase built over 21 years.

events.title: Mill Valley En Plein Air Invitational
events.description: Mill Valley En Plein Air Invitational a group exhibition of oil on canvas at The Depot Gallery.
events.event_detail: The Mill Valley En Plein Air Invitational is a group exhibition of oil on canvas artwork at The Depot Gallery, located at Depot Café and Bookstore. This event is part of the First Tuesday ArtWalk program, with a special ArtWalk event scheduled for Tuesday, May 5, 2026 from 5:30 pm to 7:00 pm. The exhibition runs throughout May 2026. Attendees can view and appreciate plein air paintings created outdoors, browse the bookstore, and enjoy coffee at the café. Admission is free. The venue is open Sun-Tue 8am-5pm and Wed-Sat 8am-8pm.

events.title: Found in the Fog SF Antique & Collectibles Market
events.description: SF Antique and Collectibles Market featuring vintage finds and unique treasures.
events.event_detail: Found in the Fog is a curated outdoor antique and collectibles market held in San Francisco's Marina District. The event takes place on Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm at Marina Middle School (3500 Fillmore St, SF 94123). Attendees can explore vintage finds, antiques, handmade goods, and one-of-a-kind treasures from local vendors and collectors. The market features food trucks, live music, and family-friendly activities. Tickets cost $10-20 at the door depending on entry time, or $15 for an all-access advance purchase. It's a great opportunity to discover unexpected treasures, support local sellers, and experience neighborhood energy in the foggy Marina.

events.title: Golden Gate Coastal Trail— Alex Nizovsky
events.description: Art exhibition of acrylic on canvas by Alex Nizovsky at Mill Valley Lumber Yard
events.event_detail: Golden Gate Coastal Trail is an art exhibition featuring acrylic paintings on canvas by Alex Nizovsky, presented as part of the First Tuesday ArtWalk series. The exhibition runs from March through May 2026 at Mill Valley Lumber Yard, located at 129 Miller Ave in Mill Valley, CA. Visitors can attend the First Tuesday ArtWalk reception on Tuesdays from 5:30 to 7:30 pm, though specific dates should be confirmed. The venue is open daily from 8:00 am to 9:00 pm. Admission is free. Attendees can view the artwork, explore the unique Mill Valley Lumber Yard space, and potentially meet the artist during reception events.

events.title: Works from our Active Adults
events.description: Works from our Active Adults a group exhibition in various mediums
events.event_detail: Works from our Active Adults is a group art exhibition featuring works in various mediums, presented by the Mill Valley Community Center and First Tuesday ArtWalk. The exhibition runs throughout May 2026 at the Mill Valley Community Center (180 Camino Alto, Mill Valley, CA 94941). A special First Tuesday ArtWalk event takes place on Tuesday, May 5, 2026 from 5:30 pm to 7:30 pm. Regular exhibition hours are 8:30 am to 5:00 pm. Admission is free. Attendees can view artwork created by active adults, participate in the ArtWalk event, and explore the community center gallery.

events.title: Election - Vote Center
events.description: Fremont Main Library is an 11-day Vote Center for the June 2, 2026 election. The Alameda County Registrar of Voters will have in-person voting available in the library Meeting Room.
events.event_detail: Fremont Main Library serves as an 11-day Vote Center for the June 2, 2026 election. The Alameda County Registrar of Voters provides in-person voting in the library Meeting Room. Early voting runs May 23 through June 1 from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Election Day on June 2 has extended hours from 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM. Voters can register, update their registration, and cast ballots at this location. The event is suitable for adults. No appointment is needed to vote.

events.title: Election - Vote Center
events.description: Newark Library is an 11-day Vote Center for the June 2 primary election. The Alameda County Registrar of Voters will have in-person voting available in the library Meeting Room.
events.event_detail: Vote Center for the June 2 primary election at Newark Library. The Alameda County Registrar of Voters provides in-person voting in the library Meeting Room. The 11-day early voting period runs May 23 through June 1, 2026, from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Election Day voting is June 2, 2026, from 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM. Voters can cast their ballots, update registrations, or request vote-by-mail ballots at this location. Bring valid photo identification to vote.

events.title: Butterfly Spring: McCosker Loops
events.description: Drop-in Program - Spring butterfly hike at Sibley
events.event_detail: Butterfly Spring: McCosker Loops is a seasonal butterfly observation event offered by East Bay Regional Parks. The event takes place along the McCosker Loop trail, typically during spring months when butterfly activity is highest. Participants can expect to observe various butterfly species in their natural habitat while walking through scenic park terrain. The event is suitable for nature enthusiasts, families, and anyone interested in learning about local butterfly populations and their habitats. Specific meeting times, registration requirements, and additional details can be found on the East Bay Regional Parks registration page.

events.title: f/8 and Be There — Steve Disenhof
events.description: f/8 and Be There photography by Steve Disenhof at Coldwell Banker - Mill Valley
events.event_detail: f/8 and Be There is a photography exhibition by Steve Disenhof presented as part of the First Tuesday ArtWalk at Coldwell Banker in Mill Valley. The exhibition runs throughout May 2026, with a special ArtWalk event on Tuesday, May 5, 2026 from 5:30 pm to 7:30 pm. Regular viewing hours are Monday through Sunday, 9:00 am to 5:00 pm. Admission is free. Attendees can view the photography collection and explore the art gallery during the event.

events.title: Election - Vote Center
events.description: Vote at your Library! The Castro Valley Library will be a 4-Day Voter Accessible Location. Saturday, May 30 thru Monday, June 1, 9:00am to 5:00pm. Election Day: Tuesday, June 2, 7:00am to 8:00pm.
events.event_detail: Vote Center at the Castro Valley Library. The library serves as a 4-Day Voter Accessible Location for the election. Early voting available Saturday, May 30 through Monday, June 1 from 9:00am to 5:00pm. Election Day voting on Tuesday, June 2 from 7:00am to 8:00pm. A secure, official ballot box is available to the left of the library entrance for ballot drop-off. Voters can cast their ballots in person or use the drop box. Visitors should check the Alameda County Registrar of Voters website for voter registration information, exact times, and other voting locations. Suitable for adults.

events.title: CCCFM Farmers Market Walnut Creek
events.description: Open Year-round. Eating in Season is the best way to get the most flavor out of your farm-fresh fruits and vegetables. Vegetables, fruits, cheeses, smoked fish, cheesecakes, bread and pastries, seafood, eggs, hummus, pasta, microgreens, tamales, honey, flowers, pork, lamb, and goat.
events.event_detail: CCCFM Farmers Market Walnut Creek is an open-air farmers market held every Saturday from May 31, 2026 through December 27, 2026, from 9:00 AM to 1:00 PM. The market is located at 1799 Locust St, Walnut Creek and is open year-round. Shoppers can find fresh seasonal produce including vegetables, fruits, cheeses, smoked fish, cheesecakes, bread and pastries, seafood, eggs, hummus, pasta, microgreens, tamales, honey, flowers, pork, lamb, and goat. The market is walking distance from BART. Free parking is available for the first hour at Grower's Square (1646 N. California, entrance at Cole St) with standard rates applying after the first hour. Visitors can enjoy eating in season for maximum flavor from farm-fresh items.

events.title: Cave Adventures With CaveSim
events.description: CaveSim is a realistic cave with over 60 feet of tunnels to explore, a 12 foot vertical caving tower, cave rescue practice with a real stretcher, STEM lessons with working cave rescue phones, and energetic games about bat biology.
events.event_detail: Cave Adventures With CaveSim is a library event featuring a realistic portable cave experience with over 60 feet of tunnels to explore, a 12-foot vertical caving tower, cave rescue practice with a real stretcher, STEM lessons with working cave rescue phones, and games about bat biology. The event runs from 9:00 AM to 4:30 PM at the Millbrae library branch. Participants can crawl through tunnels, test their careful-explorer skills, and learn about caves and bats. Activities are suitable for all ages, with the mobile cave best for ages 5 and up. Children ages 3-4 can participate with an adult or responsible sibling. While not wheelchair accessible, children who use wheelchairs can explore by getting out and crawling through. This is a free library program organized by San Mateo County Libraries.

events.title: Splash Park
events.description: Splash park open at El Cerrito Swim Center
events.event_detail: Splash Park at El Cerrito Swim Center is a family-friendly outdoor water play area featuring various spray features where kids can cool off and have fun in the water. This is a non-lifeguarded area with no pool access. The event runs on Sundays from 9:00 AM to 12:30 PM during summer months. Ages 7 and under can attend Monday through Friday, while all ages are welcome on weekends. Drop-in fee is $5 per person for ages 2 and older, with children under 1 year free. A 15-punch pass is available for $63 for residents or $79 for non-residents. Participants must choose between Splash Park and the 7 & Under Swim program and cannot switch between them during the same visit. The event takes place at 7007 Moeser Ln, El Cerrito, CA 94530.

events.title: Antioch Farmers' Market
events.description: Every Sunday 9am-1pm, in the parking lot at 3rd & I St in Downtown Antioch.
events.event_detail: The Antioch Farmers' Market is a certified farmers' market hosted by the California Farmers' Markets Association (CFMA). It takes place Saturdays from 9am to 1pm starting May 31, 2026 through June 28, 2026, located in the Rivertown District Downtown Antioch at 3rd & I St. The market offers fresh fruits and vegetables direct from farmers, grass fed beef, fresh fish, flowers, eggs, local honey, and gourmet artisan food specialties. Thousands of households attend each week to purchase fresh, local produce and support local farmers and producers.

events.title: Dyeing with Nature
events.description: Registration Required - Natural dye workshop at Sunol
events.event_detail: Dyeing with Nature is a hands-on natural dyeing workshop offered by East Bay Regional Parks at the Sunol Visitor Center. Participants meet plants used for natural dyes on a short one-mile hike, then learn the dye process while coloring their own item to take home. The event runs on Sunday, May 31, 2026, from 9:30 AM to 3:00 PM. Participants must be 16 years or older and registration is required. The workshop uses modern pantry staples combined with natural ingredients to create color. Attendees should bring an item to dye (white cotton fabric, t-shirt, or bandana works well). No prior experience needed.

events.title: Irish Hurling & Gaelic Football Finals in San Francisco (Treasure Island)
events.description: San Francisco GAA St. Patrick's Cup Finals featuring Gaelic football and hurling.
events.event_detail: The San Francisco GAA St. Patrick's Cup Finals is one of the Bay Area's most unique sporting events, held on Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 9:30 am to 5:30 pm at Páirc na nGael on Treasure Island (13th Street and Avenue E). The event features the fast-paced Irish sports of Gaelic football and hurling. Gaelic football combines elements of soccer, rugby, and basketball with players kicking, passing, and battling for points. Hurling, often called the fastest sport on grass, features high-speed action and incredible skill. San Francisco is home to some of the top hurling clubs in the United States. The finals feature men's and women's championship matches, an energetic Irish sporting community, food and drinks, and family-friendly fun. Whether you have Irish roots or are discovering Gaelic games for the first time, this is a rare opportunity to experience Ireland's national sports in the Bay Area. Admission is $10 (cash only) with plenty of free street parking available.

events.title: Lower Nob Hill Trash Cleanup with Free Sandwich
events.description: Weekly volunteer cleanup with free sandwich for participants
events.event_detail: The Lower Nob Hill Trash Cleanup is a free community volunteer event held every Sunday morning. Volunteers meet at Another Cafe (1191 Pine Street at Leavenworth Street, meet on the Leavenworth side) at 9:45am to receive supplies, a cleanup route, a partner, and instructions. Teams head out promptly at 10:00am to pick up trash, returning by 11:00am. After the cleanup, volunteers can enjoy free food and connect with fellow community members. Since July 2021, dedicated volunteers have come together to clean sidewalks, build connections, and take pride in improving their shared space. The event is funded by the Civic Joy Fund, with support from Refuse Refuse, Another Cafe, and Cheaper Than Therapy Comedy Club. Supplies are provided by SF Public Works.

events.title: Free Admission Day: We Are Bruce Lee Exhibit
events.description: Free admission day for the We Are Bruce Lee exhibit.
events.event_detail: Free Admission Day at the Chinese Historical Society of America (CHSA) celebrating Asian American & Pacific Islander Heritage Month on Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. Visitors enjoy unlimited viewing of the We Are Bruce Lee exhibit and the Challenging a Whitewashed History exhibit, featuring a new addition revealing Bruce Lee's connections to San Francisco and Oakland. A free public lecture titled "Chinese Americans and Civil Rights: Celebrating the 250th Semiquincentennial" is scheduled at 1 p.m. Guests also have access to the CHSA gift shop. This complimentary admission day is presented alongside the free Cultural Festival in Chinatown on Grant Avenue. Located at 965 Clay St in San Francisco's Chinatown neighborhood.

events.title: Activity: 歡唱音樂金曲 / Pop-Up Karaoke Station
events.description: Pop-up karaoke station activity at Chinatown branch
events.event_detail: Pop-Up Karaoke Station at San Francisco Public Library Chinatown Temporary Site. This event takes place on Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 10:00 AM to 11:45 AM at 950 Grant Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94108. Attendees can enjoy singing karaoke with family and friends, performing popular music hits. The program is conducted in Chinese (Cantonese and Mandarin) and English. This is a drop-in event with no registration required. All SFPL locations are wheelchair accessible. The event is wheelchair accessible and sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library. Perfect for families and groups looking for a fun, free activity singing popular songs together.

events.title: Manny's Neighborhood Trash Cleanup with $1 Beer
events.description: Community cleanup with $1 beer, free yoga, and free fries
events.event_detail: Manny's Neighborhood Trash Cleanup is a weekly community volunteer event held every Sunday from 10:00 am to 11:00 am at Manny's venue (3092 16th St, San Francisco, CA 94103) in the Mission District. The event is hosted by SF Public Works, TogetherSF, Shine On SF, and Manny's. Participants spend an hour picking up trash around the neighborhood to help keep the area clean. Gear is provided by the organizers. After completing the cleanup, volunteers receive a certificate with same-day discounts to local businesses, including $1 PBRs at Blondies, free yoga classes at HAUM Yoga and Love Story Yoga, free small fries at Beehive Bar, 2-for-1 empanadas at Venga Empanadas, and discounted drinks at various bars. The event is free but requires RSVP through the TogetherSF Mobilize page. Participants are encouraged to bring layers and comfortable shoes for the outdoor activity.

events.title: Computer help in English Sundays
events.description: Come and get basic computer help every Sunday 10-12pm. Tutoring is in English only.
events.event_detail: Computer help in English Sundays is a free weekly tutoring session offering basic computer assistance at the César E. Chávez Branch of Oakland Public Library. The event takes place every Sunday from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM. Participants can receive help with computer skills, technology questions, and digital literacy. Appointments can be made by calling ahead, or attendees can drop in on a first come, first served basis after scheduled appointments. The session is conducted in English only and is suitable for adults seeking computer assistance.

events.title: Cultural Festival in Chinatown 2026
events.description: Cultural celebration in San Francisco's Chinatown
events.location: 1138 Grant Avenue, San Francisco, CA, USA
events.event_detail: Cultural Festival in Chinatown 2026 is a street fair celebrating Asian culture and heritage, presented by the Chinatown History and Culture Association and sponsored by Civic Joy Fund. The event takes place on Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 10 AM to 4 PM at 1138 Grant Avenue in San Francisco's historic Chinatown district. Attendees can expect street vendors, free cultural activities including calligraphy lessons, painting workshops, and Chinese medicine consultations. Live performances feature lion dance, kung fu demonstrations, music, and martial arts shows throughout the day. The schedule includes an opening ceremony at 11 AM and a cultural parade from 2:30-3:30 PM. This family-friendly event offers a relaxed atmosphere to experience vibrant culture, tasty food, and lively entertainment in an open-air setting.

events.title: Free Cultural Festival in Chinatown + Street Fair
events.description: Cultural festival celebrating Chinatown with food and performances
events.event_detail: Free Cultural Festival in Chinatown + Street Fair takes place on Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 10:00 am to 4:00 pm at Grant Avenue in San Francisco's Chinatown neighborhood (1138 Grant Ave, San Francisco, CA 94133). This free event is presented by the Chinatown History & Culture Association with title sponsor Civic Joy Fund. Attendees can expect a vibrant street fair with vendors, free cultural activities including calligraphy, painting, martial arts demonstrations, musical performances, and lion dance performances. Free Chinese medicine consultations are available, along with free calligraphy lessons where visitors can find their Chinese surname and learn to create a Chinese calligraphy style painting. The schedule includes the opening ceremony at 11 am and a cultural parade from 2:30-3:30 pm. RSVP is required to get free tickets via Eventbrite. The event celebrates the vibrant culture, tasty food, and lively atmosphere that makes Chinatown special, making it perfect for friends and families to enjoy together.

events.title: Tall Ship Tour - RSVP
events.description: Tall ship tour with RSVP required
events.event_detail: Join Call of the Sea for a free dockside tour of the Bay Area's own tall ship, the Matthew Turner. This 132-foot wooden brigantine was built in Sausalito, CA by the nonprofit Call of the Sea, launched in 2017, and has been sailing the Bay since 2020. It serves as an educational platform for students of all ages in seamanship, marine science, nautical history, and team building. The event takes place at the Richmond Ferry Terminal, 1453 Harbour Way, Richmond, CA. Free admission, but RSVP is required in advance. Tour runs Sunday May 31, 2026 from 10:00 am to 3:00 pm. Attendees can explore the ship, learn about maritime history, and enjoy views of San Francisco Bay.

events.title: 5th Annual Clayton Pride Parade and Festival
events.description: Largest Pride Parade in Contra Costa County
events.event_detail: 5th Annual Clayton Pride Parade and Festival celebrating LGBTQQIA+ pride with theme "Just Love, No Label." Takes place Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM along Main Street in downtown Clayton with an expanded festival at The Grove Park. Features a parade with colorful floats, captivating drag performances, and live music. KTVU Meteorologist Roberta Gonzales serves as Grand Marshal and keynote speaker; Former Clayton Mayor CW Wolfe is emcee. Festival includes LGBTQ+ resource information tables, local artisans, food trucks, and a Kids' Area with games, crafts, and storytelling. Supported by Clayton residents, Clayton Business and Community Association (CBCA), churches, and local businesses. Free event, no tickets needed.

events.title: Free In-Person English Class | Clase de inglés en persona gratuita
events.description: Learn English in this free in-person class taught by a certified instructor. We will learn and practice English that will be helpful in your everyday life.
events.event_detail: Free in-person English class taught by a certified instructor at the Millbrae library branch. Learn and practice English that will be helpful in everyday life. This class is suitable for adults (19+) and is 55+ friendly. The session runs from 10:00 AM to 11:30 AM. No registration required - just drop in. Available in both English and Spanish instruction.

events.title: Mental Health First Aid Training
events.description: Most of us would know how to help if we saw someone having a heart attack—we'd start CPR, or at the very least, call 9-1-1. Would you know how to respond if you saw someone having a panic attack or if you were concerned that a friend or colleague was struggling with their mental health?
events.event_detail: Mental Health First Aid Training is an 8-hour certification course held at Millbrae Library. The training takes place across two sessions: May 30 from 10:00 AM to 2:00 PM in the Library Lounge, and May 31 from 10:00 AM to 2:00 PM in the Makerspace. Participants learn the Mental Health First Aid Action Plan and work through multiple scenarios to help someone in distress. The course teaches how to safely identify and address mental health and substance use concerns, improving understanding and confidence in starting important conversations. Attendees will receive certification upon completing both sessions and gain tools to support community members and loved ones. Registration is required, and participants must attend both days to become certified. This is an educational workshop suitable for adults (19+) focused on health, wellness, and life skills development.

events.title: Tamalpais High School Students — AP Studio Art Photography and Senior Ceramics
events.description: Photography and ceramic works by AP Studio Art Photography and Senior Ceramics
events.event_detail: An exhibition featuring photography and ceramic works by Tamalpais High School students from AP Studio Art Photography and Senior Ceramics classes. The exhibition runs throughout May 2026 at the Mill Valley Public Library in the Lower Level Gallery. A special First Tuesday ArtWalk event takes place on Tuesday, May 5, 2026 from 5:30 pm to 7:30 pm. Gallery hours are Monday through Thursday 10am-8pm, Friday 10am-5pm, and Saturday and Sunday 12pm-5pm. Admission is free. Attendees can view student artwork, meet the young artists, and enjoy an evening art walk experience in the community.

events.title: Cultural Festival in Chinatown 2026
events.description: Cultural festival celebrating Chinatown heritage
events.location: 1138 Grant Avenue, San Francisco, CA, USA
events.event_detail: Cultural Festival in Chinatown 2026 is a vibrant street fair celebrating Asian heritage and community culture. The event takes place on Sunday, May 31, 2026, from 10 AM to 4 PM along Grant Avenue in San Francisco's historic Chinatown neighborhood (venue at 1138 Grant Avenue). Organized by the Chinatown History and Culture Association with title sponsorship from Civic Joy Fund, this free public event features street vendors, live performances including lion dances, kung fu demonstrations, and musical entertainment. Attendees can participate in FREE cultural activities such as Chinese calligraphy lessons (including surname calligraphy to create personalized Chinese-style paintings), painting workshops, and complimentary Chinese medicine consultations. A cultural parade is scheduled from 2:30-3:30 PM. The opening ceremony begins at 11 AM. The event runs for 6 hours in person, offering a relaxed, family-friendly atmosphere to experience authentic Chinatown culture, food, and traditions.

events.title: Coffee & Connections
events.description: Coffee & Connections networking event at Santa Clara City Library
events.location: Santa Clara City Library, Central Park Library, 2635 Homestead Rd
events.event_detail: Coffee & Connections is a community networking event hosted by the City of Santa Clara's Recreation & Community Services Department. This event provides an informal, welcoming setting for community members to meet new people, build relationships, and enjoy coffee while connecting with others in the neighborhood. Typically held on a recurring basis, the event encourages local residents to gather, socialize, and strengthen community bonds over a warm cup of coffee. No registration is required, making it accessible to all who wish to attend.

events.title: Owl Pellets: Bones, Breaks & Breakfast
events.description: Drop-in Program - Owl pellet dissection program at Coyote Hills
events.event_detail: Owl Pellets: Bones, Breaks & Breakfast is an educational nature program offered by East Bay Regional Parks. Participants will learn about owl biology and eating habits by examining owl pellets to discover what prey owls consume. The program likely takes place at a park visitor center or nature study area. Participants can expect hands-on exploration of owl pellets, learning to identify animal bones and understand food chains. This family-friendly activity combines science education with natural discovery, suitable for children and adults interested in wildlife.

events.title: Madrone Artist Grant - Call for Artists 2026
events.description: Through Jun 01 - Free event at Madrone Art Bar
events.event_detail: The Madrone Artist Grant is a $1,500 microgrant and group showcase program supporting emerging and mid-career San Francisco-based visual artists. The application period runs from April 1 to June 1, 2026. Four artists will each receive $1,500, with their work featured in a group showcase at Madrone Art Bar. The grant is open to SF County visual artists aged 21 and older, with no application fee required. Funds can be used to support any aspect of an artistic practice. Recently featured in the SF Examiner, Madrone Art Bar has long served as a gathering space for artists, writers, musicians, and neighbors, making it a quiet incubator for San Francisco's creative life. Visit madroneartbar.com/madrone-artist-grant to learn more and apply.

events.title: Chinatown History & Culture Association Presents Cultural Festival in Chinatown 2026
events.description: Free event at San Francisco Chinatown
events.event_detail: Cultural Festival in Chinatown 2026 is presented by the Chinatown History & Culture Association with title sponsor Civic Joy Fund. This free, all-ages street fair takes place on Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM on Grant Avenue in San Francisco's Chinatown. Attendees can expect a vibrant celebration featuring street fair vendors, free cultural activities including calligraphy and painting lessons, Chinese medicine consultations, and live performances such as lion dances, kung fu demonstrations, and musical performances. The schedule includes the opening ceremony at 11 AM and a cultural parade from 2:30-3:30 PM. Bring friends and family to experience the rich culture, tasty food, and lively atmosphere that makes San Francisco's Chinatown special.

events.title: Yoga by the Water at Treasure Island (SF)
events.description: Bayfront yoga with sweeping Bay views
events.event_detail: Yoga by the Water is a weekly outdoor yoga event held every Sunday at Cityside Park on Treasure Island in San Francisco. The event runs from 10:15am to 11:15am and is led by Outdoor Yoga SF instructors. Participants can expect an all-levels vinyasa flow class with sweeping views of the San Francisco skyline and the Bay. The class costs $15 with advance registration recommended, and limited spots are available each week. Attendees should bring their own personal mat and dress in layers as the weather can be cool. Restrooms are available on site and there is ample parking. After class, visitors can stay to explore the waterfront paths, grab coffee or brunch, or enjoy the views from the island. The venue is accessible via a ferry from the San Francisco Ferry Building, taking just eight minutes.

events.title: Sunday Storytime
events.description: Drop-in Program - Sunday storytime at Tilden Nature Area
events.event_detail: Sunday Storytime is a recurring weekly event held at East Bay Regional Parks. This event appears to be a children's storytime program where young attendees can enjoy reading stories, likely in an outdoor park setting. The event is part of the East Bay Regional Parks District programming. Specific dates, times, and exact park location details are not clearly displayed on this registration page.

events.title: Sunday Storytime
events.description: Sunday storytime at Tilden Regional Park
events.event_detail: Sunday Storytime is a free children's book read-aloud program held at the Environmental Education Center in Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley. Families gather at the front desk where a wonderful children's book is read aloud. The event runs on select Sundays in May 2026 (May 10, 17, 24, 31) from 10:30 to 11:00 am. This is a drop-in program with no registration required, perfect for babies, toddlers, preschoolers, and grade schoolers. After the storytime, families can explore the park's trails and nature areas.

events.title: This New Place
events.description: This New Place group exhibition of mixed media works at Poet and the Bench
events.event_detail: This New Place is a group exhibition of mixed media artworks presented by Poet and the Bench as part of the First Tuesday ArtWalk. The exhibition runs throughout May 2026 at Poet and the Bench gallery, located at 6 Throckmorton Avenue in Mill Valley, CA. Gallery hours are Tuesday through Sunday from 10:30 am to 5:00 pm. A special First Tuesday ArtWalk event takes place on Tuesday, May 5, 2026 from 5:30 pm to 7:30 pm, offering an evening opportunity to view the artwork alongside other participating venues. Admission is free. Attendees can explore the mixed media works, meet the artists, and enjoy the Mill Valley community art scene. Parking is available via metered spots, free street parking, and nearby parking lots.

events.title: Flow & Root: Water, Memory, Place — Elizabeth Addison
events.description: Elizabeth Addison's newest prints & dimensional works are created with a hybrid process.
events.event_detail: O'Hanlon Center for the Arts presents Flow & Root: Water, Memory, Place, an exhibition of paintings by Elizabeth Addison in the Loft Gallery. The exhibition runs throughout May 2026 with free admission. Gallery hours are Tuesday through Saturday from 10:30 am to 2:30 pm. Visitors can explore the artist's hybrid printmaking process that combines digital and traditional techniques with kirigami elements. Key events include an opening reception on May 5th from 5:30-7:00 pm and an artist tour sponsored by NCWCA on May 15th at 11:00 am. The exhibition showcases Addison's phthalo-forward palette inspired by the Smith River's waters, reflecting her exploration of freshwater ecosystems as living, dynamic entities.

events.title: Wake Up The Farm
events.description: Drop-in Program - Morning farm program at Ardenwood
events.event_detail: Wake Up The Farm is an event offered by East Bay Regional Parks. The event appears to be an early morning farm-related activity held at an East Bay Regional Park location. Participants can expect to engage with farm life, possibly including animal care, gardening, or agricultural activities during the early hours. This is likely an outdoor event that takes place on a farm or farm-themed area within the regional park system. Specific dates, times, and registration details would be found on the provider's website. The event is suitable for those interested in sustainable agriculture, farm animals, or outdoor morning activities.

events.title: Coal Mine Experience
events.description: Registration Required - Mine tour experience at Black Diamond Mines
events.event_detail: Coal Mine Experience is an educational event offered through East Bay Regional Parks. Participants can expect an immersive guided tour exploring a historical coal mine site, learning about the region's mining heritage, industrial history, and the geological aspects of coal formation. These experiences typically involve descending into the mine shafts with a knowledgeable guide who explains mining techniques, equipment, safety practices, and the lives of miners who worked in the area. Participants should be prepared for cool underground temperatures, uneven terrain, and enclosed spaces. The event is likely held at a designated historical mining site within the East Bay Regional Parks District. Specific dates, times, and meeting locations would be listed on the registration page. Appropriate clothing and closed-toe shoes are recommended. Children may need to meet minimum age requirements. Advanced registration is typically required.

events.title: Playtime Storytime
events.description: Come along for an active, playful family storytime. Hear new stories and get your wiggles out with the whole family. We'll play and learn together!
events.event_detail: Playtime Storytime is an active, playful family storytime program for children ages 2-5. The event takes place at the San Carlos branch of San Mateo County Libraries from 10:30 AM to 11:00 AM. Attendees can expect to hear new stories, participate in movement activities, and get their wiggles out together as a family. The program encourages play and learning in a group setting. Adults must be accompanied by a child to attend. This is an English-language program suitable for preschoolers and their caregivers.

events.title: Jewish Papercutting Workshop
events.description: Join San Mateo County Libraries as we welcome local Judaic Artist, Writer, Teacher, and Chef Lisa Rauchwerger for a hands-on papercutting workshop in celebration of Jewish American Heritage Month.
events.event_detail: Jewish Papercutting Workshop is a hands-on art event hosted by San Mateo County Libraries at the Atherton branch. The workshop takes place from 10:30 AM to 12:30 PM, celebrating Jewish American Heritage Month. Participants will learn about the history of Jewish papercutting, receive instruction on the basics of the craft, view samples of work by local Judaic artist Lisa Rauchwerger, and then try creating their own designs using provided materials. The event is suitable for adults (19+) and seniors (55+), with no prior experience required. Participants can choose from simple pre-designed templates or create their own original patterns. All materials are provided by the library. This is an excellent opportunity to explore a traditional Jewish art form in a welcoming, educational environment.

events.title: Origami Workshop: Wishes
events.description: Explore the art of origami while reflecting on history and the human experience. In this hands-on workshop, participants will learn to fold a traditional origami crane.
events.event_detail: Origami Workshop: Wishes is a hands-on arts and creativity workshop held at San Mateo County Libraries in Foster City. The event runs from 10:30 AM to 12:30 PM and is part of the One Book, One Coast series. Participants will explore the art of origami while learning to fold a traditional origami crane, a symbol of hope, peace, and resilience. The workshop encourages reflection on history and the human experience, particularly Japanese American history connected to World War II experiences of being uprooted, separated from loved ones, and facing uncertainty. Attendees will connect historical perspectives to present-day events while creating their origami crane. This program is intended for adults (18+) and is 55+ friendly. Due to high demand, participants are asked to sign up for only one occurrence so more community members can participate. Materials are provided by the library.

events.title: 2026 San Francisco Queer Art & Music Festival
events.description: Weeklong Pride celebration with DJs, bands, drag queens, and artists
events.event_detail: The 2026 San Francisco Queer Art & Music Festival is a weeklong celebration returning for its 2nd year to kick off San Francisco Pride month. Happening May 31 through June 7, 2026, this free event takes over multiple venues across San Francisco's Tenderloin neighborhood. The festival features local and national DJs, bands, drag queens, and visual artists in a fun and irreverent celebration of queer creativity, community, and culture. The opening event on May 31 starts at 11:00 am at 620 Jones venue. Attendees can expect live performances, art exhibitions, DJ sets, and drag shows throughout the week at various locations in the Tenderloin area. RSVP is required for entry.

events.title: Bookworm Block Party
events.description: Block party celebrating books
events.event_detail: The Bookworm Block Party is an outdoor literary fair taking place on Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 11:00 am to 5:00 pm in downtown Berkeley at Center Street @ Martin Luther King, Jr. Way. This free event is the heart of Northern California's largest weekend literary event, featuring nearly 150 literary-themed exhibitors including authors, independent booksellers, publishers, and literary organizations. Attendees can meet favorite authors, discover new reads, and enjoy live presentations on four outdoor and eight indoor stages. The YouthLit Corner offers family-friendly activities led by the Social Justice Children's Book Fair and ArtEsteem. Additional highlights include the Poetry Stage with 25+ poets, YouthLit Read-Aloud and Family Stages, a new Chill Zone, Small Press Alley featuring indie presses, Health in Community Row with free health services, and delicious food from local food trucks. The event welcomes all ages.

events.title: Explore Modern Thrillers: Cults + Corruption at The Marsh
events.description: Modern thriller performances
events.event_detail: Explore Modern Thrillers: Cults + Corruption is a free author panel discussion part of the 2026 Bay Area Book Festival. Taking place Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 11:00 am to 12:00 pm at The Marsh in Berkeley, this event features authors Sarah Gailey, Jendia Gammon, Luke Goebel, and Paddy Hirsch exploring conspiracy, cults, and corruption in modern thriller fiction. The discussion covers themes of closed communities promising salvation, corporations concealing truths, and individual grief fueling public violence. Moderated by Marie Sutro, host of Twisted Passages and author of Dark Obsessions, attendees can expect conversation about writing paranoia, sustaining suspense, and the thriller genre's role in confronting power systems. The event is free to attend.

events.title: Union Square Daily Programming: Mahjong Lessons2026-05-31T16:00:00
events.location: Event Location147 Fulton St San FranciscoCA94102
events.event_detail: Union Square Daily Programming: Mahjong Lessons is a recreational activity taking place on May 31, 2026 at 4:00 PM. The event offers participants the opportunity to learn Mahjong, a traditional Chinese tile game, in a group setting at Union Square in San Francisco. Attendees can expect to receive instruction on Mahjong rules, gameplay strategies, and techniques suitable for beginners. The daily programming suggests this is part of an ongoing series of activities offered in the Union Square area. Participants should arrive ready to learn a new game and interact with others interested in Mahjong.

events.title: Head West at Fourth Street
events.description: Free event at Fourth Street
events.event_detail: Head West at Fourth Street is an outdoor marketplace and community event held on Fourth Street in Berkeley. Taking place on select fifth Sundays throughout 2026 (March 29, May 31, and August 30), the event runs from 11:00 AM to 5:00 PM and is free and open to all ages. Attendees can expect to browse local vendors, shops, and potentially enjoy food and entertainment along the Fourth Street corridor. The event is hosted by Head West Marketplace, with tickets available through their website. This is a great opportunity to explore the Fourth Street neighborhood while supporting local businesses.

events.title: Reverie — Linda Herzog
events.description: Herzog's work invites viewers to pause, dream, and reflect on the surrealist landscapes she creates.
events.event_detail: Reverie is an art exhibition featuring paintings by Linda Ridd Herzog at ÆRENA Galleries and Gardens in Mill Valley, CA. The exhibition runs May 1-31, 2026, with gallery hours Tuesday through Sunday from 11:00 am to 6:00 pm. Admission is free. Herzog's work ranges from playful to contemplative, inviting viewers to pause, dream, and reflect on surrealist landscapes she meticulously paints using eyelash-size brushes. The exhibition showcases both large-scale paintings and intimate works, presenting her distinctive vision and imaginative storytelling. Attendees can immerse themselves in a vivid, surrealist world and view the art both in-person at the gallery and online. The venue is located at 53 Throckmorton Ave.

events.title: Free Art Chalk Party on Hippie Hill
events.description: Art and chalk party with snacks, games, and music
events.event_detail: Free Art Chalk Party on Hippie Hill in Golden Gate Park. A community art event where participants use chalk to create art and envision Love as a catalyst for revolution. Scheduled for Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 11:00 am to 4:00 pm. The gathering takes place at Hippie Hill near the Janis Joplin tree in Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, CA 94117. Attendees can participate in chalk art creation, enjoy snacks, games, music, and good vibes. The event encourages bringing a park blanket to sit and create on. This free community event welcomes everyone and celebrates art, activism, and togetherness in a park setting.

events.title: Lindy in the Park Swing Dance Party
events.description: Weekly swing dance party in Golden Gate Park
events.event_detail: "Lindy in the Park" is a free weekly outdoor swing dance party held every Sunday in Golden Gate Park near the de Young Museum. The event runs from 11:00 am to 2:00 pm and features free beginner swing dance lessons taught by Hep Jen from noon to 12:30 pm. No partner is required as they rotate leaders and followers. The event takes place on JFK Drive between 8th and 10th Avenue when streets are closed to traffic. This community event operates rain or shine except for rain and Bay to Breakers weekend, which cancel it. Even holidays like New Year's Day, Christmas, and Fourth of July won't stop the dancing if they fall on Sunday. The event is completely free and open to all skill levels, from beginners to experienced dancers. Participants can expect live music, social dancing, and a friendly atmosphere in one of San Francisco's most iconic parks.

events.title: Garden Helpers
events.description: Drop-in Program - Garden volunteering at Tilden Nature Area
events.event_detail: Garden Helpers is a volunteer event at East Bay Regional Parks where participants assist with gardening tasks such as planting, weeding, mulching, and general garden maintenance. The event typically takes place outdoors in a park garden area. Volunteers work together to help maintain and beautify the park's garden spaces. This is a hands-on, outdoor activity suitable for individuals and families interested in nature, gardening, and community service. Participants should wear comfortable clothing and closed-toe shoes suitable for light physical work.

events.title: Bay Area Book Festival
events.description: Join OPL at the 2026 Bay Area Book Festival. As the Bay Area Book Festival (BABF) enters its 12th year, it stands as both a cultural celebration and a critical gathering space.
events.event_detail: The Bay Area Book Festival (BABF) is an outdoor literary celebration entering its 12th year, serving as a gathering space where activists, authors, and audiences unite around today's most urgent issues and uplift marginalized voices. Oakland Public Library is participating in this event. The festival runs from 11:00 AM to 5:00 PM in Downtown Berkeley. Attendees can expect author presentations, performances, book readings, and opportunities to engage with literary culture. Suitable for adults and families. Check the Bay Area Book Festival website for specific dates and complete schedule details.

events.title: Patchwork Redwood City Craft Fair
events.description: Local makers selling handcrafted goods
events.event_detail: Patchwork Show is a bi-annual makers festival held at Courthouse Square in downtown Redwood City. This one-day craft fair features local emerging artists, crafters, junior entrepreneurs, and designers selling handcrafted goods alongside artisan food, DIY crafting activities, and live music. The event takes place on Sunday, May 31, 2026, from 11:00 am to 5:00 pm. Attendees can explore a lively plaza surrounded by restaurants, shops, and a museum while supporting small local businesses. The festival has grown from a small parking lot craft fair into multiple Bay Area locations, each showcasing makers and collaborations that reflect the local community. Admission is free for all ages.

events.title: Sand Globe Festivity
events.description: Sand globe activity at Albany Bulb
events.event_detail: Sand Globe Festivity is a free all-ages creative community event held at Albany Bulb beach (1 Buchanan St, Albany, CA) to celebrate Earth Day. On May 31, 2026 from 11am-2:30pm, environmental artist Zach Pine teaches participants to make sand globes from moist sand and water—a technique that takes just 5 minutes to learn. Attendees can create spontaneous, evolving, and ephemeral sand globe creations together, play cooperative games like "pass the peas," learn to catch and juggle sand globes, and aim to break the world record for the largest sand globe (slightly bigger than a basketball). The event takes place at the very southeast end of the beach near the parking lot. Registration is recommended via Eventbrite.

events.title: Free Astrology Class: Use Mars for Your Highest Potential! (May 31st)
events.description: Free astrology class focusing on Mars energy
events.event_detail: Free astrology class teaching beginners how to use Mars in their astrology chart for finding their true calling. This 1 hour 15 minute online class via Zoom takes place on Sunday, May 31st at 11 AM Pacific time. Participants will learn what Mars represents in their astrology chart, how Mars guides them to their true purpose, connects with inspiration, and supports taking action. The class also covers next steps for learning to read astrology charts. Taught by Linda Mendonsa from Astrology Learners Academy with over 40 years of astrological experience. Attendees arriving on time are entered in a drawing to win a free 30-minute private chart reading tutorial with the instructor. Use code 'mars' to register and receive Zoom meeting information.

events.title: Bianca Collins — Sky Ranch Gallery's Featured Artist for May
events.description: Bianca Collins will be the Featured Artist for May at Sky Ranch Gallery in Tomales, CA
events.event_detail: Bianca Collins is the Featured Artist for May 2026 at Sky Ranch Gallery in Tomales, CA. Her exhibition runs throughout May and features oil paintings ranging from quiet landscapes to animal portraits. The artist splits her time between Napa and Sonoma counties, capturing scenes and moments that resonate with her. The gallery offers free admission with specific visiting hours: Monday and Thursday 11:00 am - 2:00 pm, and Friday, Saturday, and Sunday 11:00 am - 3:00 pm. Visitors can view her works including pieces like "Dory in Maine" and "Hide and Seek" while exploring the gallery space located at 27000 CA-1, Tomales, CA 94971.

events.title: From the Beginning
events.description: From the Beginning watercolor/gouache From the 1940's by John Grillo
events.event_detail: From the Beginning is an art exhibition featuring watercolor and gouache works from the 1940s by artist John Grillo, presented at Robert Green Fine Arts as part of the First Tuesday ArtWalk and Mill Valley Art Dealers Association. The exhibition runs throughout May 2026, with a special First Tuesday ArtWalk event on Tuesday, May 5th from 5:30-7:30 pm. Regular gallery hours are Friday-Sunday, 11:00 am - 5:00 pm, with Monday-Thursday by appointment. Admission is free. Attendees can view the vintage watercolor and gouache pieces by John Grillo, explore the gallery, and participate in the community ArtWalk event. The venue is located at 154 Throckmorton Ave., Mill Valley, CA 94941.

events.title: Baby Wearing Dance
events.description: For adult caregivers and pre-walking babies. Participants must bring their own baby carrier. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event.
events.event_detail: Baby Wearing Dance is a health and fitness event for adult caregivers and pre-walking babies. Participants dance together while wearing their babies in baby carriers. The event takes place from 11:00 AM to 12:00 PM at Cupertino Library in Santa Clara County. Participants must bring their own baby carrier. This is a family-friendly activity suitable for parents and caregivers looking to exercise with their infants in a fun, social environment at the library.

events.title: 2026 Bay Area Book Festival + Bookworm Block Party
events.description: 12th annual book festival with author talks and block party
events.event_detail: The 2026 Bay Area Book Festival (BABF) enters its 12th year as Northern California's largest weekend literary event. The Bookworm Block Party takes place on Sunday, May 31, 2026, from 11:00 am to 5:00 pm, centered on streets surrounding Allston Way in Downtown Berkeley. This free outdoor fair features nearly 150 literary-themed exhibitors, including emerging authors, independent booksellers, local publishers, and writing organizations. Attendees can meet favorite authors, discover new reads, and enjoy live presentations on four outdoor and eight indoor stages across multiple venues (The Marsh Berkeley, Freight & Salvage, The Magnus, Brower Center, Hotel Shattuck Plaza). The festival includes a YouthLit Corner with activities curated by the Social Justice Children's Book Fair, a Chill Zone, and delicious food from local food trucks. Saturday, May 30 features Writers' Workshops and Democracy Dialogues. The daytime festival is FREE and open to the public, with ticketed evening headliner events available separately ($21.99).

events.title: Wax: It's the Bee's Knees!

events.title: Coal Mine Experience

Participants can expect to descend into the mine tunnels, see mining equipment and artifacts, and learn from knowledgeable guides about the mining process and working conditions. The event is held at a designated historic mine site within the East Bay Regional Parks system. Participants should wear comfortable clothing and closed-toe shoes suitable for uneven underground terrain. Children must be accompanied by an adult. This is a family-friendly educational activity suitable for history enthusiasts and curious visitors of all ages.

events.title: Wax: It's The Bee's Knees!
events.description: Wax program at Ardenwood Historic Farm
events.event_detail: Wax: It's The Bee's Knees! is an educational family event at Ardenwood Historic Farm in Fremont exploring the fascinating world of beeswax. The event takes place on Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 11:30 am to 12:30 pm. Attendees will learn about the importance of beeswax to both bees and humans while participating in a hands-on candle-making activity and sampling Ardenwood honey. This drop-in program requires no registration and is wheelchair accessible. Ardenwood admission fee applies ($6 adults, $5 seniors, $4 children, free for under 4). Starting April 29th, Ardenwood becomes cashless. For information call (510) 544-2797.

events.title: NPU Live, Illuminate, and San Francisco Recreation and Park Department Present The Whale's Tail: Caroline Wolfson, Dan Dectis, Evan Wardell, Keepers of Humanity
events.description: Free event at The Whale's Tail
events.event_detail: The Whale's Tail is a free, all-ages outdoor music event held at The Whale's Tail venue in San Francisco's Golden Gate Park. Taking place on Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 12:00PM to 6:00PM, the event features live performances by Caroline Wolfson, Dan Dectis, Evan Wardell, and Keepers of Humanity throughout the afternoon. Presented by NPU Live, Illuminate, and San Francisco Recreation and Park Department, attendees can enjoy live music, lawn games, and food from Los Kuyas food truck. The venue offers Adirondack chairs and picnic tables for seating. Family-friendly with kids and dogs welcome. Part of a regular weekend series open May through October.

events.title: Side Gate Brewery's First-Ever Pups on the Patio Party
events.description: Bring your pup and enjoy Side Gate Brewery's first-ever Pups on the Patio Party — a full day of craft beer, dog-friendly activities, food, and community.
events.location: Side Gate Brewery & Beer Garden, Concord
events.event_detail: Side Gate Brewery's first-ever Pups on the Patio Party is a dog-friendly celebration of craft beer and community held on May 31, 2026 from 12pm to 10pm at Side Gate Brewery & Beer Garden located at 1822 Grant Street in Concord, CA. The free admission event features limited-edition Brew Biscuits made with spent grain from their Planter Box Pilsner, a raffle where buying a pint enters you to win a 4-pack for humans plus a 4-pack of dog beer, guided Paint Your Pet sessions from 2-5pm, a dog-friendly outdoor patio for meeting fellow dog lovers, and food from Limitless Kitchen serving burgers, sandwiches, street dogs, and fries. Attendees can enjoy local craft beer while their dogs play and socialize in the beer garden.

events.title: Illuminate Live and San Francisco Recreation & Parks present Golden Gate Bandshell Concerts
events.description: Through Nov 15 - Free event at Bandshell Music Concourse
events.event_detail: Illuminate LIVE and San Francisco Recreation & Parks present Golden Gate Bandshell Concerts at the Bandshell Music Concourse in Golden Gate Park. This free outdoor concert series runs from March through November 2026, with shows most Wednesdays, Fridays, and Sundays at 12:00PM, plus select Saturdays and special events. The 2026 season includes over 125 free performances featuring independent artists, local legends, cultural celebrations, and community gatherings. Now in its sixth year, the historic bandshell—renovated in 2020 with state-of-the-art sound and lighting—has hosted 700+ free concerts since 2020, welcoming nearly 1 million music lovers. The series extends SF Music Week into a months-long run of free public performances at one of the Bay Area's most vibrant and accessible outdoor venues. All ages welcome.

events.title: Yoga
events.description: Interested in learning how to do yoga or already have a practice, and want to join other adults in your community for free classes? Experienced instructor Ted Harvey will offer a combination of movement, meditation and breathing for stress relief.
events.event_detail: Free yoga class offered by San Mateo County Libraries at the Half Moon Bay branch. Classes are held from 12:00 PM to 1:00 PM. Experienced instructor Ted Harvey leads participants through a combination of movement, meditation and breathing exercises designed for stress relief, relaxation and mind-body connection. The class welcomes all skill levels, from beginners to those with an existing practice. Participants are asked to bring their own towel or mat. Suitable for adults (19+) and seniors. This is a community health and wellness event focused on making yoga accessible to everyone.

events.title: Reading Buddies
events.description: Reading Buddies provides students in grades K-3 with an opportunity to improve their reading skills by working one-on-one with a reading coach.
events.event_detail: Reading Buddies is a library reading program at the Berryessa Branch Library for students in grades K-3. The event provides children with one-on-one practice with a reading coach who listens to them read and offers support with reading and comprehension skills. Sessions run from 12:00 PM to 1:00 PM, with each participant receiving at least 20 minutes with a coach. Children can bring their favorite book or choose from the library's selection. Free tickets are required, available at the Information Desk up to 30 minutes before the program starts. This event is designed to help beginning and developing readers build confidence. Suitable for kids ages 5-10. Note: This event has been canceled.

events.title: Crafty Sundays
events.description: Crafty Sundays is a fun and creative library program where participants can explore their artistic side through various craft activities.
events.event_detail: Crafty Sundays is a weekly creative art program at San Mateo County Libraries held at the North Fair Oaks branch. Children ages 6-11 can explore their artistic side through various hands-on craft activities. The program runs on Sundays from 12:00 PM to 1:00 PM, offering a relaxed and fun environment suitable for all skill levels. Library provides craft materials, and activities may include painting, paper crafts, or other age-appropriate projects. Available in English and Spanish.

events.title: Maker Exploration
events.description: Discover our 3D printers and laser cutter with hands-on guidance from our Maker volunteers!
events.event_detail: Maker Exploration is a hands-on maker event at the Foster City Library branch of San Mateo County Libraries. The event runs from 12:00 PM to 2:00 PM. Participants can discover and use 3D printers and laser cutters with guidance from Maker volunteers. During 3D Printing sessions, attendees learn Tinkercad and create their own printable design (20-minute print limit). For Laser Cutting, participants use a Glowforge machine to make a personalized acrylic charm (2" square size limit). Drop-ins are welcome as space and time allow. This event is suitable for children ages 6-11 and teens ages 12-18. It focuses on art, creativity, technology, innovation, and STEAM education.

events.title: Family Puzzle Time
events.description: Stop by for a relaxing time working on puzzles with family and friends.
events.event_detail: Family Puzzle Time is a relaxing indoor event held at the Vineland branch library where families and friends can enjoy working on puzzles together. The event takes place from 12:00 PM to 3:30 PM and is suitable for all ages including adults, teens, kids ages 5-10, and pre-teens. This is a drop-in style program categorized as Games and Family Entertainment, conducted in English. Attendees can expect a casual, laid-back atmosphere to solve puzzles at their own pace with family members or friends. The library provides the puzzles, making this a free, low-key activity perfect for quality time together.

events.title: English & Math Tutoring
events.description: Need help with English and Math homework? Whether it's homework help or tutoring needed to improve in the subject, schedule an appointment with our volunteer who can help with English and math subjects for all grades including college level.
events.event_detail: English & Math Tutoring is a free homework help and tutoring session offered at the Hillview library branch. Sessions run from 12:00 PM to 2:00 PM. Volunteer tutors provide assistance with English and Math subjects for all grade levels, including college-level students. Registration is required - interested participants should email cassandra.ponce@sjlibrary.org to schedule an appointment. This service is suitable for adults, teens (ages 12-18), pre-teens (ages 10-12), and kids (ages 5-10). Note that help is limited to school subjects in English and Math only. Participants should bring their homework assignments, textbooks, and any specific questions they need assistance with.

events.title: Free Oakland Up Market
events.description: Shop for free treasures and art materials
events.event_detail: Free Oakland Up is a free market and Social Practice Project by Jocelyn Meggait, open every Friday through Sunday from 12-4 PM at 2809 MacArthur Blvd, Oakland, CA. The market offers free materials for art, collage, and junk journals including ephemera, electronics parts, books, CDs, DVDs, magazines, and household goods. All outdoor items are completely free to take (except tables, bins, and shelves). Indoor visitors can choose one free item per person per day, with additional items available for a monetary donation. Some plants and select treasures are for sale to help cover rent and expenses. The shop aims to keep usable items out of the landfill.

events.title: Marin City Library Puzzle Swap!
events.description: Have a bunch of puzzles sitting at home that you've already completed? Feel like being adventurous and puzzling over a new challenge with others? Join us for fun and relaxing puzzle swap! We'll set out a community puzzle folks can work on together.
events.event_detail: Join us for a fun and relaxing puzzle swap at Marin City Library! Bring your completed puzzles to swap with others, work on a community puzzle together, and take home new puzzles for free. The event runs from 12:00 PM to 4:30 PM at the Marin City Library branch. Make sure any puzzles you bring have all their pieces. This is a great opportunity for adults to meet fellow puzzle enthusiasts, enjoy a social afternoon, and discover new puzzle challenges. No registration required.

events.title: Side Gate Brewery's First-Ever Pups on the Patio Party
events.description: Side Gate Brewery is rolling out the welcome mat for our four-legged friends with its very first Pups on the Patio Party on Sunday, May 31 — a celebration of craft beer, community and canine companionship! Brew Biscuits, raffle prizes, paint your pet experience, and more. FREE event.
events.location: Side Gate Brewery & Beer Garden, 1822 Grant Street, Concord, CA 94520
events.event_detail: Side Gate Brewery's First-Ever Pups on the Patio Party is a free dog-friendly celebration of craft beer and canine companionship held on Sunday, May 31 from 12–9pm at Side Gate Brewery & Beer Garden (1822 Grant Street, Concord, CA 94520). Attendees can enjoy special Brew Biscuits made with spent grain from the brewery's Planter Box Pilsner, available for purchase for their dogs. The event features raffle prizes including a 4-pack of beer for humans and 'Dog Beer' for pets. A guided paint-your-pet experience runs from 2pm–5pm. Guests can relax in the spacious outdoor Beer Garden, meet fellow dog owners, and purchase food from Limitless Kitchen including smash burgers, sandwiches, street dogs, and fries. This is a free, all-day family-friendly event welcoming four-legged friends.

events.title: Used Book Sale - Friends of the Cupertino Library
events.description: The Friends of the Cupertino Library are having a Used Book Sale! Sunday May 31 from Noon - 3 PM (Bag Sale Day). Saturday May 30 from 9 AM - 3 PM.

events.event_detail: Used Book Sale organized by the Friends of the Cupertino Library. The sale takes place Saturday, May 30, 2026 from 9 AM - 3 PM and Sunday, May 31, 2026 from Noon - 3 PM (Bag Sale Day). Located at Cupertino Community Hall, 10350 Torre Ave, Cupertino, CA 95014. Inventory includes Fiction, Non-Fiction, Paperbacks, Cookbooks, Children's Books, Select Books, Foreign Languages & Technical Books. Bag Sale Day means you can fill a bag for a flat rate. Proceeds support library programs including the Chinese Book Club, Study Sessions for SAT Tests, Tween Book Club, Adult Book Club, Summer Reading Programs, and the County Bookmobile. The event is suitable for all ages from babies to older adults. Book donations and new memberships are also accepted.
