events.title: Family Storytime
events.description: Storytime is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities such as stories, songs, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement activities.
events.event_detail: Family Storytime is a free library event held at the Hillview branch where families gather for early literacy activities. The program runs from 12:30 PM to 1:00 PM and features stories, songs, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement activities designed for children of all ages alongside their parents and caregivers. This interactive experience promotes the joys of reading and learning while helping develop early literacy skills. No registration is required to attend. The event aligns with Early Education Quality Standards and welcomes the entire family to participate together in a fun, engaging environment.

events.title: Music with Sara Jayne & Friends
events.description: Music performance with Sara Jayne & Friends
events.event_detail: Music with Sara Jayne & Friends is a live music event for toddlers and young children (ages 0-5) held every last Sunday of the month at the Starry Plough Pub in Berkeley. The show features preschool-style music with puppets, shakers, scarves, and songs the whole family can sing and dance along to. The show runs from 12:30pm to 1:00pm, with the pub opening at noon and closing at 2pm. Bar and kitchen are available. Free admission with a $10-20 suggested donation. Parents can enjoy a draught while little ones dance and participate in the interactive musical performance.

events.title: Just Dance Academy Spring Performance 2026
events.description: Just Dance Academy for their annual spring performance! A joyful afternoon of dance for the family!
events.event_detail: Just Dance Academy Spring Performance 2026 is an annual dance recital presented by Just Dance Academy in collaboration with Marin County Department of Cultural Services and Marin Cultural Association. The event features two shows on Sunday, May 31, 2026 at 12:30 pm and 5:00 pm at Showcase Theater in San Rafael. The performance opens with JDA's beautiful rendition of the classical ballet Cinderella, followed by energetic and inspiring jazz, hip hop, and contemporary dance routines. This is a joyful afternoon and evening of dance suitable for the entire family. Admission is $40 for adults and $35 for children 12 and under. Free parking is available in lots adjacent to the theater.

events.title: Family Recreational Swim
events.description: Family recreational swim
events.event_detail: Family Recreational Swim at San Leandro Family Aquatic Center. The shallow end is open for leisure swimming and splashing around. To enter the deep water, you must demonstrate the ability to swim to the lifeguard on duty. Swimsuits are required and no cotton is allowed in the pool. Each person over 1 year old pays an entrance fee. Adults must accompany children under 10 into the facility. Children under 6 must always be within arm's reach of an adult. Takes place on Sunday May 31, 2026 from 12:30 pm to 4:30 pm. Cost is $10 per person. Located at 14900 Zelma Street, San Leandro, CA 94579.

events.title: Family Games: Cards & Board Games
events.description: Children, teens, and their families are invited to play a selection of board games and card games. The games included will be a mix of strategy-based games, educational games, and luck-based games.
events.event_detail: Family Games: Cards & Board Games is a free library event where children, teens, adults, seniors, and families can play a variety of board games and card games. The event features strategy-based games, educational games, and luck-based games suitable for all ages from young children to seniors. Takes place on Saturdays from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM at the Tully Community Branch library. Participants can expect a fun, social experience playing games together with friends and family in a welcoming library environment. No registration required – just show up and enjoy the games provided by the library.

events.title: Watercolor in the Nectar Garden
events.description: Drop-in Program - Watercolor painting in the nectar garden at Coyote Hills
events.event_detail: Watercolor in the Nectar Garden is an art program hosted by East Bay Regional Parks at the Regional Parks Botanic Garden in Tilden Nature Area. Participants will learn watercolor painting techniques while surrounded by beautiful native California plants and flowers in the garden setting. The event appears to take place in the Regional Parks Botanic Garden, which is known for its diverse collection of California native plants and provides an inspiring natural backdrop for watercolor painting. Participants can expect to create their own watercolor artwork while enjoying the peaceful garden environment. The event focuses on connecting art with nature.

events.title: Digital Help Hub |Centro de Ayuda Digital
events.description: One-on-one and small-group help for real-life tech tasks. Learn what you need, at your pace.
events.event_detail: Digital Help Hub | Centro de Ayuda Digital is a free technology assistance event held at North Fair Oaks Library. It offers one-on-one and small-group help for real-life tech tasks such as sending email attachments, navigating smartphones, and other device-related questions. Tech-savvy volunteers provide personalized assistance at your own pace. No registration is required. Available in English and Español. Suitable for adults (19+).

events.title: Bloom Shaboom 2026
events.description: Community event at San Bruno Avenue location
events.event_detail: Bloom Shaboom 2026 is a free community block party organized by Family Connections Centers, celebrating art, nature, and community. The event takes place on Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 1 PM to 4 PM at 2675 San Bruno Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94134. Attendees can enjoy gardening and nature activities, carnival games, face painting, arts and crafts, live music from DJ KG, strolling through the Green Between and Portola Garden, story time with San Francisco Public Library, bike skills practice with SF Bike Coalition, and learn about the Portola neighborhood with PNA. Food and drinks will be available from food trucks and local restaurants. This family-friendly event offers fun activities for both kids and adults in an outdoor community setting.

events.title: Reading to Children with Vivian
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning.
events.event_detail: Reading to Children with Vivian is a library storytime program where volunteer Vivian reads to children in a welcoming environment. The event takes place from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM at the Cambrian branch of the San Jose Public Library. Children ages 0-5 and 5-10 can participate and enjoy one-on-one or small group interaction with the volunteer reader. The program helps children develop imagination and sparks a love for books, reading, and learning. Kids are also welcome to practice reading to the volunteer. The reading takes place in the Children's Area of the library. This is a free library program suitable for families with young children.

events.title: San Francisco Youth Leadership Exposition
events.description: Youth leadership and development event
events.event_detail: The SF Youth Leadership Expo is a Bay Area gathering bringing together student leaders, changemakers, and builders for a day of learning, networking, and skill-building. The event takes place on Sunday, May 31st from 1 PM to 5 PM (doors at 12:30 PM) at SPUR Urban Center San Francisco, located at 654 Mission Street in San Francisco, CA 94105. Through keynote conversations, practical workshops, networking sessions, and a youth organization expo, attendees will gain actionable insights on leadership, organization-building, outreach, advocacy, fundraising, social media growth, and creating meaningful community impact. Featured speakers include San Francisco Board of Supervisors President Rafael Mandelman, TikTok's Lead Product Manager Amar Saurabh, Enterprise for Youth CEO Carlo Solis, UC Berkeley Haas Interim Director Asra Khan, content creator Viraj Ala, and startup founder Alex Barra. Workshops include Social Media for Youth Organizations and Funding Basics. Free refreshments, networking opportunities, community tabling, and a matcha bar will be available throughout the event. Dress code is business casual. Attendees can expect to connect with ambitious young leaders from across the Bay Area, discover new opportunities, and strengthen skills needed to turn ideas into lasting impact.

events.title: (Virtual) Chess Club
events.description: Are you interested in playing and learning chess? If so, sign up to attend this fun virtual Chess Club hosted by Seven Trees Branch Library!
events.event_detail: Virtual Chess Club hosted by Seven Trees Branch Library for kids ages 5-12. This weekly event takes place every Sunday from 1:00pm to 2:30pm via Zoom. Participants are paired up with other kids to play real chess games using virtual chess boards on lichess.org. Library volunteers teach strategies and tips through fun activities and interactive games. No software download is required; participants just need a computer with internet and a web browser. Registration is required (register once to be added to the roster), and the Zoom link is emailed before each session. The program is free and runs year-round with flexible attendance - kids can play every week or drop in and out as they prefer.

events.title: Engineering Hub
events.description: Explore the principles of engineering through open-ended, hands-on activities using both everyday materials and makerspace tools.
events.event_detail: Engineering Hub is a hands-on STEM event held at the Half Moon Bay Library where participants explore engineering principles through creative activities. The event takes place from 1:00 PM to 3:00 PM and includes building structures with everyday materials while learning to use makerspace tools such as a laser cutter, 3D printer, vinyl cutter, soldering iron, and iFixit toolkit. Suitable for all ages including children (6-11), teens (12-18), and adults. Participants can expect to design, build, solve creative problems, and practice repair techniques in a collaborative environment. The program is bilingual in English and Español.

events.title: Drop-In 3D Printing
events.description: Drop in and learn how to 3D print. We will take you through the whole 3D printing process from start to finish!
events.event_detail: Drop-In 3D Printing is a free library program where participants can learn the complete 3D printing process from start to finish. The event takes place from 1:00 PM to 2:30 PM at the North Fair Oaks branch of San Mateo County Libraries. No registration is required, making it easy for anyone to drop in and participate. This hands-on workshop covers topics related to 3D design, printing technology, and the workflow involved in creating 3D printed objects. The program is suitable for all ages including children (6-11), teens (12-18), and adults (19+). It falls under categories of Art & Creativity, Technology & Innovation, and STEAM. Instruction is available in both English and Spanish. Attendees can expect a welcoming, educational environment where library staff guide them through operating 3D printers and understanding the technology.

events.title: Lego Club
events.description: Come join us every Sunday for Lego Club! We have tons of Lego bricks for you to build and explore! Duplo bricks are also available for our younger friends.
events.event_detail: Lego Club is a weekly hands-on building event held every Sunday from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM at the Educational Park library branch in San Jose. The event provides Lego bricks for children to build and explore, with Duplo bricks available for younger children. Participants can work on free-form creations or ask librarians for Lego challenges to try something more difficult. Children under 5 must be accompanied by their parents due to choking hazards from small pieces. Suitable for kids ages 5-10, young children ages 0-5, and pre-teens ages 10-12. English language event.

events.title: BiblioBus at Rincon Valley Library
events.description: Explore the Sonoma County Library BiblioBus! The mobile library will be on site at Rincon Valley Regional Library while the library is closed for an update.
events.event_detail: BiblioBus at Rincon Valley Library is a mobile library service event where the library's bookmobile visits the Rincon Valley Library branch. These events typically allow community members to borrow books, use library services, and access reading materials from a mobile library unit. The BiblioBus brings a selection of books and resources to the local community, offering the same services as a traditional library branch in a mobile format. Attendees can browse and borrow books, sign up for library cards, and access educational resources. These events are typically free and open to the public.

events.title: Family Games: Cards & Board Games
events.description: Children, teens, and their families are invited to play a selection of board games and card games.
events.event_detail: Family Games: Cards & Board Games is a library event where children, teens, and their families are invited to play a selection of board games and card games. The event takes place from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM at the Tully branch of San José Public Library. The games provided include a mix of strategy-based games, educational games, and luck-based games. Attendees can come together to have fun with friends and family in a welcoming indoor environment. This event is suitable for all ages including adults, teens, kids ages 5-10, young children ages 0-5, seniors, and pre-teens. The event is held in English and is part of the library's Games & Family Entertainment programming.

events.title: The Asian Art Museum presents: The Language of Flowers in Asian Art
events.description: Our Woven Heritage: Celebrating Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islanders: This May, we are celebrating AANHPI Heritage by highlighting textiles and clothing, and their importance as a method for sharing stories.
events.event_detail: The Asian Art Museum presents: The Language of Flowers in Asian Art is an educational presentation exploring the symbolic meaning of flowers in Asian art and culture. Discover how flowers like lotus, plum blossom, cherry blossom, chrysanthemum, tulip, and rose convey powerful messages in art. The event features objects from the Asian Art Museum's permanent collection and is part of the Asian American, Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander Heritage Celebration. No registration required. Runs from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM at the Corte Madera branch of Marin County Free Library. Recommended for 4th grade and up, suitable for adults, teens, and tweens. Attendees can expect to learn about the historical and cultural significance of flowers across various Asian traditions through this engaging presentation.

events.title: Parent Cafe: Summer Reading Adventure
events.description: Join us for a parent cafe to connect with other parents and learn about summer reading tips. Recommended for parents of rising 1st-3rd grade students.
events.event_detail: Parent Cafe: Summer Reading Adventure is a library event for parents to connect with other parents and learn about summer reading tips. The event takes place from 1:00 PM to 2:30 PM in Brisbane at San Mateo County Libraries. This event is recommended for parents of rising 1st-3rd grade students. Registration is required to attend. Adults (19+) can participate in this parenting and caregiving focused social support event. Attendees can expect to meet other parents, share experiences, and receive helpful tips for encouraging their children to read over the summer months.

events.title: Deep Healing and the Coming Transformation of Human Consciousness
events.description: Exploring the Forces Changing What it Means to Be Human: Michael Lerner and host Katherine Fulton
events.event_detail: The New School at Commonweal presents Deep Healing and the Coming Transformation of Human Consciousness with Michael Lerner and host Katherine Fulton on Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 1:00 pm to 3:00 pm, followed by a book launch reception from 3:00 pm to 4:00 pm. The event takes place at Gallery Commonweal (2nd floor, 451 Mesa Rd., Bolinas, CA 94924) or via Zoom. This is part of Commonweal's 50th anniversary celebrations and explores Michael Lerner's vision of healing ourselves and healing the earth, examining what he calls the coming revolution in human consciousness and what it means for individuals, communities, and as a planetary species. Lerner brings together over 230 week-long Cancer Help Programs, Healing Circles, and experiences with personal healing, in light of new research on consciousness. The event celebrates the publication of What Matters Now: 7 Letters to a Friend with Cancer. $25 suggested donation, no one turned away. Note: venue is on 2nd floor with no elevator.

events.title: Free Humphry Slocombe Pride Ice Cream Party
events.description: Pride ice cream preview party with complimentary ice cream
events.event_detail: Free Humphry Slocombe Pride Ice Cream Preview Party happening Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 1pm-2pm at Humphry Slocombe Dogpatch (699 22nd St, San Francisco CA 94107). This is a special Pride kickoff event where attendees can be the first to taste upcoming June Pride flavors. The event features complimentary scoops, celebration with friends, neighbors, community partners, and fellow ice cream lovers. Partners include Hilda and Jesse, SF LGBT Center, and Domaine Carneros. RSVP required. The shop is located in San Francisco's Dogpatch neighborhood.

events.title: Embroidery on Clothing
events.description: Customize your clothing with embroidery in this hands-on workshop.
events.event_detail: Embroidery on Clothing is a hands-on workshop taking place at Mystic in Mill Valley, CA on Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 1:00 pm to 4:00 pm. Participants learn techniques for embellishing their own clothing with embroidery to personalize their style. You can choose from stick-on wash-off templates or design your own pattern. The workshop costs $65 per person and covers how to stabilize and hoop fabric, design transfer methods, and tools of the trade. Attendees need to bring a clothing item to embroider, preferably made of natural fibers like cotton, denim, or linen. Polyester and slippery, stretchy, or fuzzy materials are not recommended. A backup clothing option is suggested in case your primary item isn't suitable.

events.title: Art Club
events.description: Visit the library to participate in arts and crafts for kids. All tools and supplies are provided. Free. No registration required.
events.event_detail: Art Club is a free arts and crafts program for children held at the Alum Rock library branch in San Jose. The event takes place from 1:00 PM to 3:00 PM. All tools and supplies are provided by the library. No registration is required to attend. The event is suitable for kids ages 5-10 and young children ages 0-5. Children can participate in various creative art activities and projects during this drop-in program. Parents or caregivers should accompany young children.

events.title: Tech Mentor
events.description: Need help printing or using Word and Excel? Want to set up an email account? Need ideas on tech security? Questions on accessing SJPL eResources? From the basics to somewhat beyond, volunteer tech mentors are here to help.
events.event_detail: Tech Mentor is a free computer help event held at King Library in San Jose. Volunteer tech mentors provide assistance with various technology topics including printing, Microsoft Word and Excel, setting up email accounts, tech security, and accessing SJPL eResources. The event runs from 1:00 PM to 3:00 PM, with no registration or appointment required - attendees can simply drop by and ask for help. This program is suitable for adults and seniors looking to improve their technology skills or get help with specific tech problems. No prior experience is needed; assistance ranges from basic to intermediate levels.

events.title: Cal Sailing Club Open House
events.description: Open house at Cal Sailing Club
events.event_detail: Cal Sailing Club Open House offers FREE introductory sailboat rides to the general public aboard a fleet of keelboats and dinghies. Open houses run from 1-3 pm on select Sundays throughout 2026 (April 5, May 31, June 28, August 2, August 30, October 4) plus May 2 during Berkeley Bay Fest. Boat rides are first-come, first-served; sign up in front of the clubhouse between 1-2:30 pm. Children must be at least 5 years old and accompanied by an adult. The club recommends first-timers and families with small children sail in larger, more stable keelboats. Participants can borrow foulies (raincoats) and life jackets at the club. Wear shoes that can get wet and comfortable clothes including a windbreaker. Bring a change of clothes as you may get soaked. The event takes place at Cal Sailing Club, 124 University Ave, Berkeley CA.

events.title: PRIDE Ice Cream Preview Party
events.description: Free event at Humphry Slocombe Dogpatch
events.event_detail: PRIDE Ice Cream Preview Party at Humphry Slocombe Dogpatch in San Francisco on Sunday, May 31 from 1:00PM to 2:00PM. This free, all-ages event celebrates the kickoff to Pride month with complimentary ice cream tastings. Attendees can be the first to sample upcoming June Pride flavors while connecting with friends, neighbors, community partners, and fellow ice cream lovers. The event features partnerships with Hilda and Jesse, SF LGBT Center, and Domaine Carneros, creating an afternoon of celebration and community connection.

events.title: Mountain View Dance Festival
events.description: Free dance festival featuring Bay Area dance groups
events.location: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.event_detail: The Mountain View Dance Festival is a free community event presented by the San Jose Ballet Association, taking place on Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 1:00 pm at the Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts (500 Castro St., Mountain View, CA). This is the first annual festival with the 2026 theme "Groundbreaking," featuring various dance groups from the Bay Area performing in different dance styles. The event aims to make the arts accessible to everyone in the community. The performance runs for 1 hour and 15 minutes with no intermission and is appropriate for all ages. Entry is free and open to the public on a first come, first served basis with limited seating available.

events.title: Tiburon Pride Picnic 2026
events.description: Family-friendly picnic with views of Golden Gate Bridge
events.event_detail: Tiburon Pride Picnic 2026 is a free, family-friendly outdoor Pride celebration taking place on Sunday, May 31, 2026, from 1:00 pm to 4:00 pm at Shoreline Park in Tiburon. The event features stunning views of the Golden Gate Bridge and San Francisco skyline. Attendees can expect a relaxed picnic atmosphere with blankets on the grass, good music from DJ Kirill, fun activities, tarot readings by Sean Anomie, and vintage finds from Disco Dacha. The event celebrates the LGBTQ+ community in a beautiful waterfront setting with an open-air gathering. Bring your friends, family, and favorite picnic setup - or just come as you are. This is a free community event welcoming everyone to celebrate Pride together.

events.title: Mango Party in the Park: Free Mangoes & DJs
events.description: Free mangoes and DJs in the Mission
events.event_detail: Mango Party in the Park is a free outdoor event celebrating Indian mangoes, described as the 'fruit of the gods.' The event features free mangoes and DJs playing music. It takes place on Sunday, May 31, 2026, from 1:00 pm to 4:00 pm at Mission St. and 20th St. in San Francisco's Mission District. This grassroots event aims to introduce Americans to better mangoes and offers attendees a chance to enjoy fresh mangoes while listening to DJ music in an outdoor park setting. The event is free and open to the public.

events.title: Golden Gate Park Sunday Roller Disco Party
events.description: Weekly roller disco with DJ and groovy tunes
events.event_detail: Golden Gate Park Sunday Roller Disco Party is a free outdoor roller skating event held every Sunday from 1:00 pm to 5:00 pm at Skatin' Place, located at 6th Avenue and Kennedy Drive in Golden Gate Park, San Francisco. This iconic event features the Godfather of Skate with his mobile DJ unit playing groovy tunes. Attendees can skate to the music, learn choreographed roller disco dance moves from experienced skaters, and enjoy the vibrant community atmosphere. The venue is officially dedicated as the home for outdoor roller skating in San Francisco. Skaters of all skill levels are welcome, with opportunities for beginners to learn and experienced skaters to show off their moves.

events.title: San Francisco Youth Leadership Exposition
events.description: Youth leadership development event
events.event_detail: The San Francisco Youth Leadership Exposition is a Bay Area gathering for student leaders, changemakers, and builders. The event takes place on Sunday, May 31 from 1 PM to 5 PM (doors at 12:30 PM) at SPUR Urban Center San Francisco, 654 Mission Street, San Francisco, CA 94105. Attendees will participate in keynote conversations, practical workshops covering topics like social media for youth organizations and funding basics, networking sessions, and a youth organization expo. Featured speakers include San Francisco Board of Supervisors President Rafael Mandelman, TikTok's Lead Product Manager Amar Saurabh, and other nonprofit leaders, startup founders, and industry professionals. The event includes free refreshments and a matcha bar. Dress code is business casual. This is a great opportunity for students leading clubs, nonprofits, advocacy initiatives, or passion projects to gain actionable insights on leadership, organization-building, outreach, and creating meaningful community impact.

events.title: Golden Gate Park Band Free Symphony in the Park
events.description: Free weekly concert by 30-piece symphony since 1882
events.location: Spreckels Temple of Music (Golden Gate Park Bandshell)
events.event_detail: The Golden Gate Park Band presents its 144th season of free outdoor concerts at the Spreckels Temple of Music in Golden Gate Park's Music Concourse. This 30-piece symphony has been performing free concerts since 1882. The May 31, 2026 concert features "Songs and Dances" with works by Morton Gould, Frank Ticheli, and more. Concerts run most Sundays from 1:00 pm to 2:30 pm (approximately 70-90 minutes) through September 27th. The event is free and open to the public, though donations are welcome. Performances often feature music of specific nationalities or cultures with costumed guest performers including dancers, singers, and speakers. The venue is located between the de Young Museum and the California Academy of Sciences. Attendees can bring blankets or lawn chairs to sit on the grass and enjoy the symphony in the beautiful park setting.

events.title: Bloom Shaboom 2026
events.description: Community event and festival
events.event_detail: Bloom Shaboom 2026 is a free community block party celebrating art, nature, and community, organized by Family Connections Centers. The event takes place on Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 1 PM to 4 PM at 2675 San Bruno Avenue in San Francisco. Attendees can expect gardening and nature activities, carnival games, face painting, arts and crafts with FCC, live music from DJ KG, strolling through the Green Between and Portola Garden, story time with San Francisco Public Library, bike skills practice with SF Bike Coalition, learning opportunities about the Portola neighborhood with PNA, and food from food trucks and local restaurants. The event is designed for both kids and adults to enjoy.

events.title: Club de tejer en crochet || Crochet Club
events.description: Unete a nuestro programa de crochet para principiantes, abierto a todas las edades. Las y los participantes aprenderan tecnicas basicas de crochet y, a medida que desarrollen sus habilidades, podran crear proyectos sencillos como portavasos.
events.event_detail: Club de tejer en crochet (Crochet Club) is a beginner-friendly crochet program at San Jose Public Library's Biblioteca Latinoamericana branch. The event runs from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM and is open to all ages including adults, teens, pre-teens, and seniors. Participants will learn basic crochet techniques and have the opportunity to create simple projects such as coasters and placemats as they build their skills. The program is conducted in Spanish with English speakers welcome in a supportive and inclusive environment. Free admission with no registration required. Suitable for adults ages 18+, teens ages 12-18, seniors ages 65+, and pre-teens ages 10-12. Part of the Family Learning Centers program under Crafts & Hobbies.

events.title: BiblioBus at Rincon Valley Library
events.description: Explore the Sonoma County Library BiblioBus! The mobile library will be on site at Rincon Valley Regional Library while the library is closed for an update.
events.event_detail: The BiblioBus at Rincon Valley Library is a mobile library outreach event. The BiblioBus brings library services and resources directly to the community at the Rincon Valley Library branch. Attendees can expect to check out books, access library materials, and engage with library staff. The BiblioBus typically visits on a scheduled basis, bringing a wide selection of reading materials to the local community.

events.title: 4th Annual Gamelan in the Garden at SF Botanical Garden
events.description: Balinese music and dance performances
events.event_detail: 4th Annual Gamelan in the Garden at San Francisco Botanical Garden. This free outdoor event features traditional Balinese music and dance performances by Gamelan Sekar Jaya. Schedule includes Gender Wayang music (1-1:30pm) at Fountain Plaza, Jegog bamboo marimba orchestra (1:30-2:20pm) at Great Meadow, interactive Harmonic Drift percussion ensemble all afternoon, Artist Meet & Greet (2:30-3:30pm) with Indonesian desserts and refreshments, and Gong Kebyar/Angklung final performance (3:30-5:30pm) in Celebration Garden. Free admission for San Francisco residents; non-residents pay regular park admission. Located in Golden Gate Park at 1199 9th Avenue, San Francisco.

events.title: Free In-Person English Class | Clase de inglés en persona gratuita
events.description: Learn English in this free in-person class taught by a certified instructor. We will learn and practice English that will be helpful in your everyday life.
events.event_detail: Free in-person English class taught by a certified instructor. Learn and practice everyday English in a supportive environment. Classes are held from 1:00 PM to 2:30 PM at the Foster City library branch. Suitable for adults (19+) who want to improve their English language skills for daily life. Bilingual instruction available in English and Spanish.

events.title: Free Block Party: Bloom Shaboom w/ Live Music
events.description: Block party with live music
events.event_detail: Free Block Party: Bloom Shaboom is an annual celebration of art, nature, and community organized by Family Connections Centers. The event takes place on Sunday, May 31, 2026, from 1:00 pm to 4:00 pm at the BMO Parking Lot (2675 San Bruno Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94134). Attendees can enjoy gardening and nature activities, carnival games, face painting, and arts and crafts. Live music will be provided by DJ KG. Families can stroll through the Green Between/Portola Garden, participate in story time with San Francisco Public Library, practice bike skills with SF Bike Coalition, and learn about the Portola neighborhood with PNA. Food and drinks will be available from food trucks and local restaurants. This free celebration offers fun for both kids and adults. Registration is required (free).

events.title: Social: Afternoon Board Games
events.description: Afternoon board games social event
events.event_detail: Social: Afternoon Board Games is a free drop-in event hosted by the San Francisco Public Library at the Sunset Branch. The event takes place on Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 1:00 PM to 4:00 PM in the Sunset Children's Area. Attendees can discover new board games or enjoy old favorites in a friendly, social setting. This event is designed for children and their caregivers to enjoy together. No registration is required. The program is wheelchair accessible, and accommodations such as ASL can be requested by contacting the library at least 3 business days in advance. This event is sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library.

events.title: FULL Workshop: Learn to Become a Dungeon Master
events.description: Full workshop to learn to become a Dungeon Master
events.event_detail: FULL Workshop: Learn to Become a Dungeon Master - A 6-week beginner-friendly workshop at San Francisco Public Library's Main Library (Mix: Lounge, 2nd Floor) teaching the fundamentals of running tabletop roleplaying games. Scheduled for Sunday, 5/31/2026 from 1:00 - 3:00 PM. Participants will explore storytelling, worldbuilding, encounter design, improvisation, and tips for guiding players through engaging adventures. Perfect for new or aspiring Dungeon Masters looking to build confidence, develop creative skills, and start running games for friends. No prior DM experience required. Space is limited and reservations are required. This is a free library program sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library, designed for ages 8-18. Attendees can expect hands-on learning, interactive activities, and guidance from experienced instructors in a supportive environment.

events.title: Friends of the Library Children's Book Sale
events.description: Children's Book Sale includes books, games, puzzles, DVDs, and more, plus a special education section for teachers, all to raise money for the library. Bag Sale: $4 per bag or $10 for 3 bags.
events.location: Petaluma Meeting Room at Petaluma Regional Library
events.event_detail: The Friends of the Library Children's Book Sale is a fundraising event where community members can purchase discounted children's books. These sales are typically organized by volunteer library supporters, with proceeds often benefiting library programs, children's services, or facility improvements. Attendees can expect to find a variety of children's literature including picture books, early readers, chapter books, and young adult titles at reduced prices. The event provides an excellent opportunity for parents, grandparents, and caregivers to build home libraries at affordable prices while supporting their local library system. Books are usually organized by age group or category to help shoppers find appropriate selections. Early arrival is recommended as popular titles tend to sell quickly. Payment is typically accepted at the event, with many sales offering additional pricing deals like fill-a-bag specials.

events.title: Tech Mentor
events.description: Need help printing or using Word and Excel? Want to set up an email account? Need ideas on tech security? Questions on accessing SJPL eResources? From the basics to somewhat beyond, volunteer tech mentors are here to help.
events.event_detail: Tech Mentor is a free computer help session at King Library in San Jose. Volunteer tech mentors provide one-on-one assistance with technology basics including printing, Microsoft Word, Excel, email account setup, tech security, and accessing SJPL eResources. The event runs from 1:00 PM to 3:00 PM. No registration or appointment is required—attendees can simply drop by for assistance. This program is designed for adults and seniors seeking help with technology questions, from basic to intermediate level. The service is free and open to the public.

events.title: Mottainai - Rope Bowl Making Class
events.description: Explore the intersection of craft and history through the lens of mottainai—the Japanese philosophy of respect and waste-reduction.
events.event_detail: Mottainai - Rope Bowl Making Class is a craft workshop exploring the Japanese philosophy of mottainai (respect and waste-reduction). This mindset helped Japanese Americans during WWII incarceration camps turn limited resources into handmade necessities. Instructor Katie Furukawa Bonifacio guides participants through sewing their own rope bowl using beautiful Japanese scrap fabrics while sharing reflections on her family's incarceration experience. The event connects to George Takei's 'They Called Us Enemy' and is part of the One Book, One Coast community reading event. Suitable for teens ages 12-18. Takes place from 1:00 PM to 2:30 PM at the Belmont branch of San Mateo County Libraries. Participants will learn basic sewing techniques while exploring themes of resilience and resourcefulness from Japanese American history.

events.title: Fremont Adult Tabletop Gamers

Playwright Sharr White transforms Sultan's work into a moving exploration of family mythologies, as the Marin County resident turns his lens on his parents, traveling from his Greenbrae home to their San Fernando Valley house over a decade. The play wrestles with generational differences and the search for deeper understanding between a son and his parents. Best for children ages 0-8 with their caregivers, the event runs from 4:00 PM to 5:00 PM. Storytime takes place from 4:00-4:30pm and includes early literacy activities such as stories, songs, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement activities designed for the whole family. After storytime, Stay & Play continues until 5pm where children can play with toys, meet new friends, get book recommendations, and create something. The program promotes the joys of reading and learning for all ages. Free with limited capacity. Indoor program.

events.title: Free Reggae in the Park: Dub Mission 30th Anniversary
events.description: 30th anniversary celebration of Dub Mission
events.location: Spreckels Temple of Music (Golden Gate Park Bandshell)
events.event_detail: Free reggae in the park event celebrating Dub Mission's 30th anniversary at the historic Spreckels Temple of Music (Golden Gate Park Bandshell). The event runs Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 4:30pm to 7:30pm as part of the Illuminate LIVE free outdoor concert series. Resident DJs Sep, Vinnie Esparza, and Maneesh the Twister spin dub and reggae classics. This is a free, all-ages outdoor concert in Golden Gate Park's Music Concourse. Attendees can enjoy live reggae music in a scenic park setting, with room to dance or sit on the grass. The event is part of a larger 125+ free concert series running through November 2026.

events.title: Crucial Reggae Sundays: Free Weekly Reggae Concert in Golden Gate Park 2026
events.description: Free weekly reggae concert in Golden Gate Park
events.location: Spreckels Temple of Music Bandshell, Music Concourse
events.event_detail: Crucial Reggae Sundays is a free weekly outdoor reggae concert held at the Spreckels Temple of Music Bandshell in the Music Concourse of Golden Gate Park, San Francisco. The event runs almost every Sunday from March through December, with live music starting at 4:20 PM and lasting approximately 3 hours. Hosted by DJ Irie Dole, DJ Guid8nce, and DJ Sep, with weekly special guests, the event features an all-ages open-air experience with positive vibes where attendees can relax, dance, and enjoy reggae music in one of the world's most beautiful parks. Presented by Illuminate and San Francisco Recreation and Parks in association with Jah Warrior Shelter Hi-Fi, Nice Up Radio, Dub Mission, and Value Culture. The event is free to attend. Follow @CrucialReggaeSundaysSF on Instagram for weekly updates.

events.title: Crucial Reggae Sundays: Free Weekly Reggae Concert in Golden Gate Park 2026
events.description: Free weekly reggae concert in Golden Gate Park
events.location: Spreckels Temple of Music Bandshell, Music Concourse
events.event_detail: Crucial Reggae Sundays is a free weekly reggae concert held every Sunday from March through December at the Spreckels Temple of Music Bandshell in Golden Gate Park's Music Concourse. Events run for approximately 3 hours starting at 4:20 PM. The concert features live performances by DJs Irie Dole, Guid8nce, and Sep, along with weekly special guests, with Steffan Franz serving as Positivity Director. This all-ages outdoor event is one of northern California's premier open-air weekly reggae experiences, held in one of the world's most beautiful parks. Attendees can expect to relax, dance, and enjoy positive vibes in a welcoming community atmosphere. The event is presented by Illuminate and San Francisco Recreation and Parks in association with Jah Warrior Shelter Hi-Fi, Nice Up Radio, Dub Mission, and Value Culture. Admission is free.

events.title: Breaking Open: A Night of Solo Stories and Playback Theater
events.description: Solo stories and playback theater performance
events.event_detail: Breaking Open: A Night of Solo Stories and Playback Theater is an intimate, powerful evening of truth-telling and human connection hosted by Marin Shakespeare at 514 Fourth Street Theatre in San Rafael. The event takes place on Sunday, May 31, 2026 from 5:00 pm to 7:00 pm. The show features performers from the Formerly Incarcerated People's Performance Project (FIPPP), who share raw, heartfelt solo stories exploring vulnerability, humor, grief, and resilience. Their performances illuminate the complexities of survival, incarceration, and transformation. The evening culminates in an interactive Playback Theater experience by Marin Shakespeare's Returned Citizens Theatre Troupe (RCTT), where audience members are invited to share their emotional responses and see them spontaneously brought to life on stage. This is a free event with sliding scale tickets ranging from $0 to $37, making it accessible to all.

events.title: Supercosmos of Dreams — Jean-Marc Brugeilles
events.description: Jean-Marc Brugeilles paintings have a surreal quality, because they are inspired by dreams.
events.event_detail: Supercosmos of Dreams is an art exhibition featuring oil on canvas paintings by Jean-Marc Brugeilles at Throckmorton Theatre. The artist's surreal work is inspired by dreams, exploring themes of daily life, poetry, and the human soul through rich symbols and timeless imagery. The exhibition runs throughout May 2026, with a special First Tuesday ArtWalk and artist reception on Tuesday, May 5 from 5:00 pm to 7:00 pm. Attendees can view the paintings during regular theatre hours or by appointment. The exhibition is free to attend and held at Throckmorton Theatre, 142 Throckmorton Avenue in Mill Valley.

events.title: Convention Snapshots; Family Snapshots; Business Snapshots — Marin Theatre
events.description: Photography and written text by Larry Sultan
events.event_detail: Photography and written text exhibition by Larry Sultan featuring three series: Convention Snapshots, Family Snapshots, and Business Snapshots. The exhibition is part of the First Tuesday ArtWalk, a community event where attendees can walk between multiple venues to view art. The ArtWalk takes place on Tuesday, May 5, 2026, from 5:30 pm to 7:30 pm. The exhibition runs throughout May 2026 at Marin Theatre. Visitors can explore the photography works, engage with the written text accompanying the images, and experience the gallery space. The event is held at Marin Theatre, 397 Miller Avenue, Mill Valley, CA 94941. Attendees should arrive early as parking may be limited.

events.title: HellaSecret Speakeasy Comedy Show & Cocktail Night
events.description: Secret pop-up comedy show at new bar in Temescal, Oakland
events.event_detail: HellaSecret Speakeasy Comedy Show & Cocktail Night is a secret pop-up comedy event held at Mesa Maguey, an agave bar and Oaxacan kitchen in Oakland's Temescal neighborhood (4031 Broadway). The show runs approximately 70+ minutes featuring 4-5 comedians with credits from venues like Cobbs, Punchline, SF Sketchfest, and networks like ABC and NBC. Shows are held multiple nights weekly (Sundays at 6p, Mondays/Tuesdays/Thursdays at 7p). Admission is free with RSVP, though venue is 21+. Attendees should arrive 20-30 minutes early with tickets ready on their phone. The bar offers curated mezcal cocktails and Oaxacan dishes like mole, tacos, and ceviche.

events.title: FREE: Hayes Valley Comedy Night at The Function
events.description: Free comedy night in Hayes Valley district
events.event_detail: Hayes Valley Comedy Night at The Function is a weekly comedy show at San Francisco's only Black-owned comedy club. Located at 1414 Market Street in the Mid Market/Hayes Valley area, the event runs Sundays at 7:00 pm (also available other nights throughout the week). Each show features 4-5 comedians with credits from venues like Cobbs, Punchline, SF Sketchfest, Clusterfest and Outside Lands. The 70-90 minute show takes place in an upscale comedy club with avant-garde decor and an upstairs lounge. Admission is FREE with Eventbrite RSVP (first 100 people get free tickets), otherwise $20-25 at door. Like most comedy clubs, there is a two-drink minimum per person to support the bar and waitstaff. Donations are appreciated and cash is recommended.

events.title: Coyote Howl
events.description: Evening coyote howl program
events.event_detail: This event invites participants to experience the natural soundscape of Santa Clara County's wildlife. Typically, a Coyote Howl event is an outdoor evening program where attendees gather in a park setting to learn about local wildlife behavior and participate in guided howling sessions. Participants can expect to explore the natural environment, observe nocturnal creatures in their habitat, and learn from park naturalists about the ecological role of coyotes in the area. The event usually takes place during evening hours, often around sunset or later, and may involve a short hike to a designated viewing area. Attendees should be prepared for outdoor conditions in an undeveloped park setting.

events.title: Full Moon Grunion Search
events.description: Registration Required - Full moon grunion fishing program at Crown Beach
events.event_detail: Full Moon Grunion Search - A unique nighttime event at East Bay Regional Parks where participants explore the beach during a full moon to observe grunion fish. Grunion are small, silvery fish known for their dramatic spawning behavior where they wash ashore onto beaches to lay eggs during spring and summer nights. This guided event typically occurs on the beach during evening/night hours around the full moon. Participants will learn about grunion behavior, conservation, and the ecological significance of these fish while enjoying the nighttime beach environment. The event is family-friendly and offers a memorable outdoor experience combining marine biology education with the magic of a moonlit beach walk.

events.title: Teen-Led Passion Projects
events.description: Are you a Morgan Hill high school student (ages 14-18) who wants to lead a program or a project here at the library? This is your chance to share your Passion Project with your community! Morgan Hill Library is accepting applications for teens to lead projects.
events.event_detail: Teen-Led Passion Projects is a library program where teens can work on projects they are passionate about. This event provides teens with the opportunity to explore their interests, develop new skills, and share their creativity with peers. Attendees can expect to collaborate with other teens, access library resources, and work on self-directed projects in a supportive environment. Teens are encouraged to bring their own ideas and materials for their passion projects.

events.title: Sunday Pony Rides at Marin Country Mart
events.description: Pony rides every Sunday at Marin Country Mart.
events.event_detail: Sunday Pony Rides at Marin Country Mart offers children the opportunity to ride ponies at this outdoor market location. The event occurs on Sunday, May 31, 2026, from 11:00am to 3:00pm. Families can visit the Mart, located behind Rustic Bakery, where kids can enjoy pony rides. This is a recurring weekly event held at the Marin Country Mart shopping center in San Rafael. Children should be accompanied by a parent or guardian, and there may be a fee per ride. The venue offers additional shopping and dining options for visitors.

events.title: Whimsical Garden: An Art Exhibit
events.description: Saratoga Library's May - June 2026 exhibit is by Megan Wu. Artist's Statement: Through my watercolor process, I try to capture that sense of wonder - the feeling of lying in the grass, watching sunlight filter through leaves.
events.event_detail: Whimsical Garden is an art exhibit featuring watercolor paintings by artist Megan Wu. The exhibit captures the sense of wonder in nature, inspired by lying in grass, watching sunlight filter through leaves, and flowers fluttering in the breeze. The exhibit runs during Saratoga Library's open hours from May 3 to June 29, 2026, displayed in the lobby. Visitors can view the artwork throughout their visit to the library during regular operating hours. The exhibit is suitable for teens, adults, and families with children. Photo courtesy of Megan Wu.

events.title: Works by the Friday Artists: Extended through May
events.description: A group exhibit featuring works in oil, pencil, and watercolor by: Katie Baxter, Karen Gray, Joyce Laws, Martha Proctor, Susan Nelson, & Sally Torrance. On exhibit April 2026 at the Point Reyes Library - extended through May.
events.event_detail: Works by the Friday Artists is a group art exhibit featuring works in oil, pencil, and watercolor by six local artists: Katie Baxter, Karen Gray, Joyce Laws, Martha Proctor, Susan Nelson, and Sally Torrance. The exhibit is on display at the Point Reyes Library and runs throughout April 2026, extended through May 2026. Visitors can view the artwork any time during library hours as an all-day event. The exhibit showcases diverse styles including watercolor pieces like 'Morning Has Broken' by Katie Baxter. This event is suitable for adults interested in local art and is held at the Point Reyes Library branch.

events.title: Live Music Sundays at Tony's Seafood
events.description: Live music every Sunday at Tony's Seafood.
events.event_detail: Live Music Sundays at Tony's Seafood is a weekly event held at Tony's Seafood Restaurant in Marshall, California. The event features live music performances every Sunday from 5:00 pm to 7:00 pm during dinner service. On May 31, 2026, the performance is by All Swing Considered, playing American Songbook Swing music. Guests can enjoy fresh seafood while taking in scenic views of Tomales Bay. Part of the Hog Island Oyster Co. family, Tony's Seafood has been a beloved waterfront gathering place since 1948, serving locals and visitors with fresh seafood rooted in West Marin's fishing traditions. The restaurant offers both reservations and walk-in dining. This is a great opportunity to combine great food, live music, and beautiful bay scenery.

events.title: Art Exhibit: Looking for Beauty and Inspiration
events.description: Looking for Beauty and Inspiration by Barbara Janis will be displayed in the Corte Madera Community Room from May 3rd through June 18th. Art has been a fascination for me since childhood.
events.event_detail: Art exhibit featuring Looking for Beauty and Inspiration by Barbara Janis displayed in the Corte Madera Community Room from May 3rd through June 18th. The artist has studied painting at multiple institutions including the Academy of Art in San Francisco, UC Berkeley, California College of Arts and Crafts, and several junior colleges. This is her first opportunity to devote quality time to her passion in retirement. An artist reception celebrating Janis and her work will be held on Sunday, May 3rd from 2-4PM. Suitable for adults. The exhibit showcases her lifelong dedication to art and her journey of artistic development.

events.title: AANHPI Heritage Month Seek & Find
events.description: Celebrate AANHPI Heritage Month with us! Search the Children's Area for images of books about AANHPI culture and experiences. Find them all to receive a prize. Complete an additional challenge on the back of the game sheet to win a second prize.
events.event_detail: Celebrate AANHPI (Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander) Heritage Month with this fun seek-and-find activity at the Clayton Community Library! Children search the Children's Area for images of books about AANHPI culture and experiences. Find them all to receive a prize, and complete an additional challenge on the back of the game sheet to win a second prize. Pick up a game sheet at the front of the library or at the Study Area/Discovery Zone counter to get started. One entry per month allowed. This event runs all day from May 1 to May 31, 2026. Perfect for preschoolers (ages 3-5) and children (ages 6-9). The program is made possible by the Clayton Community Library Foundation.

events.title: Fried Chicken Sundays at Farmshop Marin
events.description: Fried chicken special every Sunday at Farmshop Marin.
events.event_detail: Fried Chicken Sundays is a weekly dining event at Farmshop Marin restaurant in Larkspur. Every Sunday, the restaurant serves their famous Herbed Jidori Fried Chicken available by the bucket for dine-in or takeout. The event runs from 10:30am to 9:30pm on Sundays only. The specific occurrence is May 31, 2026, but this is a recurring weekly Sunday event. Attendees can enjoy fried chicken in a restaurant setting, either sitting down to dine or ordering ahead to take home. The restaurant is located at 2233 Larkspur Landing Circle in Larkspur, Marin County. This is a casual family-friendly food event focused on specialty fried chicken.

events.title: Food and Farm Tour: Flavors of Point Reyes
events.description: Food and farm tour exploring flavors of Point Reyes.
events.event_detail: Food and Farm Tour: Flavors of Point Reyes is a popular guided culinary tour through Point Reyes exploring the region's diverse food offerings. The event takes place on Sunday, May 31, 2026, from 10:00am to 3:00pm. Participants visit multiple local destinations including a renowned creamery, oyster farm, meadery, and organic vegetable farm. The $225 per person cost includes tours and tastings at all locations plus a locavore lunch. Additional alcoholic beverages are available for purchase during lunch. A minimum of 4 guests (or payment for 4 guests) is required to schedule the tour. Attendees should dress appropriately for outdoor farm walking and be prepared for a full day of tasting and touring.

events.title: Goat Yoga at Charlie's Acres Farm Animal Sanctuary
events.description: Goat yoga experience at the farm sanctuary.
events.event_detail: Goat Yoga at Charlie's Acres Farm Animal Sanctuary is an outdoor yoga class where participants practice yoga poses alongside rescued goats and sheep. The event takes place on Sunday, May 31, 2026 at 10:00am. Yoga mats are provided, and participants are positioned 6+ feet apart. The class is designed for all skill levels and is meant to be fun rather than serious. Participants should arrive 15 minutes early for check-in and to meet the animals. The 1-hour class is followed by a 30-minute meet and greet with more rescued animal residents. Ages 14+ only. If weather is bad, the event will be rescheduled. Cost is $60 per person plus fees. The event is offered April through October.

events.title: 1:1 Tech Mentor Appointment
events.description: Free. By appointment only. Call for availability. Same day booking not always possible. Offered in English, Español, or Tiếng Việt. Would you like to find out more about computers? Learn at your own pace!
events.event_detail: 1:1 Tech Mentor Appointment at Seven Trees branch of San Jose Public Library. Free personalized technology help session available by appointment only. Offered in English, Spanish, and Vietnamese. Mentors provide one-on-one assistance with computer basics, device or account setup, Microsoft Office introduction, job search and resume help, email navigation and organization, and more. Perfect for adults and seniors looking to improve their digital skills at their own pace. Contact Seven Trees by phone (408) 808-3056 or email tiffany.lam@sjlibrary.org to schedule.

events.title: Estate Sale Showroom at Fine Estate Inc
events.description: Estate sale showroom featuring antiques and collectibles.
events.event_detail: Estate Sale Showroom at Fine Estate Inc is a large-scale estate sale event held on Sunday, May 31, 2026, from 10:00am to 5:00pm at their 6,000 square foot showroom. The event features a huge selection of vintage, antique, contemporary, and mid-century modern art, furniture, collectibles, decor, toys and games, fashion and accessories, and coins from top brands. Unique pieces are added daily. Fine Estate Inc is a San Francisco Bay Area auction and estate sales service with over 25 years of experience, offering curated and well-marketed monthly auctions and bi-weekly estate sales. Photos and sales descriptions are uploaded by Wednesday, May 27, 2026 at 5 pm. Attendees can discover unique items at great prices and potentially find one-of-a-kind treasures.

events.title: Finals Frenzy Study Hall
events.description: Get Ready for Finals at the Library! Need a quiet place to focus? Join us for Finals Frenzy! We are providing a dedicated study space to help you power through your exams. Perks: Free snacks, Free water, A quiet, structured study environment.
events.event_detail: Finals Frenzy Study Hall is a dedicated study space event for students preparing for exams, hosted by Contra Costa County Library at Dougherty Station branch. The event runs all day on multiple dates in late May and early June 2026: Tuesday May 26 through Thursday May 28, Friday May 29, Saturday May 30, and Tuesday June 2 through Thursday June 4. Attendees can expect a quiet, structured study environment with free snacks and free water provided. The program is primarily targeted at teens ages 13-18 but open to any student needing a focused space for finals preparation. Location: 17017 Bollinger Canyon Road, San Ramon, CA 94582.

events.title: Sol Horizon Bob Marley Tribute at Sweetwater Music Hall
events.description: Sol Horizon Bob Marley tribute at Sweetwater Music Hall.
events.event_detail: Sol Horizon Bob Marley Tribute at Sweetwater Music Hall on Sunday, May 31, 2026. Doors open at 7:00pm, show starts at 8:00pm. Sol Horizon is Sonoma County's premier Bob Marley tribute band, featuring 8-12 musicians including horns and female background vocalists. The band has won "Best Band" awards in the North Bay Bohemian's Reader's Picks for 2022-2023 and has received the NorBay Award for "Best Reggae Band" 9 times. Attendees can expect a high-energy performance of Bob Marley classics, from well-known chart-toppers to rare cuts, with subtle musical interpretations and blazing solos. General admission tickets are $31.42. The venue is located at 19 Corte Madera Avenue, Mill Valley, CA 94941. This is an indoor concert at Sweetwater Music Hall.

events.title: Weekend French Brunch at Left Bank
events.description: Weekend French brunch at Left Bank restaurant.
events.event_detail: Weekend French Brunch at Left Bank is a French-inspired brunch event held at Petite Left Bank in Larkspur. The event takes place on Sunday, May 31, 2026, from 10:00am to 3:00pm. Attendees can enjoy a relaxed morning filled with great food, warm ambiance, and a touch of French flair. Located at 507 Magnolia Avenue, Larkspur, CA 94939, the restaurant offers traditional French dishes and a charming atmosphere perfect for meeting friends or treating yourself. Bon appetit!

events.title: Catch a Movie at CAFILM Sequoia Cinema
events.description: Movie screenings at CAFILM Sequoia Cinema.
events.event_detail: Catch a Movie at CAFILM Sequoia Cinema is a movie theater event featuring first-run independent, foreign-language, and documentary films. The event takes place on Sunday, May 31, 2026 at various times throughout the day. The Sequoia is owned and operated by CAFILM (California Film Institute), the same non-profit organization that runs the Smith Rafael Film Center in San Rafael and produces the annual Mill Valley Film Festival and Doclands Documentary Film Festival. Attendees can expect a diverse schedule of quality film programming and may encounter special guests for engaging conversations about the films. Showtimes vary, so visitors should call (625) 253-1316 or visit www.sequoiafilm.org for current schedule and ticket information.

events.title: Marin Symphony Presents Masterworks 4: Hogarth Conducts Firebird at James Dunn Theatre
events.description: Marin Symphony Masterworks 4 featuring Firebird conducted by Hogarth.
events.event_detail: Marin Symphony Presents Masterworks 4: Hogarth Conducts Firebird is a classical music concert taking place on Sunday, May 31, 2026 at 3:00pm and 7:30pm at the James Dunn Theatre, College of Marin in Kentfield, CA. This season finale features conductor Brad Hogarth, a Music Director finalist, leading the orchestra through a program spanning centuries of music. The concert opens with Handel's Overture from Music for the Royal Fireworks and closes with Stravinsky's Firebird Suite, bookending the program with fire-themed compositions. Marin Symphony Concertmaster Ani Bukujian performs Prokofiev's Violin Concerto No. 1 in D Major, a virtuosic and flavorful work. The program also includes Ravel's Ma mere l'Oye (Mother Goose) Suite. Tickets range from $43-$83 for single seats with youth pricing available for $20. Attendees can expect an elegant evening of world-class orchestral music in an intimate theater setting.

events.title: Teen Volunteer Sign-Ups for Ages 14 to 18 at Gilroy Library
events.description: Need community service hours for school? The next volunteer session at the Gilroy Library will be from June through August. Teens can sign up for a weekly 2-hour shift which they must attend for the whole 3-month period.
events.event_detail: Teen Volunteer Sign-Ups at Gilroy Library for ages 14-18. This event helps teens complete their community service hour requirements for school. The next volunteer session runs from June through August, with teens signing up for a weekly 2-hour shift over the entire 3-month session. First week of sign-ups (May 18-24) is reserved for rising high school seniors, while general sign-ups open to all ages 14-18 starting May 26th. To sign up, teens must pick up an application from the Gilroy Library Information Desk or print one from the provided link, complete it, and bring it during the sign-up period to select their shift. Requirements include being 14-18 years old and living in Gilroy or San Martin, or being a student in Gilroy Unified School District. Volunteers must attend a mandatory orientation on Saturday, May 30th at 3PM. Note: Only one 3-month session per volunteer is allowed. Shifts fill quickly, so early sign-up is recommended. Contact the Information Desk or email lib-giteen@lib.sccgov.org with questions.

events.title: Angel Island Ferry Service
events.description: Ferry service to Angel Island for hiking, biking, and exploring historic sites.
events.event_detail: Angel Island Ferry Service provides roundtrip transportation from Tiburon to Angel Island in San Francisco Bay. The ferry departs from Tiburon on May 31, 2026 at 10:00am, 11:00am, and 1:00pm (with additional times on other days). Service operates daily with varying schedules: no service Mondays/Tuesdays unless pre-booked, reduced weekday service, and expanded weekend service including Memorial Day. Roundtrip tickets are $18 for adults (13-64), $16 for seniors (65+), $15 for children (6-12), and $6 for small children (3-5). Once on Angel Island, visitors can explore historic military fortifications, hike trails, enjoy panoramic views of the Bay Area, and experience nature. The ferry terminal is located at 21 Main Street in Tiburon, Marin County.

events.title: Branch Closure - Rincon Valley Regional Library
events.description: The Rincon Valley Regional Library will close from March 16 to late June 2026 for significant upgrades, including a brand-new makerspace, a dedicated area for teens, an upgraded children's area, new furniture, and a more comfortable layout.
events.event_detail: This is a notification about the temporary or permanent closure of the Rincon Valley Regional Library branch. The message indicates that this particular library location is not operating and may not be accepting visitors, returns, or providing services at this time. Patrons should check with the library system for alternative locations or service updates. This is not an active event but rather an administrative notice about branch availability.

events.title: AAPI Teen Art Exhibit 2026
events.description: In celebration of AANHPI Heritage Month, enjoy the AAPI Teen Art Exhibition on display in Saratoga Library's Group Study Room now through May everyday during the library's open hours. This exhibit showcases the artistic talents of local teens.
events.event_detail: The AAPI Teen Art Exhibit 2026 is an art exhibition celebrating AANHPI Heritage Month at Saratoga Library's Group Study Room. The exhibit runs through May during regular library hours and showcases over 30 pieces of artwork including drawings, acrylic paintings, and oil paintings created by student artists from the AAPI community. All student artists, from emerging to established, were invited to submit their work for consideration. The exhibit celebrates the diversity and richness of AAPI cultures, highlighting the unique perspectives and experiences of the community. Suitable for teens and adults. Free admission.

events.title: Kumihimo Craft
events.description: Celebrate Asian American and Pacific Islander month at the Rodeo Library! Kumihimo is a traditional Japanese braiding craft, used to make beautiful, patterned cords. Drop in to the Rodeo Library, pick your choice of yarn color, and make a Kumihimo bracelet to take home.
events.event_detail: Kumihimo Craft is a free craft event at the Rodeo Library celebrating Asian American and Pacific Islander month. Kumihimo is a traditional Japanese braiding craft used to create beautiful, patterned cords. The event runs all day from May 1 to May 31, 2026 (entire month). Participants can drop in at the Rodeo Library location, choose their preferred yarn color, and make a bracelet. All materials and instructions are provided, and attendees can enjoy the craft at the library or take supplies home. The library is located at 220 Pacific Avenue, Rodeo, CA 94572. Accommodations are available with advance notice.

events.title: Paddle the Gate Kayak Tour with Sea Trek
events.description: Kayak tour to paddle the Gate with Sea Trek.
events.event_detail: Paddle the Gate Kayak Tour with Sea Trek is a guided kayaking adventure offering an up-close view of the Golden Gate Bridge. The tour launches from Horseshoe Cove at Fort Baker and follows the scenic Marin Headlands shoreline, providing dramatic coastal views of San Francisco Bay. Participants receive full orientation and instruction from experienced guides. The three-hour tour is suitable for active beginners ages 16 and up, though participants should be comfortable with moderate physical activity and changing water conditions. Date: Sunday, May 31, 2026 at 8:30am. Price: $175 per person (non-members). Reservations are required.

events.title: Wild Garden
events.description: Wild Garden is an exploration of collaboration, care, and connection.
events.location: Rotating Art in the Depot Plaza
events.event_detail: Wild Garden is a collaborative crochet art exhibition created by four women artists from Mill Valley: J'Amy Tarr, Jackie LaLanne, Sarah McNeil, and Naomi Tamura. The artwork, a crochet landscape print on dibond, is installed on the exterior wall of the Depot building at the corner of Miller Avenue and Throckmorton Avenue in Mill Valley. The exhibition runs March through May 2026 as part of the Rotating Art in the Depot Plaza program. A special First Tuesday ArtWalk event takes place on March 3 from 5:30-7:30 pm. The piece explores themes of collaboration, care, and connection, having grown organically through weekly gatherings where the artists engaged in conversation, experimentation, and mutual support. Free admission. Outdoor venue, visible at all hours.

events.title: Sunday Cafe with Muir Woods Park Community Association
events.description: Sunday cafe hosted by Muir Woods Park Community Association.
events.event_detail: Sunday Cafe with Muir Woods Park Community Association is a weekly Sunday brunch event held at the community association café from 3:00pm - 6:00pm. The event features a rotating lineup of local hosts each week, offering attendees great food in a welcoming atmosphere. This is a relaxing way to spend a Sunday afternoon, with visitors invited to stop by before or after exploring the surrounding area. The café provides a casual, community-oriented setting for brunch. Date: Sunday, May 31, 2026, 3:00pm - 6:00pm. Location: 40 Ridge Avenue, Mill Valley, CA 94941.

events.title: Teen Study Hall
events.description: Extra tables and school supplies will be available upstairs for students who are studying for finals. Good luck! Important: Teen Study Hall space is reserved for teens only during afterschool hours and all day on Saturday.
events.event_detail: Teen Study Hall is a study session for teens held at the San Ramon branch of Contra Costa County Library. The event runs from May 26 to June 3, 2026, during all day hours, specifically designed for students studying for finals. Extra tables and school supplies are available upstairs for attendees. The space is reserved for teens only during afterschool hours and all day on Saturdays. Located at 100 Montgomery Street, San Ramon, CA 94583. This is an ideal event for middle and high school students looking for a quiet, focused environment to prepare for exams.

events.title: Herstory Exhibit: The Legal History of Chinese American Women
events.description: Invisible No More: Chinese American Women Shaping American Law. From the landmark 1874 Supreme Court case involving Chinese women to today's generation of judges and elected officials, this exhibit celebrates Chinese American women's legal history.
events.event_detail: Herstory Exhibit: The Legal History of Chinese American Women is a special exhibit celebrating Chinese American women who shaped U.S. law against significant odds. From the landmark 1874 Supreme Court case involving Chinese women to today's generation of judges and elected officials, this exhibit highlights everyday individuals who stood up for their rights and redefined the American story. Visitors will discover how Chinese American women influenced U.S. law, why their stories were nearly erased, the growing presence of women in the judiciary and public life, and the power of visibility in advancing justice. The exhibit runs May 2 - May 31, 2026, and is available for viewing during regular library hours at the Dublin Library. Curated by Dr. Chang C. Chen, a California attorney whose Herstory series is collected by the Library of Congress and exhibited in over 80 institutions. This is a self-guided viewing experience suitable for everyone. Library staff may be present for photos; notify them if you prefer not to be recorded.

events.title: Prize Puzzler for Teens
events.description: Try a new puzzle challenge each Tuesday in the Teen/Young Adult book area. Solve the puzzle to uncover a hidden four-digit code, then visit the Prize Puzzler box near the 3D printer by the Service Desk.
events.event_detail: Prize Puzzler for Teens is a puzzle challenge event held at the Clayton branch of Contra Costa County Library. Each Tuesday during May 2026 (May 1-31), teens can try a new puzzle challenge in the Teen/Young Adult book area. Participants solve puzzles to uncover a hidden four-digit code, then visit the Prize Puzzler box near the 3D printer by the Service Desk to enter their code and unlock two fun prizes. This program is designed for students in Grades 9-12. The event runs all day and is free to attend. Accommodations are available with advance notice.

events.title: Sunday Farmers Market at Marin Civic Center
events.description: Sunday farmers market at Marin Civic Center.
events.event_detail: The Sunday Farmers Market at Marin Civic Center is one of the largest local gatherings in California, ranking as the third largest farmers market in the state. First opened in 1987, this weekly market has grown into a beloved community institution while maintaining its Marin County roots. The event takes place every Sunday from 8:00am to 1:00pm at 3501 Civic Center Drive, San Rafael, CA 94903, rain or shine. The market features nearly 200 local farmers, specialty food purveyors, and artisans offering locally grown and organic produce, local seafood, grass fed meats, pastured eggs, milk and cheese, nuts and nut butters, honey, rice and grains, breads and baked goods, plants and fresh-cut flowers, coffee, pre-packed and hot foods, artisanal crafts and jewelry, soap and personal care items, and pet food. The New York Times listed this market as one of the top places to visit in Marin. Free parking is available.

events.title: June LIVESTREAM Asset Protection & Wealth Creation Summit
events.description: Virtual livestream event about asset protection and wealth creation
events.event_detail: The June LIVESTREAM Asset Protection & Wealth Creation Summit is a free online educational event organized by Protect Wealth Academy. It takes place on Monday, June 1 through Tuesday, June 2, from 9 AM to 4 PM MDT each day (approximately 7 hours per day). This is a virtual livestream event, meaning attendees can participate from anywhere with an internet connection. The summit covers topics related to asset protection strategies and wealth creation techniques, featuring expert speakers and educational content designed to help individuals protect their assets and build wealth. Attendees can expect to learn practical strategies, hear from industry experts, and gain insights into financial protection and wealth building. The event is held entirely online via livestream, allowing participants to attend from the comfort of their own homes.

events.title: Japanese Tea Garden Free Admission Hour
events.description: Free admission from 9-10am on Monday, Wednesday and Friday
events.location: Japanese Tea Garden, Golden Gate Park
events.event_detail: The Japanese Tea Garden in Golden Gate Park offers free admission from 9-10am every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. This historic garden, originally created for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, features classic Japanese elements including an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April. The free hour is available to everyone, not just San Francisco residents. Regular admission for non-residents is $12-16 depending on the season. Visitors can expect a tranquil, meditative experience walking through beautifully landscaped grounds.

events.title: Splash Park
events.description: Splash park open at El Cerrito Swim Center
events.event_detail: Splash Park is a family-friendly water play area at the El Cerrito Swim Center featuring various spray features where children can cool off and have fun playing in the water. The event runs on select dates throughout May and June 2026 (Mondays, Thursdays, Saturdays, and Sundays). Age restrictions apply: Monday-Friday is for ages 7 and under; Saturday and Sunday is open to all ages. Hours vary by day: Saturdays 9am-12:30pm and 4:30pm-7pm, Sundays 9am-12:30pm, and Monday-Friday 9am-7pm. Drop-in fee is $5 per person for ages 2 and older, free for children 1 year and under. A 15-punch pass is also available ($63 Resident / $79 Non-Resident). This is a non-lifeguarded area with no pool access. Note that Splash Park and 7&U Swim are separate programs - participants must choose one and cannot move between them.

events.title: Veterans' In Person Services
events.description: Our Veterans Service Representatives (VSR's) are thoroughly trained and accredited by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs to represent you. Contra Costa County VSR's are not employees of the federal government, they are county employees.

Veterans Service Representatives (VSR's) who are trained and accredited by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs will assist veterans with securing maximum benefits. They can help with compensation for service-related disabilities, pension for wartime Veterans, education benefits, vocational rehabilitation, medical treatment at VA Medical Centers, home loan benefits, government life insurance, burial benefits, military survivor benefits, and the California College Tuition Fee Waiver Program. Representatives work closely with service officers from Veterans organizations. Appointments are required. Each day of the week features a special focus such as arts & crafts, STEM/numbers/reading, or creative play/dance/music. All children must be accompanied and supervised by a parent or caregiver at all times. Registration is encouraged but free. Daily fee is $6 per child. events.description: Contra Costa County Health Services in partnership with Contra Costa County Library System are here to support library staff and patrons alike. Currently the Library Wellness Team consists of a Community Support Worker and Mental Health Clinician.
events.event_detail: The Library Wellness Team is a partnership between Contra Costa County Health Services and the Contra Costa County Library System. The team includes a Community Support Worker and Mental Health Clinician who assist library patrons with various needs that library staff may not be able to address. They provide education about Contra Costa County's mental health and community support services, offering a supportive ear and connections to resources. The event occurs on Monday, June 1, 2026, from 10:00am to 4:00pm at the Concord Library (2900 Salvio Street, Concord, CA 94519). This event takes place in the Main Children's Room at Oakland Public Library from 10:00 AM to 11:30 AM. Attendees can learn about FRN's services and chat with them in person. The organization helps families navigate new diagnoses, provides emotional support, assists with transition to adulthood for young adults with disabilities, and helps families navigate complex systems like IEPs and therapies. They offer guidance on available options for continued education, independence, and job readiness. FRN serves families who live or work in the East Bay.
