events.title: Tai Chi
events.description: Chen-style Taijiquan (Tai Chi) is widely acknowledged as the ancestor of all other styles of Taijiquan. This class will introduce the Chen-style Taijiquan form, Silk-reeling Exercises and Wuji Qigong.
events.event_detail: Chen-style Taijiquan (Tai Chi) class offered by San Mateo County Libraries at the Foster City branch. This event introduces Chen-style Taijiquan form, Silk-reeling Exercises, and Wuji Qigong (standing meditation). The Chen-style form is soft and graceful with strong rooted stands that help students develop strength, balance, coordination, and an understanding of basic Taiji principles. Silk-reeling Exercises are spiral movements that promote muscle relaxation and flexibility by reducing physical tension. Wuji Qigong helps cultivate internal energy (qi) through proper body alignment, improving energy flow and enhancing immune systems while reducing physical and mental stress. Suitable for adults 19+ and adults 55+. Space is limited and admission is first-come, first-served. No registration required.

events.description: What is T'ai-chi? T'ai-chi Ch'uan is an ancient Chinese art which combines meditation in movement and healthful exercise. The training includes the practice of a 37 posture form which teaches relaxation, balance and strength.
events.event_detail: Tai Chi class at Walnut Creek Library on Monday, June 1, 2026 from 10:15am to 11:15am in the Oak View Room upstairs. The class focuses on relaxation, balance and strength, plus a partner practice building sensitivity and timing. No prior training is needed; everyone with interest is welcome. Medical research demonstrates benefits including reduced incidence of falls, increased relaxation, calmness, flexibility and balance. events.description: Qigong means 'practice of vital energy'. In this class, we will practice a series of gentle spiral movements that help to open all the major joints.
events.event_detail: Qigong is a free wellness class offered by San Mateo County Libraries at the San Carlos Adult Community Center (601 Chestnut Street). The class runs from 10:30 AM to 11:30 AM. Qigong means "practice of vital energy" and involves gentle spiral movements designed to open all major joints in the body and increase internal energy flow. The practice promotes better flexibility and mobility while reducing tension and strain. This class is suitable for adults (19+) and is also 55+ friendly. Participants should wear comfortable, loose-fitting clothing that allows for easy movement. No prior experience with Qigong is required to attend.

events.title: Free Basic English Class / Curso gratuito de ingles básico
events.description: Adults (18+) are invited to join us to practice and improve basic English speaking and listening skills. This six-week class is for learners with little to no English. No registration required but space is limited.
events.event_detail: Free Basic English Class at Gilroy Library. Adults (18+) are invited to practice and improve basic English speaking and listening skills in this six-week class designed for learners with little to no English. Classes run from 10:30 AM to 11:30 AM. No registration required, but space is limited. Available in both English and Spanish. This is an inclusive, welcoming environment for language learners to build confidence and foundational English skills.

events.title: Storytime: For Toddlers
events.description: Toddler storytime at Portola
events.event_detail: Storytime: For Toddlers is a library program for children 16 months through age 2 and their caregivers. The event features books, songs, movement activities and more. It takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026, from 10:30 to 11:00 AM at the Portola Meeting Room, located at the Portola Branch of the San Francisco Public Library (380 Bacon Street, San Francisco, CA 94134). This is a drop-in program with no registration required. The session is conducted in English and is wheelchair accessible. Accommodations such as ASL are available upon request by calling (415) 557-4557. The program is sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library.

items.name: Small cushion or portable seat pad

events.title: California Mahjong Game Time
events.description: Join us for California Mahjong Game Time! Whether you're a seasoned player or brand new to the game, all are welcome to enjoy a fun and friendly session of California-style mahjong.
events.event_detail: California Mahjong Game Time is a community game session hosted by San Mateo County Libraries at the Millbrae branch. The event runs from 11:00 AM to 1:00 PM and welcomes players of all skill levels, from beginners to experienced players. Attendees can expect a fun and friendly atmosphere to learn, play, and connect with others over tiles using California-style rules. This event is suitable for adults (19+) and is also friendly for those aged 55 and older. Participants can drop in to enjoy the game, meet fellow mahjong enthusiasts, and improve their skills in a relaxed setting.

events.title: Dan Serbin, June's Featured Artist at Sky Ranch Gallery
events.description: June's Featured Artist at Sky Ranch Gallery, Tomales
events.event_detail: Featured Artist exhibition at Sky Ranch Gallery showcasing Dan Serbin's oil paintings throughout June 2026. Dan Serbin was introduced to oil painting by an uncle at age 13 and draws inspiration from California's diverse scenic environments. The exhibition runs the entire month of June with gallery hours Thursday through Monday from 11:00 am to 2:00 pm. Admission is free. Attendees can view the artist's paintings featuring California landscapes and scenic locations. The venue is located at 27000 CA-1, Tomales, CA 94971.

events.title: Clases Gratuitas de Ingles | 免費英文課程 | Free English Classes
events.description: Aprende y practica inglés en una clase presencial y acogedora en la Biblioteca de Brisbane.
events.event_detail: Free English Classes at Brisbane Library - Learn and practice English in a welcoming, in-person class with a certified instructor. This workshop develops speaking, listening, reading, and writing skills for everyday life. All levels are welcome! The class runs from 11:00 AM to 12:30 PM. Suitable for adults (19+).

events.title: Garden Playdate
events.description: Join us in the Melrose Branch Garden and Patio for open play time!
events.event_detail: Garden Playdate is a family-friendly outdoor event at Oakland Public Library's Melrose Branch. Children from birth to age 5, toddlers, preschoolers, and their families are invited to join in the Melrose Branch Garden and Patio for open play time. The event runs from 11:00 AM to 12:00 PM and is part of the OPL Summer program with a gardening theme. Programming is provided in both English and Spanish (Acompañanos a jugar en el Patio de Melrose). Attendees can expect casual outdoor play in a garden setting, suitable for young children and families looking for free community activities.

events.title: Music and Movement
events.description: Music and Movement is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities through songs, rhymes, finger plays, and movement activities.
events.event_detail: Music and Movement is a free family program held at the Mt. Pleasant library branch, running from 11:00 AM to 12:00 PM. The event is designed for young children ages 0-5 and their parents/caregivers, inviting the entire family to participate in early literacy activities through songs, rhymes, finger plays, and movement activities. This interactive program promotes the joys of learning for all ages and aligns with Early Education Quality Standards. Attendees can expect a fun, engaging experience where children develop early literacy skills through active play and music. The event welcomes children of all ages to enjoy this supportive, family-friendly environment at the library.

events.title: Storytime: For Babies
events.description: Baby storytime at Richmond
events.event_detail: Storytime: For Babies is a library program designed for infants and their caregivers. The event features songs, rhymes, and books appropriate for babies. It takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026, from 11:00 AM to 12:00 PM at the Richmond Meeting Room in the Richmond Branch of the San Francisco Public Library, located at 351 9th Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94118. Space is limited, and tickets are available on a first-come, first-served basis at the Children's desk starting at 10:30 AM. Playtime follows the storytime session. The program is sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library and is conducted in English. The library is wheelchair accessible, and accommodations such as ASL can be arranged by contacting the library in advance.

events.title: Storytime: For Toddlers
events.description: Toddler storytime at Noe Valley
events.event_detail: Storytime for Toddlers is a 30-minute early literacy program featuring books, songs, movement and more at the San Francisco Public Library. This event takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026, from 11:15 to 11:45 AM at the Noe Valley Meeting Room in the Noe Valley/Sally Brunn branch, located at 451 Jersey Street, San Francisco, CA 94114. Designed for toddlers aged 16 months through age 2 and their caregivers, the program provides an interactive experience to develop early reading skills. Space is limited and tickets are available on a first-come, first-served basis at the door starting at 11:00 AM.

items.name: Small stuffed animal or comfort toy

events.title: Storytime: For Toddlers
events.description: Toddler storytime at Ingleside
events.event_detail: Storytime for Toddlers is a free library program featuring books, songs, movement and more, designed for toddlers 16 months through age 2 and their caregivers. The event takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026 from 11:30 AM to 12:30 PM at the Ingleside Meeting Room (Ingleside Branch, 1298 Ocean Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94112). This is a drop-in program with no registration required. The session is sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library. All SFPL locations are wheelchair accessible, and accommodations like ASL can be arranged by contacting the library in advance. Parents and caregivers can expect interactive reading, singing, and movement activities suitable for young toddlers.

items.name: Small stuffed animal or comfort toy

events.title: Early Learning: Play with Purpose Playgroup
events.description: Early learning playgroup for young children
events.event_detail: Early Learning: Play with Purpose Playgroup is a 9-week facilitated playgroup for families with young children ages 0-3 with mild to moderate concerns about child development. The program focuses on research-based, playful ways to support emerging literacy, language skills, and learning. This session takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026 from 11:30 AM to 12:30 PM at the Glen Park Meeting Room, located at Glen Park Branch (2825 Diamond Street, San Francisco, CA 94131). Participants receive free books and toys every week along with professional support and guidance on using the free Sparkler app (available in English, Spanish, and Chinese). The program includes developmental screening, a library of 2,000 playful activities, and connections to local support services through the San Francisco Department of Early Childhood. Space is limited and reservations are required.

events.title: Let's Chat - Mondays
events.description: Improve your conversation skills by chatting with other English learners in a friendly, welcoming setting. Receive a news article on the Thursday before the meeting. Read and discuss the article during the meeting.
events.event_detail: Let's Chat - Mondays is a virtual English conversation practice session hosted by Alameda County Library. The event takes place every Monday from 11:30 AM to 12:30 PM via Zoom. Participants improve their conversation skills by chatting with other English learners in a friendly, welcoming setting. Attendees receive a news article on the Thursday before the meeting, which they read and discuss during the session. Everyone gets a chance to speak. The event is best suited for advanced beginner and intermediate English speakers. Registration is required to receive the Zoom link and article/topic of the day. Articles are usually sent out on Thursday evenings and again on the morning of the meeting.

events.title: Baby Bounce
events.description: Bring your babies to the library for songs, socializing, and playtime! This event is suited for little ones who are 0 to 18 months.
events.event_detail: Baby Bounce is a storytime event for babies aged 0 to 18 months, held at the Lakeview Branch of the Oakland Public Library. The event runs from 11:45 AM to 1:00 PM, with storytime beginning at 11:45 AM followed by open playtime until 1 PM. Caregivers can bring their infants to enjoy songs, socializing, and playtime in a library setting. Note that this library branch does not have a bathroom on site, so visitors should use facilities outside the library adjacent to the nearby park. This is a free, drop-in event suitable for babies and their caregivers.

events.title: Opening: The Biggest Small Works Show 2026
events.description: Call for Entry: 2D and Wall Mounted 3D. -Small work exhibit. Presented by Gallery Sausalito, Sausalito
events.event_detail: Opening reception for The Biggest Small Works Show 2026 at Gallery Sausalito. This is the third annual exhibition featuring small artwork in all mediums, with this year's theme being SWEET. The exhibition runs from June 1-25, 2026, with the opening reception on the first Saturday in June. Attendees can view artwork from approximately 74 artists displayed in the gallery, meet the artists, and enjoy the reception. Gallery hours are Thursday through Monday, 12:00 pm - 6:00 pm. The venue is located at 30 Princess Street in Sausalito. Artists are encouraged to attend and bring friends to this community art event.

events.title: Baby Bounce Storytime With Stay and Play!
events.description: Bring your bouncing baby to our weekly playtime, full of nursery rhymes and songs you can do together to stimulate your baby's development.
events.event_detail: Baby Bounce Storytime With Stay and Play! is a weekly event held at the Atherton library branch of San Mateo County Libraries. The event takes place on Thursdays from 12:00 PM to 12:45 PM. Designed for babies from newborns up to 18 months old, the program features nursery rhymes and songs that parents and caregivers can do together with their little ones to support early development. After the storytime portion, attendees can participate in Stay and Play, an open-ended exploration session where children and caregivers can interact and learn together in a social setting. All are welcome, though the program is ideally suited for families with infants and toddlers.

events.title: Monday English Conversations at Newark Library
events.description: Please join us for English Conversations at Newark Library. This group is open to learners of any English skill level. As a participant, you will receive free learning material to make your English conversation skill development engaging.
events.event_detail: Monday English Conversations at Newark Library is a free English language practice group open to learners of any skill level. The event runs every Monday from 12:00 PM to 1:30 PM at the Newark Branch of Alameda County Library. Participants receive free learning materials to support their English conversation skill development. This is a casual, welcoming environment where attendees can practice speaking, listening, and conversation skills with others. The group is suitable for adults looking to improve their English proficiency in a supportive, low-pressure setting. Library staff may be present and could take photos or recordings during the event.

events.title: Computer Help
events.description: Computer docents are volunteers who answer simple technical questions and offer basic instruction on library computers. They help you get started, so you can take those skills and continue to explore and learn on your own!
events.event_detail: Computer Help event at Pleasant Hill Library on Monday, June 1, 2026, from 12:00pm to 2:00pm. Volunteer Computer Docents provide free basic technical assistance including teaching email usage, creating and saving documents, printing documents or web pages, performing basic web searches, and assistance with eBooks on the Libby app. First come, first served with no appointment necessary. Help limited to 30 minutes if others are waiting. Located at 2 Monticello Avenue, Pleasant Hill, CA 94523. For questions, call (925) 349-0883.

events.title: Free summer lunch
events.description: Newark Unified School District is providing free summer lunch to anyone age 1-18. Lunch will be distributed in the library lobby while supplies last. Children and teens must be present to receive lunch.
events.event_detail: Free summer lunch program provided by Newark Unified School District at Alameda County Library. This free meal service is available to anyone age 1-18 during the summer months. Lunch is distributed in the library lobby from 12:30 PM to 1:30 PM while supplies last. Children and teens must be present to receive their own meal. The program aims to provide nutritious meals to youth during summer break when school lunch programs are unavailable. No registration or proof of income is required to participate.

events.title: Monday Book Club
events.description: You're invited to attend the Pleasant Hill Library's Monday book club. This book club will meet on June 1 at 1:00 pm; where we will be discussing Martyr! by Kaveh Akbar. Copies of the book will be available for pickup at the Pleasant Hill Library.
events.event_detail: Monday Book Club is a book discussion group held at the Pleasant Hill Library in Contra Costa County. The club meets on Monday, June 1, 2026, from 1:00pm to 2:30pm in the Maker Space. Attendees will discuss "Martyr!" by Kaveh Akbar. Copies of the book are available for pickup at the Pleasant Hill Library starting May 4, 2026. Participants can expect a facilitated discussion about the book's themes, characters, and literary elements. The event is designed for adults and conducted in English. The library is located at 2 Monticello Avenue, Pleasant Hill, CA 94523. Accommodation requests should be made at least three days in advance.

events.title: Friends of the Millbrae Library Book Club
events.description: Join us at the Millbrae Library on the first Monday of every month at 1:00 PM to discuss the month's chosen book.
events.event_detail: Friends of the Millbrae Library Book Club is a monthly book discussion group that meets on the first Monday of every month from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM at the Millbrae Library. This is an ongoing, casual discussion of works of all forms and genres, welcoming both casual and avid readers. Attendees discuss the month's chosen book. The event is suitable for adults (19+) and is conducted in English. No registration is required to attend.

events.title: East Bay Vivarium
events.description: Experts from the East Bay Vivarium will share some of their scaly friends and teach us about the fascinating world of reptiles, amphibians, and bugs.
events.event_detail: Experts from the East Bay Vivarium visit the Eastmont Branch of Oakland Public Library to share reptiles, amphibians, and bugs with attendees. This educational program teaches about the fascinating world of cold-blooded creatures and insects. The event runs from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM and is part of the OPL Summer program. Suitable for kids of all ages, grade schoolers, tweens, toddlers, preschoolers, and families. Attendees can expect to meet some scaly friends up close, learn interesting facts about reptiles, and enjoy an engaging live animal presentation.

events.title: Book Group
events.description: Join us for a lively discussion of select fiction and non-fiction books on the first Monday of the month.
events.event_detail: Book Group is a monthly book discussion event held at the Woodside library branch of San Mateo County Libraries. The group meets on the first Monday of each month from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM to discuss select fiction and non-fiction books. If the first Monday falls on a holiday, the meeting moves to the second Monday. This event is suitable for adults (19+) and conducted in English. Attendees can expect a lively discussion with other book lovers, sharing insights and perspectives on the selected reading material.

events.title: *Virtual* Adult Literacy & ESL Volunteer Info session
events.description: Learn about volunteering as an Adult Literacy & ESL tutor at the San Jose Public Library! You can support adults in achieving their personal and professional goals by helping them improve their reading, writing, and English conversation skills.
events.event_detail: Virtual information session for adults interested in volunteering as tutors for the San Jose Public Library's Adult Literacy & ESL programs. The session provides an overview of the programs, explains the tutoring experience, and guides participants through the initial steps to become a volunteer tutor. Attendees will learn how to support adults in improving their reading, writing, and English language skills to help them achieve personal and professional goals. This orientation is the first required step for becoming a tutor. The event is free, conducted in English, and suitable for adults 18 and older. Participants should be prepared to take notes on program requirements and next steps.

events.title: YMCA Community Resource Center at the Library
events.description: YMCA Community Resource Center caseworkers will be at the library to help with a variety of safety net services.
events.event_detail: YMCA Community Resource Center at the Library is a free community resource event where YMCA caseworkers provide safety net services including food assistance, emergency housing assistance, emergency utility assistance, shelter referrals, and help with other basic needs. The event takes place at the Brisbane library branch from 1:00 PM to 4:00 PM. Appointments are recommended but walk-ins may be accepted. Available in English and Spanish. Suitable for adults (19+) and seniors. Contact (650) 271-3850 or crc@ymcasf.org to schedule an appointment.

events.title: Meditation Mondays
events.description: The Library Wellness Team offers a guided meditation to relax and re-center the mind, body, and spirit. Meditation will be guided in English at 1pm and will be guided in Spanish at 2pm. Offered every first and third Monday of the month.
events.event_detail: The Library Wellness Team offers a guided meditation session to relax and re-center the mind, body, and spirit. The event takes place on the first and third Monday of each month at the Concord Library (2900 Salvio Street, Concord, CA 94519). Sessions are held in English at 1:00 PM and in Spanish at 2:00 PM. Attendees can expect a guided meditation experience focused on relaxation and mindfulness. The event is free and open to adults and teens (13-18 years). No registration is required.

events.title: Tech Mentor: One on One Computer Help
events.description: Confused by your computer? Get personalized tech assistance. Help is available for basic tasks such as printing, using email, connecting to WiFi, creating documents, and accessing library resources such as e-books.
events.event_detail: Tech Mentor: One on One Computer Help is a free personalized technology assistance program at the Joyce Ellington Library branch in San Jose. The event runs from 1:00 PM to 5:00 PM and offers drop-in help with basic computer tasks including printing, email usage, WiFi connectivity, document creation, and accessing library digital resources like e-books. Staff and mentors also provide basic instruction for devices such as laptops, smartphones, and e-readers. No registration or appointment is required – attendees can simply arrive during the hours and ask for assistance. The program is designed for adults (18+) and seniors (65+) looking to improve their digital literacy skills in a relaxed, supportive library environment. All help is provided free of charge.

events.title: Coloring for Adults
events.description: Coloring sheets and pencils are provided every Monday afternoon from 1:00-6:30 PM in the lobby of Bascom Library. Relax and explore your creativity with this great activity! All ages welcome.
events.event_detail: Coloring for Adults is a relaxing weekly event held every Monday from 1:00 PM to 6:30 PM in the lobby of Bascom Library in San Jose. The library provides coloring sheets and pencils for participants to use. This free activity allows adults to unwind, explore their creativity, and enjoy a calming artistic experience in a peaceful library setting. No registration is required, and all ages are welcome to participate. Simply drop in during the specified hours to color, de-stress, and connect with others in a welcoming environment.

events.title: Tech Mentor: One on One Computer Help
events.description: Confused by your computer? Get personalized tech assistance from a Librarian or adult volunteer at the Evergreen Branch Library! Help is available for basic tasks such as connecting to WiFi, using email, creating documents, and accessing library resources.
events.event_detail: Tech Mentor: One on One Computer Help is a free, drop-in computer help session at the Evergreen Branch Library of San José Public Library. Participants receive personalized tech assistance from librarians or adult volunteers for basic tasks including connecting to WiFi, using email, creating documents, accessing library resources like e-books and virtual programs, and getting basic instructions for devices such as laptops, smartphones, and e-readers. The schedule varies: Monday and Tuesday 1:00-3:00pm, Wednesday and Thursday 12:00-1:00pm. No registration or appointment required - just drop by and ask for assistance. Not suitable for passport applications, DMV renewals, or government forms. Designed for adults and seniors who want one-on-one help with technology basics.

events.title: Yoga
events.description: Interested in learning how to do yoga or already have a practice, and want to join other adults in your community for free classes?
events.event_detail: Free yoga classes for adults at San Mateo County Libraries, Half Moon Bay branch. Classes run from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM and are led by experienced instructor Ted Harvey. The session focuses on a combination of movement, meditation, and breathing exercises designed for stress relief, relaxation, and mind-body connection. All skill levels are welcome. Participants are asked to bring their own towel or mat. This health and wellness event is suitable for adults 19+ and is also 55+ friendly.

events.title: Reptile Show with East Bay Vivarium
events.description: Reptile show with East Bay Vivarium
events.event_detail: The Reptile Show with East Bay Vivarium is a free family event taking place at the Eastmont Branch of the Oakland Public Library on Monday, June 1, 2026 from 1:00 pm to 2:00 pm. Experts from the East Bay Vivarium will bring their reptiles, amphibians, and bugs to share with attendees. Children and families can meet scaly friends up close and learn about the fascinating world of reptiles through this interactive educational presentation. The event is suitable for toddlers, preschoolers, and grade schoolers. No registration is required, and admission is free.

events.title: 1-on-1 Tech Help / Ayuda con la Tecnología
events.description: Do you need help using a computer? Want to set up an email account? Our Tech Mentor is a bilingual (English / Spanish) volunteer who will do their best to assist you with your technology needs. No registration or appointment required.
events.event_detail: 1-on-1 Tech Help event at Gilroy Library providing free technology assistance for community members. A bilingual (English/Spanish) volunteer Tech Mentor helps attendees with various technology needs including setting up email accounts, connecting to Wi-Fi, using laptops and Chromebooks, and Microsoft Office applications. No registration or appointment required. Drop in on Mondays between 1pm-5pm. Suitable for teens, adults, and older adults. This is an ongoing weekly program at the Gilroy Library branch in Santa Clara County.

events.title: Work Success
events.description: Are you looking for a job or a change of career? Come visit NOVAworks Job Resource Center during this drop-in resource hour.
events.event_detail: Work Success is a free job search resource event hosted by San Mateo County Libraries at the North Fair Oaks branch. NOVAworks Job Resource Center representatives provide drop-in assistance for job seekers from 1:15 PM to 3:15 PM. No appointment is necessary. Attendees can learn about job search resources, workshop opportunities, and career advisors, and get help with their job or career change. The event is suitable for adults (19+) and offers bilingual assistance in English and Spanish.

events.title: Activity: Shut Up and Write
events.description: Writing session activity for adults
events.event_detail: Shut Up and Write is a quiet writing session for adults held at the San Francisco Public Library's Potrero Branch. The event takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026 from 1:15 to 3:15 PM in the Potrero Meeting Room. Participants begin with a brief check-in and introductions where they share their name, current writing project, and goals for the session. The majority of the time (1:30-3:15 PM) is dedicated silent writing time in a distraction-free environment. At 3:15, the formal session ends and attendees may stay to chat and socialize, or continue writing on the main library floor. No critiques or read-alouds occur during the session unless individuals choose to share their work voluntarily. The program is facilitated by volunteers from Shut Up & Write!, a community writing group, and is sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library. This is a drop-in program with no registration required. Attendees should bring whatever writing tools they prefer to use during this focused creative time.

events.title: Rafiki Community Market
events.description: Community market event
events.event_detail: The Rafiki Community Market is a free food distribution event organized by Rafiki Coalition and SF-Marin Food Bank, providing healthy, fresh groceries to eligible Bayview residents in need. The event takes place on Mondays from 1:30 pm to 3:30 pm at 600 Cesar Chavez Street, San Francisco, CA 94124. To participate, attendees must live in the 94124 zip code and have low-to-moderate income (at or below twice the federal poverty level). No proof of income is required—eligibility is based on self-attestation. Each household may only attend one weekly distribution. This is a free community resource designed to increase food access for underserved residents in the Bayview neighborhood.

events.title: Activity: Beginners Tai Chi with Patrick Lau
events.description: Beginners Tai Chi class with instructor Patrick Lau
events.event_detail: Beginners Tai Chi with Patrick Lau is a weekly drop-in class offering Tai Chi instruction for beginners. The class takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026 from 1:30 to 2:15 PM at the Presidio Meeting Room in the Presidio branch of the San Francisco Public Library, located at 3150 Sacramento Street, San Francisco, CA 94115. Participants can expect gentle, slow-paced movements suitable for those new to Tai Chi. The class is part of the Library's Health & Wellness programming and is sponsored by the Friends of the San Francisco Public Library. No registration is required as this is a drop-in program. The session lasts approximately 45 minutes and provides an opportunity to learn basic Tai Chi fundamentals in a supportive group setting.

events.title: Presentation: Fraud Fighters — Outsmarting Financial Abuse for Older Adults
events.description: Presentation on financial abuse awareness for seniors
events.event_detail: Presentation workshop designed to help older adults recognize and protect themselves from financial abuse and scams. The event takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026, from 2:00 to 3:00 PM at the Mission Bay Program Room in the San Francisco Public Library Mission Bay branch (960 4th Street, San Francisco, CA 94158). Presented by experts from The Institute on Aging and The Department of Disability and Aging, the workshop covers common scams targeting older adults, identifies red flags to watch for, and provides practical tools and strategies to safeguard personal information and finances. Attendees will learn how scammers operate, ways to protect themselves and their loved ones, and where to report financial abuse. This is a drop-in event with no registration required. The presentation is conducted in English and is wheelchair accessible.

events.title: Community Craft Circle
events.description: Bring your current project and join a welcoming space to craft and connect. Work on your own project alongside others, share conversation, and enjoy the creativity of making together. All crafts and skill levels are welcome.
events.event_detail: Community Craft Circle is a free craft gathering at the Pittsburg library branch in Contra Costa County. The event takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026, from 2:00pm to 4:00pm. Attendees are encouraged to bring their own current craft project and work on it in a welcoming group setting. The event provides an opportunity to craft alongside others, share conversation, and enjoy the creativity of making together. All types of crafts and all skill levels are welcome. No registration is required to attend.

events.title: Day for DIY
events.description: Take time for creativity at this hands-on event designed for teens and adults. Explore guided and do-it-yourself stations and more (subject to availability). All materials and instructions are provided—limited to one project per person.
events.event_detail: Day for DIY is a hands-on creative event for teens and adults held from 2:00 PM to 4:00 PM at the Half Moon Bay library branch. Participants explore guided and do-it-yourself stations where they can create projects by hand. All materials and instructions are provided by the library, though projects are limited to one per person. No prior experience is necessary—attendees simply need to bring their curiosity. This event focuses on art, creativity, and STEAM activities, and is suitable for teens aged 12-18 and adults. The event is 55+ friendly and conducted in English.

events.title: Mending Mondays
events.description: Do you have clothing items that need repair? Want company while you mend? Or have other handicrafts in mind? Bring your projects to the Bolinas Library and join our mending circle. We meet most Mondays from 2-4 pm.
events.event_detail: Mending Mondays is a community craft event held at the Bolinas Library where people can bring their clothing and fabric items that need repair. The gathering takes place most Mondays from 2:00 PM to 4:00 PM. Attendees work on their own mending projects while enjoying company and shared creativity. Those with sewing notions like bobbles and thread are encouraged to bring them. This welcoming circle is suitable for adults and teens aged 12 and older who enjoy crafts, sewing, and handicrafts. No experience is required—participants simply bring their repair projects and join others for an afternoon of productive and social mending.

events.title: Activity: Advanced Tai Chi with Patrick Lau
events.description: Advanced Tai Chi class with instructor Patrick Lau
events.event_detail: Advanced Tai Chi class with instructor Patrick Lau held at the Presidio Meeting Room. This is a weekly drop-in class that takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026 from 2:15 to 3:00 PM. The session follows the beginner's class at 12:15 PM and provides advanced-level Tai Chi instruction for participants. The class is part of the Health & Wellness programming at San Francisco Public Library and is sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library. No registration required. Participants should wear comfortable clothing suitable for gentle exercise and movement. The library is wheelchair accessible and accommodations can be arranged by contacting accessibility@sfpl.org.

events.title: Digital Help Hub |Centro de Ayuda Digital
events.description: One-on-one and small-group help for real-life tech tasks. Learn what you need, at your pace.
events.event_detail: Digital Help Hub is a free library technology assistance program offering one-on-one and small-group help for real-life tech tasks. Attendees can receive personalized tech support at their own pace, with sessions focusing on understanding operating systems and internet browsers. Whether you need help sending email attachments, navigating a new smartphone, or other technology questions, volunteer tech experts are available to assist. The event takes place in the Sunrise Room from 2:30 PM to 4:30 PM. No registration is required. Bilingual support is available in English and Spanish. This event is suitable for adults (19+) and is also senior-friendly.

events.title: Virtual English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club at Calabazas Library
events.description: This program is presented by the Calabazas Branch of the San Jose Public Library. Join our wonderful volunteer instructor to improve your English conversation skills with other adult learners in a welcoming and respectful environment.
events.event_detail: Virtual English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club at Calabazas Library. This free virtual program runs weekly from 2:30 PM - 3:30 PM, presented by the Calabazas Branch of the San Jose Public Library. Join a volunteer instructor and other adult learners in a welcoming environment to improve English conversation skills. Enhance speaking and listening abilities, expand vocabulary, and discuss current events. Registration is required to receive the Zoom meeting link - sign up to get the link and preview upcoming lesson topics before each session. Participants need a computer, tablet, or smartphone with internet access to join via Zoom. Suitable for adults and seniors ages 18+.

events.title: Finals Study Zone
events.description: A place for teen students to study for finals.
events.event_detail: Finals Study Zone is a library event for teen students to study for their finals exams. The event takes place from 3:00 PM to 6:00 PM. It is held at the Albany branch of Alameda County Library. This is a dedicated quiet study space where teens can focus on their coursework and prepare for upcoming exams. Library staff may be present, and the space offers a supportive environment for academic preparation. The event is suitable for teens and conducted in English.

events.title: Reading Buddies
events.description: Reading Buddies provides students in grades K-3 with an opportunity to improve their reading skills by working one-on-one with a reading coach. Reading Buddies creates a positive reading experience for beginning and developing readers.
events.event_detail: Reading Buddies is a free library program that provides students in grades K-3 with one-on-one reading support. The event takes place from 3:00 PM to 4:00 PM at the Joyce Ellington Branch Library in San Jose. A reading coach listens to children read and provides support in reading and comprehension, helping beginning and developing readers build confidence. Students can bring their favorite book or choose from the library's available selection. No pre-registration is required, but sessions are available on a first come, first served basis and may be limited depending on the number of participants. The program is suitable for kids ages 5-10 and conducted in English.

events.title: After School Meals
events.description: San Pablo Library has free, healthy meals for students after school Monday-Friday from 3-5pm. Meals are provided by the WCCUSD Food Services. Must be 18 and under, no registration required.
events.event_detail: Free, healthy meals for students provided by WCCUSD Food Services at San Pablo Library. The event runs Monday through Friday from 3:00pm to 5:00pm, offering free meals to children and teens after school. This is a no-registration-required program open to students 18 and under. The meals are served at the San Pablo Library branch located at 13751 San Pablo Avenue, San Pablo, CA 94806. Families can drop in during the specified hours to pick up a nutritious meal for their children.

events.title: Paws to Read
events.description: Would your child like to earn Summer Reading minutes reading to a friendly dog? Children in grades K through 5 can 'Paws to Read' with dogs certified for sociability. Beginning readers get a calm, patient listener.
events.event_detail: Paws to Read is a free library program where children in grades K through 5 can read aloud to certified, friendly therapy dogs. The event takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026, from 3:00pm to 3:15pm at the Contra Costa County Library Orinda branch, specifically in the Children's Alcove located at 26 Orinda Way, Orinda, CA 94563. This 15-minute session is designed for beginning readers who benefit from a calm, patient listener, as well as for confident readers who want to de-stress by reading to a furry friend. Children can earn Summer Reading minutes by participating. Registration is full, but interested families can join the waitlist. Accommodations are available with advance request.

events.title: LEGO® Club (Ygnacio Valley Library)
events.description: Join us on the 1st and 3rd Mondays for the LEGO® Club at Ygnacio Valley Library! We provide the LEGO's®, you provide the fun. No registration required.
events.event_detail: LEGO Club at Ygnacio Valley Library is a free, drop-in building event for children ages 6-12 and tweens. The club meets on the 1st and 3rd Mondays of each month from 3:00pm to 5:00pm in the library's Meeting Room. The library provides all LEGO bricks, and no registration is required to attend. Children can build freely with provided materials, explore their creativity, and take their creations home. This is a casual, fun library program suitable for families with school-age children looking for an afternoon activity.

events.title: Reading to Children with Aysha
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books.
events.event_detail: Reading to Children with Aysha is a storytime program hosted by San Jose Public Library at the Cambrian branch. This event takes place from 3:00 PM to 4:00 PM and is designed for young children ages 0-5 and kids ages 5-10. The program provides children with one-on-one or small group interaction with a volunteer reader, helping them develop imagination and spark a love for books, reading, and learning. Children can also practice reading to the volunteer. The event occurs in the Children's Area of the library. Note: This event appears to be canceled. Participants should check the library website for the most current schedule and any rescheduled sessions.

events.title: 1-on-1 Tech Help
events.description: BY APPOINTMENT ONLY. Do you need help using the computer? Don't know how to send an email or set up a Zoom meeting? Our tech mentor can help! Learn how to open an email account, connect to Wi-Fi/hotspots, use laptops/Chromebooks, and use Microsoft Office.
events.event_detail: 1-on-1 Tech Help is a free library program offering personalized computer and technology assistance. Sessions run from 3:00 PM to 5:00 PM at the Bascom branch of San José Public Library. By appointment only, this program connects attendees with a tech mentor who can help with essential digital skills including: opening email accounts, connecting to Wi-Fi and hotspots, using laptops or Chromebooks, navigating Microsoft Office, filling out online forms, using social media, and browsing the SJPL website. Participants can receive one-on-one support tailored to their specific needs and skill level. Registration is required and availability is not guaranteed. To book an appointment, call (408) 808-3077 or email eric.debold@sjlibrary.org. Suitable for adults and seniors looking to improve their technology literacy in a supportive environment.

events.title: Elmhurst Branch Lego Club
events.description: Come build with us at Lego club! Every Monday we unleash our imagination building amazing Lego creations.
events.event_detail: Elmhurst Branch Lego Club is a free weekly kids event held every Monday from 3:00 PM to 5:00 PM at the Elmhurst Branch of the Oakland Public Library. Children can unleash their imagination and build amazing Lego creations using the library's provided Lego blocks. The club encourages creativity and allows participants to see their favorite creations displayed at the branch for all visitors to admire. This is a drop-in program suitable for kids, no registration required. All materials are provided by the library.

events.title: Digital Help Hub
events.description: One-on-One and small group help for real life tech tasks. Learn what you need, at your own pace.
events.event_detail: Digital Help Hub is a library technology assistance event offering one-on-one and small group help for real life tech tasks. Attendees can learn what they need at their own pace in a supportive environment. The event takes place at the Half Moon Bay library branch from 3:00 PM to 7:00 PM. This session is suitable for adults (19+) and focuses on technology and life skills. Participants receive personalized assistance with various tech-related needs, learning at their own pace with available library resources and staff guidance. The event is free and open to all adults seeking help with technology tasks.

events.title: Free Snacks for Kids! / Meriendas Gratis Para Niños!
events.description: Stop by the library and pick up a FREE after-school snack! For kids 18 years old and under. Monday - Friday (3pm - 4pm) while supplies last. Every school day until June except for GUSD school breaks. Snacks provided by the Second Harvest Food Bank.
events.event_detail: Free after-school snack program for kids 18 and under at Gilroy Library. Snacks provided by the YMCA are available Monday through Friday from 3pm to 4pm while supplies last. The program runs every school day until June, except during Gilroy Unified School District (GUSD) breaks. This is part of the Meals at the Library program, suitable for babies, toddlers, preschoolers, kids in grades K-8, and teens. Available in both English and Spanish.

events.title: Make It With Magnetic Tiles
events.description: Explore shapes, colors, and design as you build with Superspace magnetic tiles.
events.event_detail: Make It With Magnetic Tiles is a children's STEAM and early learning program held at the Portola Valley library branch. The event takes place from 3:00 PM to 5:00 PM, offering an open-ended creative building activity using Superspace magnetic tiles. Children ages 6-11 can explore shapes, colors, and design concepts while building everything from simple patterns to tall towers. The activity encourages imagination, creativity, and discovery through hands-on play with magnetic building tiles. No registration is required—attendees simply drop in to play, create, and explore the fun of magnetic building at their own pace.

events.title: 1-on-1 Tech Help
events.description: BY APPOINTMENT ONLY. Got a tech question? Our Tech Mentor can help!
events.event_detail: 1-on-1 Tech Help is a canceled library event offering personalized technology assistance at the Bascom branch. Sessions run from 3:00 PM to 5:00 PM by appointment only. A Tech Mentor provides one-on-one support in a friendly environment for adults and seniors seeking help with everyday tech questions. The mentor can assist with basic smartphone, tablet, and computer help, connecting to Wi-Fi, setting up and using email, downloading apps, making video calls (Zoom, FaceTime, Google Meets), browsing the internet, and navigating the SJPL website and digital resources. Note that this service does not include job search or resume assistance. To schedule an appointment, call (408) 808-3077 or email Yesenia Ortega at yesenia.ortega@sjlibrary.org.

events.title: Plot, Pot, and Paint
events.description: Drop in after school and paint a flowerpot inspired by your favorite book, character, or genre. Learn how to plant a succulent in your pot and how to properly care for it in this workshop led by staff from the Ruth Bancroft Garden.
events.event_detail: Plot, Pot, and Paint is a craft workshop for tweens and teens (6th to 12th grade) held on Monday, June 1, 2026, from 3:00pm to 4:00pm at the Pleasant Hill Library in the maker space. Attendees drop in after school to paint a flowerpot inspired by their favorite book, character, or genre. The workshop includes planting a succulent in the painted pot and learning proper succulent care, led by staff from the Ruth Bancroft Garden. No registration is required, though attendance is limited to tweens and teens as space and supplies permit. The event is generously funded by the Friends of the Pleasant Hill Library. Location: 2 Monticello Avenue, Pleasant Hill, CA 94523.

events.title: Summer Adventure Middle School Volunteer Orientation
events.description: Are you going into 6th, 7th, or 8th grade in the fall? Consider volunteering for the library this summer! Our Summer Adventure volunteers help kids and families participate in Summer Adventure and earn prizes!
events.event_detail: Summer Adventure Middle School Volunteer Orientation is an informational session for students entering 6th, 7th, or 8th grade in the fall who are interested in volunteering at the library during Summer Adventure. The orientation takes place from 3:00 PM to 4:00 PM at the Castro Valley library branch. Volunteers will learn about helping kids and families participate in Summer Adventure activities and earn prizes. Required qualities include being friendly, organized, and enthusiastic about engaging with the community. All potential volunteers must attend one of the three orientation sessions offered. Library staff may take photos or recordings at the event, and accessibility accommodations like ASL interpreters or closed captioning are available with 7 days advance notice.

events.title: Game Room
events.description: Come enjoy some video games! We'll have games for all ages available for you to play together on the Nintendo Switch.
events.event_detail: Game Room is a video gaming event held at the Half Moon Bay library branch in San Mateo County Libraries. The event takes place from 3:00 PM to 4:30 PM (specific dates not shown in excerpt). Participants can enjoy playing Nintendo Switch games together, with games available for all ages. Attendees are encouraged to bring their own controllers if they prefer. No registration is required to attend. This event is designed for children ages 6-11 and teens ages 12-18, providing a fun, social gaming experience in a library setting.

events.title: Paws to Read
events.description: Would your child like to earn Summer Reading minutes reading to a friendly dog? Children in grades K through 5 can 'Paws to Read' with dogs certified for sociability.
events.event_detail: Paws to Read is a library reading program where children in grades K through 5 can read aloud to friendly therapy dogs certified for sociability. The event takes place at the Orinda Library branch in the Children's Alcove. Children can earn Summer Reading minutes while practicing reading with a calm, patient listener. Beginning readers benefit from the dogs' non-judgmental attention, while more confident readers can de-stress by reading to a furry friend. The event runs on Monday, June 1, 2026 from 3:15pm to 3:30pm. Registration is full but interested attendees can join the waitlist.

events.title: Free Meals at the Library / Comida gratis en la biblioteca
events.description: Get your FREE meal at the East Palo Alto Library. Adults with kids eat free too!
events.event_detail: Free Meals at the Library is a community food program providing complimentary meals to children and adults at the East Palo Alto Library. The event runs from 3:15 PM to 3:45 PM. Adults with children eat free as well, making this an excellent resource for families. The program is available in English, Spanish, and Tongan, reflecting the diverse East Palo Alto community. Attendees can simply show up during the specified time to receive a free meal. This initiative is part of San Mateo County Libraries' community resources and food security programs, supporting local families with nutritious meals. No registration or documentation is required to participate.

events.title: Eastmont Teen Cineplex
events.description: Teens! Come by the Eastmont Branch Teen Zone every Monday after school and watch a movie!
events.event_detail: Eastmont Teen Cineplex is a weekly movie screening event for teens held every Monday from 3:30 PM to 5:30 PM at the Eastmont Branch Teen Zone of the Oakland Public Library. The program runs every Monday after school during the school year. Attendees can watch a variety of films including comedies, dramas, documentaries, sci-fi/fantasy, and action/adventure movies. Free snacks are provided. After the screening, teens can hang out on comfy couches and discuss the film with fellow attendees. It's a casual, social event where teens decide whether the movie is a timeless classic or "trash." The event is suitable for teens and conducted in English.

events.title: LEGO Club for Grades K - 8
events.description: Join us for an hour of fun building with LEGOs. Children will use their creativity and engineering skills to free build anything they can imagine.

events.title: Game Zone
events.description: Are you an expert at video, board, and card games? Do you want to demonstrate your skills, or just want to learn the basics?
events.event_detail: Game Zone is a free teen gaming event held at the Hillview Branch Library in San Jose. The event runs from 3:30 PM to 4:30 PM and is open to teens ages 12-18 and pre-teens ages 10-12. Attendees can play video games, board games, card games, or enjoy a game of pool in the Teen Room. The event is casual and designed for both experienced gamers and beginners wanting to learn or demonstrate their skills. No registration is required. Note: This specific occurrence is canceled.

events.title: Paws to Read
events.description: Would your child like to earn Summer Reading minutes reading to a friendly dog? Children in grades K through 5 can 'Paws to Read' with dogs certified for sociability.
events.event_detail: Paws to Read is a reading program where children in grades K through 5 can read to friendly, certified therapy dogs. The event takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026, from 3:30pm to 3:45pm at the Orinda Library branch in the Children's Alcove (26 Orinda Way, Orinda, CA 94563). Children can earn Summer Reading minutes by reading to the dogs. Beginning readers benefit from a calm, patient listener, while more confident readers can de-stress by spending time with a furry friend. This is a free library event open to children ages 6-12, with registration required (currently full, waitlist available).

events.title: Storytime: For Toddlers
events.description: Toddler storytime at Park
events.event_detail: Storytime for Toddlers is a library program designed for young children ages 16 months through 2 years, along with their caregivers. The event features books, songs, movement activities, and more in an interactive, engaging format. This drop-in program requires no registration and takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026, from 3:30 PM to 4:00 PM. The event occurs in the Park Meeting Room at the Park branch of the San Francisco Public Library, located at 1833 Page Street in San Francisco. Caregivers can expect a fun, educational experience that helps develop early literacy skills while young toddlers stay engaged through songs, stories, and movement. All SFPL locations are wheelchair accessible, and accommodations can be requested by contacting the library.

events.title: Free Computer Classes
events.description: Join us at the East Palo Alto Library for a free Computer Classes! Learn the basics of using a computer in a friendly, hands-on environment.
events.event_detail: Free Computer Classes at the East Palo Alto Library. Classes run from 3:30 PM to 5:00 PM, with Monday sessions conducted in Spanish and Tuesday sessions in English. This beginner-friendly, hands-on class teaches essential computer skills including mouse and keyboard use, internet navigation, email setup, and basic document creation. No prior experience is required. Suitable for adults 19 and older. The event is free and hosted by San Mateo County Libraries.

events.title: Homework Help Center
events.description: Need homework help? Drop by San Lorenzo Library's Learning Center for free after-school help for kids. Get your homework questions answered for grades K-8 every Monday through Thursday from 3:30-5:30PM.
events.event_detail: Homework Help Center is a free after-school homework assistance program for children in grades K-8. The event takes place at San Lorenzo Library's Learning Center every Monday through Thursday from 3:30 PM to 5:30 PM. Students can drop in without registration to get help with their homework questions. Library staff or volunteers provide the assistance. Note: The program is closed during San Lorenzo School District holidays and teacher in-service workdays. The event is suitable for kids and conducted in English.

events.title: Presentation: Edible and Poisonous Mushrooms of California
events.description: Presentation on California mushrooms
events.event_detail: Presentation on Edible and Poisonous Mushrooms of California at San Francisco Public Library. Carrie Staller from Fork in the Path leads an interactive hour exploring the fascinating world of mushrooms, teaching attendees how to identify different varieties and understand the key differences between edible and poisonous mushrooms. The event takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026, from 3:30 to 5:00 PM at the Marina Branch Library Back Courtyard, located at 1890 Chestnut Street in San Francisco. This is a drop-in program with no registration required. Attendees can expect hands-on fun and interactive learning about mushroom identification, sustainable foraging practices, and California fungi. The presentation is part of the Summer Stride program and sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library. All SFPL locations are wheelchair accessible.

events.title: Maker Monday: Acrylic Stained Glass
events.description: Join us every Monday and be a Maker! Discover what you can make using our library maker tools.
events.event_detail: Maker Monday: Acrylic Stained Glass is a weekly craft program held every Monday from 3:30 PM to 4:30 PM at the Brisbane library branch of San Mateo County Libraries. Participants join the Maker Monday program to discover what they can create using the library's maker tools. The specific activity teaches techniques for creating faux acrylic stained glass artwork using paint. No registration is required; programs operate on a first-come, first-served basis. This event is suitable for children ages 6-11 and teens ages 12-18. It falls under Art & Creativity and STEAM categories. The program is conducted in English and provides a fun, crafty experience for young makers to explore their creative side in a supportive library environment.

events.title: Lego Club
events.description: Join us for LEGO fun every Monday afternoon! ¡Únete a nosotros para la diversión de LEGO cada lunes por la tarde!
events.event_detail: Lego Club is a weekly crafting and making event held every Monday from 3:30 PM to 4:30 PM at the Bolinas branch of the Marin County Free Library. Children ages 1-9 and their families are invited to join for LEGO building fun. The event is family-friendly and open to toddlers, preschoolers, and kids. Bilingual description available in English and Spanish. Participants can build and create with LEGOs in a fun, collaborative library setting.

events.title: Mending Circle / Círculo de Zurcir

events.event_detail: Mending Circle / Círculo de Zurcir is a community crafting event held at the Inverness Library on the first Monday of each month from 3:30 PM to 5:30 PM. The library provides basic mending sewing tools, and participants are encouraged to bring materials to share with others. This is a bilingual event (English and Spanish) suitable for adults. Attendees can expect a friendly, social environment where people gather to learn and practice clothing repair techniques together, share knowledge, and extend the life of their garments. The event fosters community connection through the sustainable practice of mending.
