The event takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026 from 3:45pm to 4:00pm in the Children's Alcove at the Orinda Library branch (26 Orinda Way, Orinda, CA 94563). Children can earn Summer Reading minutes while reading to the dogs. Beginning readers benefit from having a calm, patient listener, while confident readers can de-stress by spending time with a furry friend. Registration is full with a waitlist available. Parents or guardians should accompany their children. The program is indoor and climate-controlled, offering a relaxed, supportive atmosphere for developing reading skills.

events.title: Activity: Watercolor Painting
events.description: Watercolor painting activity for children
events.event_detail: A drop-in watercolor painting activity for children ages 5 and older, held at the Excelsior Meeting Room of the San Francisco Public Library. The event takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026 from 4:00 to 5:00 PM. Participants can express themselves creatively through watercolor painting with all materials provided by the library. This is part of the Summer Stride and Make + Do programs sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library. The event is wheelchair accessible and requires no registration. Children will learn basic watercolor techniques while creating their own artwork in a fun, supportive environment.

events.title: New Book Storytime
events.description: New book storytime at Alameda Free Library
events.event_detail: New Book Storytime is a free 20-30 minute storytime event for children in Kindergarten through third grade featuring picture books new to their collection. The event takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026 from 4:00 pm to 4:30 pm at the Main branch of the Alameda Free Library located at 1550 Oak St, Alameda, CA 94501. Children can expect to hear newly acquired picture books read aloud in a group setting by library staff. The event is free to attend with no registration required. Accessibility accommodations are available with advance notice. Note: Date and time are subject to change, and there are no children's programs during August.

events.title: Tech Mentor / Computer & iPad Assistance
events.description: Tech mentoring and Computer 1-on-1 assistance. A Volunteer Tech Mentor/computer coach will be available to help customers increase their computer skills.
events.event_detail: Tech mentoring and 1-on-1 computer assistance event at San Jose Public Library's Pearl Avenue branch. A volunteer tech mentor helps customers increase their computer skills, particularly useful for seniors wanting to learn digital literacy basics. Learn how to create an email, search the internet, create Microsoft Word documents, and complete online job applications. iPads are available for in-library use during the session. Drop-in schedule, no appointment needed. Held every week, typically 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM. For more information, call 408-808-3053. Suitable for adults and seniors.

events.title: Summer Learning Kickoff: For Goodness Snakes
events.description: Join us for Calabazas Branch Library's Summer (Reading) Learning Kickoff with For Goodness Snakes! For Goodness Snakes is a company that provides educational and fun filled programs through the fascinating world of reptiles.
events.event_detail: Summer Learning Kickoff: For Goodness Snakes is an educational and interactive event hosted by Calabazas Branch Library as part of the Summer Learning program. The event runs from 4:00 PM to 5:00 PM and features For Goodness Snakes, a company that provides fascinating programs about reptiles with a hands-on experience. Attendees of all ages can learn about exotic reptiles, see them up close, and even touch docile animals in a safe, fun environment. Free tickets are available at the desk 30 minutes before the program starts, with limited capacity. Registration for the broader Summer Learning program is encouraged. The event is suitable for young children, kids, teens, adults, and seniors.

events.title: Slime-Tastic Summer Series: Ocean Slime Time
events.description: Splash into an underwater slime adventure! Create crystal-clear blue ocean slime filled with fun sea creatures and seashells.
events.event_detail: Slime-Tastic Summer Series: Ocean Slime Time is a children's art and creativity event held at the Atherton library branch. The event takes place from 4:00 PM to 5:00 PM as part of a summer series. Children ages 6-11 can participate in making crystal-clear blue ocean slime decorated with sea creatures and seashells. Attendees can expect a fun, hands-on slime-making experience with an ocean theme. The event is free and held indoors at the San Mateo County Libraries location in Atherton.

events.title: Novato Conversation Club in English for Adults
events.description: Come join us at the Novato Library to practice your English language skills. Be part of this free weekly program. At every class there will be a leading tutor from the Novato Library and assisting tutors to help participants practice their English.
events.event_detail: Novato Conversation Club in English for Adults is a free weekly program held at the Novato Library where adults can practice their English language skills. The club meets every week from 4:00 PM to 5:30 PM. Trained tutors from the Novato Library lead the sessions and assist participants in improving their English conversation abilities. No registration is required to attend. This is an excellent opportunity for adults looking to practice speaking English in a supportive, welcoming environment with guidance from experienced language instructors.

events.title: Teen Dungeons & Dragons Club @ Main TeenZone
events.description: DungeonMaster Vic Presents... Dungeons & Dragons Club! Mondays 4:00-6:00pm. Free and open to all teens 12-18; no experience needed.
events.event_detail: Teen Dungeons & Dragons Club is a free gaming event held at the Main Library TeenZone in Oakland. The club meets on Mondays from 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM and is open to all teens ages 12-18. No experience with Dungeons & Dragons is needed to participate. All materials are provided, including snacks for attendees. The event is hosted by DungeonMaster Vic and space is limited, so calling ahead to confirm availability is recommended. Teens can expect to play tabletop role-playing games, create characters, and enjoy an interactive social gaming experience in a library setting.

events.title: Drop-In Tech Help (Concord)
events.description: Do you have basic computer and technology questions? Need help with eBooks, emailing, printing, or basic web searching? Drop in to the Concord Library for help from one of our tech volunteers! Feel free to bring your own device.
events.event_detail: Drop-In Tech Help is a free library program where volunteers help attendees with basic computer and technology questions. The event takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026, from 4:00pm to 6:00pm at the Concord Library branch located at 2900 Salvio Street, Concord, CA 94519. Attendees can bring their own devices (tablet, phone, or laptop) or use a library computer. Volunteers can assist with basic web searching, eBooks and eReaders, printing and copying, emailing, saving and attaching files, navigating the library website, using digital resources like Libby, Kanopy, and Flipster, and Microsoft Office and Google Suite. Please note that volunteers cannot repair devices, install software updates, provide typing services, or conduct personal research. This is a casual drop-in session, so attendees may need to wait if volunteers are assisting others.

events.title: Dungeons & Dragons®
events.description: Join a Dungeons & Dragons® adventure with other teens. Our teen volunteers will create the one-shots. D&D at the San Ramon Library plays at level 5. Get a jump start on the game by bringing a level 5 character sheet!
events.event_detail: Dungeons & Dragons® adventure for teens at the San Ramon Library. Join other teens for a D&D one-shot adventure created by teen volunteers. The game plays at level 5, so attendees are encouraged to bring a pre-made level 5 character sheet. This event takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026, from 4:00pm to 5:30pm at the San Ramon Library branch located at 100 Montgomery Street, San Ramon, CA 94583. Open to middle schoolers and high schoolers only. Programming is supported by the San Ramon Library Foundation. Note: This event has been canceled.

events.title: Chess Club for Kids
events.description: Come learn to play chess, or just play a game! This is an informal and welcoming program for kids up to age 12 and their families. Chess Club meets every Monday.
events.event_detail: Chess Club for Kids is an informal and welcoming program at the Willow Glen library branch where children up to age 12 and their families can come learn to play chess or simply enjoy a game. The club meets every Monday from 4:00 PM to 5:00 PM. This is a great opportunity for kids who want to learn chess strategy, practice their skills, or play casually with peers. Chess boards and pieces are typically provided by the library. Parents and caregivers are welcome to participate or observe. Participants should check the event listing for any date cancellations due to library holidays.

events.title: Tech Help
events.description: Need tech assistance? Drop by for personalized support at our Tech Drop-Ins! Whether it's software updates, data transfers, or general computer queries, our experts are here to help. Explore affordable internet options, navigate ACP.
events.event_detail: Tech Help is a free library program offering personalized tech assistance at Tully Community Library. Drop in anytime between 4:00 PM and 5:30 PM for help with software updates, data transfers, computer queries, and other technology issues. Library experts can also help you explore affordable internet options and navigate the Affordable Connectivity Program (ACP) transitions. Tech help is available in both English and Vietnamese. This event is suitable for adults and seniors who need guidance with technology. No registration required—just bring your device and questions. The library provides free Wi-Fi and access to technology resources to help you succeed.

events.title: One-On-One Reading Coach for Kids
events.description: Our One-on-One Reading Tutor for Kids provides students in grades K-3 with an opportunity to improve their reading skills by working one-on-one with a reading coach.
events.event_detail: One-On-One Reading Coach for Kids is a free library program at the Cambrian Branch Library providing students in grades K-3 with one-on-one reading support. Children work with a reading coach who helps build confidence through phonics, sight words, and comprehension practice. Sessions run 15 minutes on a first come, first served basis during the scheduled 4:00 PM – 5:00 PM time slot. Kids can bring their favorite book or choose from the library's available selection to read aloud to their coach. The program encourages young readers to practice their skills with an adult volunteer in a positive environment. Participants can also use their session to read away library fines. No pre-registration required.

events.title: Make It Mondays: Paper Stingrays Grab & Go
events.description: Join us every Monday for arts and crafts at the library! Each week will feature a different activity that focuses on building creativity, social-emotional, and school readiness skills through art. All supplies will be provided!
events.event_detail: Make It Mondays: Paper Stingrays Grab & Go is a weekly arts and crafts program held every Monday from 4:00 PM to 5:00 PM at the Seven Trees branch of the San Jose Public Library. This family-friendly event encourages children to explore their creativity through hands-on art activities designed to build creativity, social-emotional skills, and school readiness. Participants will create paper stingray crafts. All supplies are provided by the library, so no prior materials are needed. The program is suitable for young children ages 0-5 and kids ages 5-10. Attendees can expect a welcoming environment where they can learn, create, and have fun with other families in the community.

events.title: Crochet Club
events.description: All are welcome—from beginners to experienced enthusiasts. Bring your own project or start a new one as we refine our skills and discuss all things crochet. A volunteer is available to provide instructions and offer advice to beginners.
events.event_detail: Crochet Club is a free crafting and hobby event held at the Tully library branch. The event runs from 4:30 PM to 6:00 PM. All skill levels are welcome, from beginners to experienced crocheters. Attendees can bring their own ongoing project or start something new. A volunteer is available to provide instructions and advice to beginners. The library provides all tools and supplies, so no equipment is needed to attend. The minimum age to participate is six years old. The event is suitable for adults, teens, pre-teens, kids, and seniors. Participants can refine their crochet skills, learn new techniques, and socialize with other craft enthusiasts in a relaxed library setting.

events.title: Gaming Mondays
events.description: Welcome to Gaming Mondays! Join us for video games, board games, and puzzles. Plus, there will be snacks and drinks. This program is for students in middle school and high school.
events.event_detail: Gaming Mondays is a weekly teen gaming event held at the Newark Branch of Alameda County Library. The event runs every Monday from 4:30 PM to 5:30 PM. Participants can enjoy video games, board games, and puzzles. Snacks and drinks are provided for attendees. This program is designed for middle school and high school students. Library staff may be present to assist and facilitate the activities. ASL interpretation and closed captioning are available upon request with 7 days notice.

events.title: Music and Movement in Vietnamese and English and Craft
events.description: Bilingual Music and Movement in English and Vietnamese is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities through songs, rhymes, finger plays, and movement activities.
events.event_detail: Bilingual Music and Movement in English and Vietnamese is a family-friendly event held at the Evergreen Branch of San José Public Library. The program runs from 4:30 PM to 5:30 PM, typically on the 4th Tuesday of each month. Families with children of all ages are invited to participate in early literacy activities including songs, nursery rhymes, finger plays, and movement activities conducted in both English and Vietnamese. Following the storytime, children create a simple craft to take home. On the 4th Tuesday of each month, a bilingual story is read during the program. This indoor event is free and requires no registration. Designed for young children ages 0-5 and kids ages 5-10 along with their parents and caregivers, the program promotes the joys of learning through interactive musical and movement experiences for the whole family.

events.title: ELL Conversation Club for Beginners
events.description: Come and practice speaking English with a friendly group in the library. We will practice vocabulary for everyday activities, listening skills, reading skills, and speaking skills. Free. No registration is required. For ages 18+ only.
events.event_detail: ELL Conversation Club for Beginners is a free English language learning event held at the Cambrian branch of San Jose Public Library. The event runs from 4:30 PM to 5:30 PM. Attendees practice vocabulary for everyday activities while developing their listening, reading, and speaking skills in a supportive, friendly group environment. No registration is required to attend. This event is specifically designed for adults ages 18+ and seniors. Participants can expect interactive conversation practice with others at a similar English proficiency level, making it an ideal starting point for beginners looking to improve their conversational English skills in a low-pressure setting.

events.title: Santa Teresa Junior Math Club
events.description: Want to grow in understanding basic math concepts and working on basic competitive math skills? Join us in Santa Teresa Junior Math Club and see your math and problem-solving skills improve!
events.event_detail: Santa Teresa Junior Math Club is a free weekly library program for children in 3rd through 5th grade (ages 8-11). The club helps kids grow their understanding of basic math concepts and competitive math skills, including rounding, fractions, area, perimeter, data and graphs, money, polygons, angles, and decimals. Sessions take place every Monday from 4:30 PM to 5:30 PM, starting March 2, 2026, in the Santa Teresa Library Community Room. The program is led by a teen volunteer and runs weekly with some scheduled exceptions. No registration is required—walk-ins are welcome until capacity is reached, and you can join any session since they are not related to each other. Participants can register online to receive reminder emails 24 hours before events.

events.title: 星期一下午:三国演义 (儿童读书会)
events.description: A book club dedicated to 'Three Kingdoms,' the classic Chinese fiction. This club is designed for children who are fans of the story and is conducted entirely in Mandarin Chinese.
events.event_detail: A children's book club dedicated to the classic Chinese novel 'Romance of the Three Kingdoms' (三国演义). The event is held at Calabazas library branch on Monday afternoons from 4:30 PM to 5:30 PM. Conducted entirely in Mandarin Chinese, the club features exciting stories including famous battles, heroes like Cao Cao, Liu Bei, and Sun Quan, and classic Chinese idioms (成语故事) such as 'Three Brothers of the Plum Blossom,' 'The Battle of Guandu,' and 'The Three Visits to the Thatched Cottage.' Organized by teen volunteers from Lynbrook High School, this free parent-child activity has limited seating. Tickets are distributed 30 minutes before the session at the information desk. Suitable for children ages 0-12 and their families. The event was scheduled for 7/20/2026 but is currently canceled.

events.title: English Conversation Club
events.description: Practice your English with others in a friendly group setting. Different discussion topics each week. All levels welcome.
events.event_detail: English Conversation Club at the Eastmont Branch of Oakland Public Library. Practice your English with others in a friendly group setting. Different discussion topics each week. All levels welcome. Takes place from 4:30 PM – 5:30 PM. Suitable for adults and seniors. This ESL event provides an opportunity to practice speaking English in a supportive environment with fellow learners. No registration required.

events.title: Sip Tea and Paint, for Adults
events.description: Join us for a relaxing afternoon with coffee, tea, and paint. Paint supplies, instruction, and hot beverages will be provided. Follow the given example, or paint something original!
events.event_detail: Sip Tea and Paint is an arts and crafts program for adults and teens held at the Cherryland branch of Alameda County Library. The event runs from 4:30 PM to 6:00 PM and offers a relaxing afternoon of painting with coffee and tea provided. Participants receive paint supplies, instruction, and hot beverages. Attendees can follow the provided example design or create something original. Space is limited to 15 people, so registration is required to guarantee a spot. The program is bilingual, offered in both English and Spanish.

events.title: English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club
events.description: Boost your English conversation skills with our volunteer instructor, Ms. Veena, in a welcoming and respectful setting tailored for adult learners. Improve your speaking and listening abilities, broaden your vocabulary.
events.event_detail: English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club is a free weekly conversation class for adult learners held at the Calabazas branch library in the Group Study Room. Sessions run every Monday from 4:30 PM to 5:30 PM, except for the last Monday of each month. Participants can improve their English speaking and listening skills, expand their vocabulary, and engage in discussions on current events with guidance from volunteer instructor Ms. Veena. The welcoming environment is designed for adults and seniors seeking to enhance their English proficiency. Pre-registration is required to receive reminder emails and lesson plan details. All skill levels are welcome to attend this no-cost program.

events.title: Youth Arts Connection Workshops
events.description: Hey Teens! Got something to say? Want to write poetry, drop bars, make music, or just get creative with others who understand where you're coming from? Youth Arts Connection is your space to do all that and more.
events.event_detail: Youth Arts Connection Workshops are free creative sessions for teens held at the Pittsburg Library in Contra Costa County. The workshops take place on Monday, June 1, 2026, from 5:00pm to 7:00pm. These sessions are led by local artists Jeremy Phillips and Tajanique, who are experienced voices in poetry, music, and community work. The program is designed for young people ages 12 to 18 who want to express themselves creatively through activities like writing poetry, creating music, and exploring various art forms. Participants can expect a welcoming space focused on self-expression, connection with peers, and building real-life skills that support academic success and future goals. The workshops emphasize community building and providing teens with tools to share their voices. Art classes are funded by Measure X. Accommodations are available for those who need them with advance notice. The Pittsburg Library is located at 80 Power Avenue, Pittsburg, CA 94565.

events.title: Digital Help Hub |Centro de Ayuda Digital
events.description: One-on-one and small-group help for real-life tech tasks. Learn what you need, at your pace.
events.event_detail: Digital Help Hub is a free tech assistance event held at North Fair Oaks Library in San Mateo County. The event runs from 5:00 PM to 8:00 PM and offers one-on-one and small-group help for real-life technology tasks. Attendees can get personalized assistance with everyday tech challenges such as sending email attachments, using smartphones, navigating devices, or any other technology needs at their own pace. Tech-savvy volunteers provide the guidance. No registration is required—simply drop in during the scheduled hours. The event is bilingual, available in both English and Spanish. Suitable for adults aged 19 and older. This is an excellent opportunity for anyone looking to build confidence with technology in a supportive, patient environment.

events.title: Reading Buddies with Grant
events.description: Children in grades K-5 will discover the joy of reading while improving their reading skills through practice with Grant on Mondays. Our reading buddy will listen to children and help them build confidence.
events.event_detail: Reading Buddies with Grant is a free library program held at King Library (Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr., Library) in San Jose. Children in grades K-5 meet with Grant on Mondays from 5:00 PM to 6:00 PM for one-on-one reading practice. Grant is a trained reading buddy who listens to children read, helps them build reading confidence, and asks questions about books to encourage reading comprehension. Sessions are available on a first come, first served basis. This is an academic support event suitable for kids ages 5-10. Children should arrive ready to read and enjoy a supportive learning environment.

events.title: Cambrian Pokemon Club
events.description: Join us to have fun playing Pokemon, trading cards, and learning strategies for improving your game!
events.event_detail: Cambrian Pokemon Club is a weekly event at the Cambrian Library branch of San Jose Public Library held from 5:00 PM to 6:00 PM. Children ages 5-10 and pre-teens ages 10-12 are invited to join for fun playing Pokemon, trading cards, and learning strategies to improve their game. Note: This event is currently canceled. Participants can expect to interact with other Pokemon enthusiasts, participate in card trading sessions, and learn game tactics in a fun, social environment.

events.title: Family Movie: Finding Nemo
events.description: Join us for a family friendly movie. Bring a blanket to watch on the floor the movie Finding Nemo. After his son is captured in the Great Barrier Reef and taken to Sydney, a timid clownfish sets out on a journey to bring him home.
events.event_detail: Family Movie: Finding Nemo is a free family-friendly movie screening at the Alameda County Library in Dublin. The event runs from 5:00 PM to 7:00 PM. Attendees are encouraged to bring a blanket to sit on the floor while watching the film. Finding Nemo follows a timid clownfish who embarks on a journey to rescue his son from Sydney after he's captured in the Great Barrier Reef. This event is part of the Summer Adventure program and is suitable for adults, teens, kids, and everyone. ASL interpretation or closed captioning can be provided if requested at least 7 days in advance.

events.title: Minty Mondays OG Karaoke at The Mint
events.description: OG Karaoke night
events.event_detail: Minty Mondays is a free open-stage karaoke event held every Monday from 5 PM to 2 AM at The Mint Karaoke Lounge in San Francisco. This iconic karaoke night has been running since 1993 and is considered the original OG crowd in the Castro/Mid-Market area. There's no cover charge and no song fees - just a cash bar. Attendees are seated on a first come, first served basis. The crowd typically includes a mix of regulars and walk-ins from the Castro and Mid-Market neighborhoods. It's a great way to enjoy karaoke for free in one of SF's longest-running karaoke institutions.

events.title: In-Person English Conversation Club
events.description: Improve your English and make new friends! Practice your speaking skills with fluent speakers and other English language learners in a small group.
events.event_detail: In-Person English Conversation Club is a library-hosted event where English language learners practice speaking with fluent speakers in a small group setting. The event runs from 5:00 PM to 6:00 PM at the Atherton branch of San Mateo County Libraries. Participants can improve their English conversation skills, meet new people, and build confidence in speaking. Open to all skill levels, the club welcomes adults ages 18 and over who want to practice everyday English conversation in a supportive, friendly environment. No registration required, though capacity limits may apply.

events.title: Open Sewing
events.description: Join us for open time to use the library's sewing machines. Bring your own project or use some of our supplies to make your own.
events.event_detail: Open Sewing is a drop-in crafting event at the Half Moon Bay Library where attendees can use the library's sewing machines to work on personal projects or use available supplies. The event runs from 5:00 PM to 7:45 PM. No formal instruction is provided, but staff assistance is available for machine operation if needed. Suitable for all ages (children 6-11, teens 12-18, and adults 19+). Participants are encouraged to bring their own sewing projects and materials. The event is held in English and Spanish.

events.title: Gentle Yoga / Yoga Relajante
events.description: Discover a soothing practice designed for all bodies and all levels. Gentle Yoga invites you to relax, restore, and feel better from the inside out. Free. No registration required. Bring your own mat.
events.event_detail: Gentle Yoga / Yoga Relajante is a free yoga class held at the Hillview branch of San Jose Public Library. The class runs from 5:00 PM to 6:00 PM and is designed for all bodies and all levels, focusing on relaxation and restoration. Attendees can expect gentle stretches and calming exercises that help feel better from the inside out. No registration is required, but participants must bring their own yoga mat. The class is offered in English with a Spanish description available, making it accessible to a diverse community. This event is suitable for adults and seniors looking for a low-impact, peaceful exercise opportunity in a welcoming library environment.

events.title: Clases de inglés para Hispanos - Nivel 1
events.description: ¿Quieres mejorar tu vocabulario en Inglés, aprender gramática y hacer amigos?
events.event_detail: English Classes for Hispanics - Level 1 is a free language learning program offered by San José Public Library at Educational Park branch. Classes run from 5:00 PM to 6:30 PM, taught by volunteer Mike. The class is designed for Spanish speakers who want to improve their English vocabulary, learn grammar, and make new friends. No class sessions are held on April 22 and May 25 (Memorial Day). Registration is required via email to marcela.guevara@sjlibrary.org. Educational materials are provided at no cost. This program is suitable for adults ages 18+ and seniors ages 65+. Classes are conducted in both English and Spanish, making them accessible for beginning English learners.

events.title: Arts and Crafts Storytime
events.description: Join us for stories and songs for children 0-5 followed by arts and crafts time every first Monday! Develop your child's early literacy skills through reading, singing, playing, writing, and talking.
events.event_detail: Arts and Crafts Storytime is a library program for children ages 0-5 years old. The event takes place on the first Monday of each month from 5:15pm to 5:45pm at the San Pablo Library branch, located at 13751 San Pablo Avenue, San Pablo, CA 94806. Each session begins with stories and songs, followed by hands-on arts and crafts activities. The program aims to develop early literacy skills in young children through reading, singing, playing, writing, and talking. Parents and caregivers attend with their children to participate together in this engaging and educational experience. No registration is required to attend this free library program.

items.name: Children's smock or old shirt for craft time

events.title: Crockett Library Game Night
events.description: Come join us for Game Night Mondays - except the 1st Monday of the month - at the Crockett Library. Chess, card games, other classics, and even Settlers of Catan. Additionally, every THIRD Monday we're playing Dungeons and Dragons.
events.event_detail: Crockett Library Game Night is a weekly community gaming event held on Mondays (except the 1st Monday of each month) from 5:30pm to 7:30pm at the Crockett Library branch, located at 991 Loring Avenue, Crockett, CA 94525. Attendees can enjoy various board games including chess, card games, classic games, and Settlers of Catan. On the third Monday of each month, the event features Dungeons and Dragons gameplay. This event is designed for teens (13-18 years) and tweens (9-12 years). The library provides a welcoming space for social gaming, strategy building, and fun with peers. No registration is required to attend.

events.title: Family Storytime + Stay & Play
events.description: Storytime is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities such as stories, songs, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement activities.
events.event_detail: Family Storytime + Stay & Play is a free library program at Seven Trees branch for children of all ages and their parents/caregivers. The event runs from 5:30 PM to 6:30 PM, with Storytime from 5:30-6:00 PM featuring stories, songs, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement activities, followed by Stay & Play from 6:00-6:30 PM where children can play with toys, meet new friends, get book recommendations, and create something. The program promotes early literacy and the joys of reading for the whole family. Limited capacity; no registration required.

events.title: Open Sewing
events.description: Join us for open time to use the library's sewing machines. Bring your project or use some of our supplies to make your own.
events.event_detail: Open Sewing is a drop-in crafting event at the Foster City Library where participants can use the library's sewing machines during open studio time. The event runs from 6:00 PM to 7:30 PM and is a recurring program. Attendees can bring their own sewing project or use supplies provided by the library to create something new. There is no formal instruction, but staff assistance is available for the machines as time and staffing permit. Children ages 7 and younger are welcome with caregiver supervision. Suitable for children (6-11), teens (12-18), adults (19+), and is 55+ friendly. No registration is required.

events.title: Monday Vibe Check: Teen Hangout - DIY Photo Collage
events.description: The Atherton Library and the Atherton Youth Advisory Group present Monday Vibe Check – Teen Hangout as part of this summer's teen programming lineup.
events.event_detail: Monday Vibe Check is a monthly teen hangout event held on the first Monday of each month at the Atherton Library from 6:00 PM to 7:00 PM. This session features a DIY photo collage activity where teens can create a cozy, personalized hanging wall display using their favorite photos, polaroids, and aesthetic prints. The event includes art projects, music, snacks, and casual social time. Part of the summer teen programming lineup presented by the Atherton Library and the Atherton Youth Advisory Group. Suitable for teens ages 12-18. No registration required.

events.title: Clase de inglés gratuita | Free English Class
events.description: Aprende inglés en esta clase en persona gratuita enseñada por un instructor certificado.
events.event_detail: Free English Class (Clase de inglés gratuita) is a free in-person English language learning event taught by a certified instructor. The class runs from 6:00 PM to 7:30 PM and focuses on learning and practicing English that will be helpful in everyday life. This event is suitable for adults (19+) and covers life skills, literacy, and ESL topics. The class takes place at Pescadero Elementary School in San Mateo County Libraries system. Attendees can expect to learn practical English skills in a supportive environment with a certified instructor.

events.title: Grateful Mondays Tribute w/ Ted & Company
events.description: Grateful Dead tribute show
events.event_detail: Grateful Mondays is a weekly free live music event featuring Ted & Company, a local Grateful Dead cover band. The event takes place every Monday from 6:00 PM to 10:00 PM at Winters Tavern in Pacifica. Attendees can expect to hear two rocking sets of classic Grateful Dead tunes performed by a five-piece band including Ted Silverman on guitar/vocals, Odin Berkelman-Rosado on guitar/vocals, Anthony Albert on keys, Steve Tocchini on bass/vocals, and Jerry Herrera on drums/vocals. The event is described as a 'real good time' and is free to attend.

events.title: Fiction Book Club: Global Reads
events.description: Join the San Carlos Library's fiction book club as we explore world literature one translation at a time.
events.event_detail: Fiction Book Club: Global Reads is a monthly book club at the San Carlos Library that explores world literature through translated works originally written in languages other than English, with a focus on 21st century works and diverse cultural voices. The club meets twice monthly - on the first Monday at 6 PM and the first Wednesday at 10:30 AM, with each session lasting one hour. Attendees can expect engaging group discussions about the selected translated fiction. For June, the club is reading and discussing 'Fever Dream' by Samanta Schweblin. This event is suitable for adults (19+) and is also 55+ friendly. Participants should obtain a copy of the current month's book selection prior to attending.

events.title: Free In-Person English Class | Clase de inglés en persona gratuita
events.description: Learn English in this free beginner's in-person class. We will learn and practice English, which will be helpful in your everyday life.
events.event_detail: Free In-Person English Class hosted by San Mateo County Libraries. This is a beginner-level English language class for adults (19+) where participants learn and practice English for everyday life situations. The class runs from 6:00 PM to 7:15 PM. Registration is required as space is limited. The venue is KIPP Esperanza High School. The class is bilingual, offering instruction in both English and Spanish to accommodate diverse learners.

events.title: Castro Valley Library Teen Advisory Group
events.description: Make a difference in your community by joining the Castro Valley Library Teen Advisory Group (CSVTAG). Brainstorm, Organize and Plan Library Events. Gain Leadership Skills. Earn Volunteer Hours. Give Back to Your Community.
events.event_detail: Castro Valley Library Teen Advisory Group (CSVTAG) is a recurring monthly meeting for teens in grades 8-12 who want to make a difference in their community. The group meets on the 1st and 3rd Monday of each month from 6:00 PM to 7:00 PM at the Castro Valley Library branch. During meetings, teens brainstorm, organize, and plan library events while gaining leadership skills and earning volunteer hours. Members uphold responsibilities as community leaders and are expected to attend regularly scheduled meetings. This is an opportunity for teens to actively contribute to library programming, develop leadership abilities, and give back to their local community. The event is organized by Alameda County Library.

events.title: Reading Buddies for Grades K-6 (6:00pm session)
events.description: Practice your reading skills by reading aloud one on one with a furry friend! Each 15-minute session is with a specially trained therapy dog.
events.event_detail: Reading Buddies is a library program at Morgan Hill Library where children in grades K-6 can practice reading aloud one-on-one with a specially trained therapy dog and its volunteer handler. The...

events.title: Family Storytime
events.description: Enjoy stories, songs, and rhymes that encourage a love of reading and learning. This program is geared towards toddlers and preschoolers but is open to all ages.
events.event_detail: Family Storytime is a library program featuring stories, songs, and rhymes designed to encourage a love of reading and learning in children. The event takes place at the Alameda County Library branch in Castro Valley, typically at 6:00 PM – 6:30 PM as a recurring program. Geared towards toddlers and preschoolers but open to all ages, this 30-minute session offers a fun and educational experience for families. Children can expect to participate in interactive reading activities, sing along to songs, and learn rhymes in a welcoming library environment. Parents and caregivers can attend with their children to enjoy quality storytime together. Library staff may take photos or videos at the event, and accessibility accommodations like ASL interpreters or closed captioning are available with advance notice.

events.title: Drop-In Shop for Adults
events.description: If you're a seasoned artist, someone crafty, DIY enthusiast who likes to dabble, come check out Drop-In Maker Space. Our volunteers and community experts are there every Monday night to assist with starting a new project.
events.event_detail: Drop-In Shop for Adults is a maker space event at the Pleasant Hill Library on Monday, June 1, 2026 from 6:00pm to 7:45pm. The event is held in the Maker Space at 2 Monticello Avenue. This drop-in session welcomes seasoned artists, crafters, and DIY enthusiasts to work on projects with help from volunteers and community experts. The space is equipped with a Cameo Silhouette Pro for crafting, an Epilog Fusion Pro laser cutter, Ultimaker s5 3D printer, and multiple sewing machines. Whether you need help starting a new project, overcoming a creative hurdle, or just want room to spread out and create, the Maker Space has resources available. No high-tech experience is required to use the equipment. This event is for adults 18 and over only. A Maker Safety Waiver is required for hands-on participation. The space continues to evolve, so drop in to see what's new each week.

events.title: Zumba at Morgan Hill Library
events.description: Join us for a free dance and rhythm based workout. This Latin-inspired, easy-to-follow, dance-fitness party exhilarates your senses and works all major muscle groups.
events.event_detail: Zumba at Morgan Hill Library is a free dance and rhythm based workout event. The event takes place from 6:00 PM to 7:00 PM at Morgan Hill Library, part of the Santa Clara County Library District. This Latin-inspired, easy-to-follow dance-fitness party exhilarates your senses and works all major muscle groups in a high-energy cardio blast. The class features rhythms like salsa, merengue, cumbia and samba set to Latin and international beats. Attendees should wear comfortable workout clothes and shoes, bring a bottle of water and a towel. This event is suitable for adults and older adults. Note: This event is currently canceled.

events.title: Computer Help
events.description: Drop in for computer help with our volunteers. Volunteers can assist with eReaders, Smart phones, basic computer skills, and printing/scanning. They are first come first serve.
events.event_detail: Computer Help is a free library event offering drop-in assistance from volunteers who can help with eReaders, smartphones, basic computer skills, and printing/scanning. The session is scheduled for Monday, June 1, 2026, from 6:00pm to 7:45pm at the Brentwood library branch located at 104 Oak Street, Brentwood, California 94513. This is a first come first served program suitable for all ages. Attendees can expect personalized help with their devices in a welcoming library environment.

events.title: SF Arcade Bar Emporium - 8 Free Game Tokens for Industry Night
events.description: 8 free game tokens for industry workers
events.event_detail: Emporium Arcade Bar hosts Industry Night every Monday from 6 pm to 2 am at their San Francisco location on Divisadero Street. This weekly event offers 8 free game tokens to anyone who works in the hospitality industry, including bar staff, restaurant workers, and nightlife employees. The venue features classic arcade games, pool tables, pinball machines, foosball, and retro console games on a 50-inch HD screen. Guests can enjoy craft beer selections, innovative cocktails, boozy slushies, and an expansive liquor menu. Most games only require one token, so industry workers can play approximately four games for free. Emporium SF is open daily to guests 21 years or older. The venue showcases vibrant murals by local artists and has a fun-loving, colorful atmosphere.

events.title: Community Co-Working Night
events.description: Finally tackle your to-do list in a relaxed, supportive community space.
events.event_detail: Community Co-Working Night is a relaxed, donation-based event at Mystic in Mill Valley, CA, designed to help attendees finally tackle tasks they've been putting off. The event takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026, from 6:15 pm to 7:45 pm. Participants are encouraged to bring their laptop, to-do list, and whatever tasks they've been avoiding. The evening offers a cozy, supportive environment where like-minded individuals can work alongside each other in a low-key setting. Whether it's emails, scheduling, creative projects, or life admin, attendees can focus on their work while enjoying community support. The venue is located at 31 Sunnyside Ave, and admission ranges from $5 to $60 per person. Come as you are, stay as long as you like.

events.title: Clases Gratuitas de Ingles | Free English Classes
events.description: Aprende y practica inglés en una clase presencial y acogedora en la Guardería Footsteps.
events.event_detail: Free English Classes (Clases Gratuitas de Ingles) held at Footsteps Childcare, hosted by San Mateo County Libraries. This is a welcoming, in-person English as a Second Language (ESL) class where childcare is provided while parents study. Attendees can build their speaking, listening, reading, and writing skills for everyday life with a certified instructor. All skill levels are welcome. Classes run from 6:15 PM to 7:45 PM and are suitable for adults (19+) and those 55 and older. The program focuses on life skills and literacy development.

events.title: Reading Buddies for Grades K-6 (6:15pm session)
events.description: Practice your reading skills by reading aloud one on one with a furry friend! Each 15-minute session is with a specially trained therapy dog.
events.event_detail: Reading Buddies for Grades K-6 is a library reading program where children practice reading aloud one-on-one with a specially trained therapy dog and their volunteer handler. Each session lasts 15 minutes. Children can bring a book from home or borrow one from the library. Registration opens the 3rd Monday of the month for the following month, and children may register for 1 session per month. The event takes place at Morgan Hill Library and is designed for kids in kindergarten through 6th grade. This is a great opportunity for children to build confidence in reading in a relaxed, supportive environment with furry reading companions.

events.title: Pajama Storytime [Hora de Cuentos en Pijama]
events.description: Please join us at Gilroy Library for the Pajama Storytime where we read stories, sing songs, play games, and wear our pajamas for children of all ages.
events.event_detail: Pajama Storytime (Hora de Cuentos en Pijama) is a family storytime event held every Monday from 6:30 PM to 7:30 PM at Gilroy Library, where children of all ages are invited to wear their pajamas for...

events.title: Monday Evening Storytime
events.description: Monday evening storytime
events.event_detail: Monday Evening Storytime is a free family storytime event for children ages 2-5, held at Berkeley Public Library Central Branch on the 4th floor. The event features stories, songs, puppets, and more. Sessions run every Monday evening from 6:30 PM to 7:00 PM. Parents and children are encouraged to come in their pajamas. The library is located at 2090 Kittredge Street in Berkeley. This is a recurring weekly event, perfect for toddlers and preschoolers to enjoy interactive storytelling and musical activities in a welcoming library setting.

events.title: Cupcake Decorating Workshop Canyon Club Danville
events.event_detail: Hands-on cupcake decorating workshop at Canyon Club Brewing in Danville. Learn professional buttercream piping techniques in a small-group setting with Chef Amna. Event includes all supplies (cupcakes, frosting, tools), recipes and take-home instruction guide. Participants take home six decorated cupcakes. Takes place June 1, 2026 from 6:30-8:00pm. Ages 18+. Ticket required. Closed-toe shoes required; aprons recommended. Class includes dairy and eggs, no nuts used.

events.title: Gentle Yoga for All
events.description: A gentle moving meditation to restore balance to the body and mind. Join us Monday evenings to practice Yoga in a comfortable and friendly setting. We meet in person, upstairs, in the Oakview Room at the Walnut Creek Library.
events.event_detail: Gentle Yoga for All is a free community yoga class held at the Walnut Creek Library, upstairs in the Oakview Room. This gentle moving meditation event is designed to restore balance to the body and mind. Classes take place on Monday evenings from 6:30pm to 7:30pm, with the next session on June 1, 2026. No registration is required - simply drop in. All abilities and experience levels are welcome. Participants are encouraged to bring a yoga mat if they have one. The class provides a comfortable and friendly setting for everyone. This event is sponsored by the Walnut Creek Library Foundation.

events.title: After Hours Tabletop Gaming
events.description: Drop by and start off your week with board game night at the library! Meet your fellow gamers and learn a new table top, board, or party game.
events.event_detail: After Hours Tabletop Gaming is a weekly board game night event held at the Foster City library branch. The event runs from 6:30 PM to 7:30 PM and provides an opportunity for adults ages 18+ to drop by and enjoy tabletop, board, or party games with fellow gamers. No registration is required to attend. Attendees can meet new people, learn new games, and have a fun casual evening playing games at the library. The event is organized by San Mateo County Libraries and is suitable for adults looking for a social gaming activity.

events.title: Family Storytime
events.description: Family Storytime is a fun mix of songs, books, and stories, suited for 3-5 year-olds, but all are welcome. Children will develop language, literacy, and social skills alongside their families. No registration is required.
events.event_detail: Family Storytime is a fun mix of songs, books, and stories, suited for 3-5 year-olds, but all are welcome. Children will develop language, literacy, and social skills alongside their families. The event takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026, from 6:30pm to 7:00pm at the San Ramon branch of Contra Costa County Library located at 100 Montgomery Street, San Ramon, CA 94583. No registration is required. Accommodations are available with advance notice.

events.title: Inner Richmond Board Game Night
events.description: Weekly board game night in the Richmond
events.event_detail: Inner Richmond Board Game Night is a casual, low-pressure weekly gathering at The Plough & the Stars pub, held every Monday at 6:30pm. The event is free to attend and features a large library of 80+ easy-to-learn social board games, ranging from quick party games to longer classics. Attendees can show up solo or with friends, grab a drink from the bar, and jump into a game with the friendly group. No experience is needed, making it perfect for beginners and experienced gamers alike. The venue is located at 116 Clement Street in San Francisco's Inner Richmond neighborhood.

events.title: Reading Buddies for Grades K-6 (6:30pm session)
events.description: Practice your reading skills by reading aloud one on one with a furry friend! Each 15-minute session is with a specially trained therapy dog.
events.event_detail: Reading Buddies is a free library program where children in grades K-6 practice reading aloud one-on-one with a specially trained therapy dog and its volunteer handler. Each session lasts 15 minutes. The event takes place at Morgan Hill Library, typically in the evening at 6:30 PM. Children can bring a book from home or borrow one from the library to read to the friendly dog. Registration is required and opens the 3rd Monday of the month for the following month. Parents should register with their child's name and email. This is a great opportunity for kids to build confidence in reading in a relaxed, non-judgmental environment with furry companions. The program is suitable for grades K-8 and runs in English.

events.title: In-Person English Conversation Club
events.description: Improve your English and make new friends! Practice your speaking skills with fluent speakers and other English language learners in a small group.
events.event_detail: In-Person English Conversation Club hosted by San Mateo County Libraries at the Belmont branch. This event runs from 6:30 PM to 7:30 PM, likely on a recurring weekly basis (specific dates not shown). The club provides a welcoming environment for English language learners to practice speaking with fluent speakers and other learners in a small group setting. Open to all skill levels, this event is designed for adults ages 18 and over who want to improve their English conversation skills and make new friends. Capacity limits may apply, so attending on time is recommended.

events.title: Soft Pretzel Workshop, Canyon Club Brewing Danville June
events.event_detail: A 90-minute hands-on soft pretzel workshop held at Canyon Club Brewing in Danville on June 1, 2026 from 6:30pm to 8:00pm. Participants learn to shape and bake soft pretzels, including fun animal designs. The class covers dough preparation using the spent grain and sodium carbonate method (no lye). Each attendee gets hands-on experience shaping pretzels, takes home 4-6 hot pretzels plus extras to freeze, receives recipes for pretzels, cheese dip, and mustard, and keeps a dough cutter/bench scraper. This is a social, casual event suitable for groups, dates, or solo attendees. Ages 18+ only. Participants can eat on-site or take their pretzels home. Optional: buy extra frozen dough.

events.title: Reading Buddies for Grades K-6 (6:45pm session)
events.description: Practice your reading skills by reading aloud one on one with a furry friend! Each 15-minute session is with a specially trained therapy dog.
events.event_detail: Reading Buddies for Grades K-6 is a library reading program where children in grades K-6 practice reading aloud one-on-one with a specially trained therapy dog and their volunteer handler. Each session lasts 15 minutes. The event takes place at Morgan Hill Library. Registration opens the 3rd Monday of the month for the following month, and children may register for one session per month. Attendees can bring a book from home or borrow one from the library. The 6:45 PM session runs from 6:45 PM to 7:00 PM. This program helps young readers build confidence through reading in a relaxed, supportive environment with furry reading companions.

events.title: Art Talk - The Etruscans: From the Heart of Ancient Italy
events.description: Togas, temples, hydraulic engineering, winemaking, and even 'Roman' numerals, all widely credited to the Romans, were actually Etruscan innovations.
events.event_detail: Art Talk - The Etruscans: From the Heart of Ancient Italy is a lecture event held at San Mateo County Libraries. The event takes place from 7:00 PM to 8:00 PM. Attendees will learn about the Etruscans, an ancient civilization that thrived in Italy from around 900 to 100 BC. The talk covers how the Etruscans pioneered innovations like togas, temples, hydraulic engineering, winemaking, and Roman numerals that were later credited to the Romans. The lecture draws on the latest archaeological discoveries and cutting-edge scholarship, complementing the most comprehensive Etruscan exhibition in the United States. Attendees can expect to discover nearly 200 examples of bronze and terracotta sculpture, gold jewelry, ceramics, and architectural features. The event is suitable for adults (19+) and registration is required.

events.title: Mystery Monday Book Club
events.description: Join us for our monthly Mystery Monday Book Club at Saratoga Library. This month, we will be reading Rebecca by Daphne du Maurier.
events.event_detail: The Mystery Monday Book Club is a monthly book club meeting at Saratoga Library where adults gather on the first Monday of each month at 7:00 PM to discuss mystery novels. This month's selection is...

events.title: Campbell Book Club: Casualties of Truth
events.description: Join us for our monthly Campbell Book Club at Campbell Library. For Caribbean Heritage Month, we will be discussing Casualties of Truth by Lauren Francis-Sharma.
events.event_detail: Join the monthly Campbell Book Club at Campbell Library for a lively discussion of Casualties of Truth by Lauren Francis-Sharma. This meeting takes place on Monday, June 1st at 7:00 PM as part of Caribbean Heritage Month celebrations. The event runs from 7:00 PM to 8:00 PM and is held at Campbell Library. Attendees can expect a book discussion with fellow literature enthusiasts, with copies of the book available at the adult reference desk or by placing a hold through the library catalog. The club meets on the first Monday of each month. This event is suitable for adults and older adults, conducted in English. Contact Shannon Sullivan to join the email list for updates.

events.title: Monday Evening Chat
events.description: Come join our Monday Evening Chat group and practice spoken English. Our tutors are all native speakers. They are caring and devoted. You will also meet people from around the globe and make new friends.
events.event_detail: Monday Evening Chat is an English conversation practice group at the Fremont library branch of Alameda County Library. The event takes place every Monday from 7:00 PM to 8:00 PM. Participants practice spoken English with native speaker tutors who are caring and devoted. Attendees can expect to meet people from around the globe, make new friends, and improve their English speaking skills in a friendly, supportive environment. There is also a Tuesday afternoon chat session from 4:00 PM to 5:00 PM. The event is suitable for adults and seniors. Library staff may take photos or recordings at the event.

events.title: Ygnacio Valley Library Book Club
events.description: Join the Ygnacio Valley Library Book Group for lively, thoughtful book discussions! Share your thoughts and connect with fellow readers. Our club meets in person every 1st Monday of the month at the Ygnacio Valley Library.
events.event_detail: The Ygnacio Valley Library Book Club is a monthly in-person book discussion group held on the first Monday of each month from 7:00pm to 8:30pm at the Ygnacio Valley Library branch in Walnut Creek, CA. The club welcomes all teens and adults to join for lively, thoughtful discussions about selected books. Attendees share their thoughts and connect with fellow readers. The library provides book selection information each month, and members can obtain copies by checking with library staff. The club meets regularly throughout the year with upcoming selections including titles like CONNIE by Connie Chung (June 2026) and REMARKABLY BRIGHT CREATURES by Shelby Van Pelt (July 2026). No registration is required to attend these free discussions.

events.title: Point Reyes Book Club: What We Can Know
events.description: The Point Reyes Library Book Club will discuss What We Can Know by Ian McEwan on Monday, June 1 from 7 to 8 pm. This book club will meet online. Facilitator - Lorelei Sontag.
events.event_detail: Point Reyes Library Book Club meeting discussing the novel 'What We Can Know' by Ian McEwan. This is an online event meeting on Monday, June 1 from 7:00 PM to 8:00 PM. The book club is facilitated by Lorelei Sontag. Attendees can expect to participate in a group discussion about the novel, which tells the story of a mysterious poem read at a dinner party in 2014, and a lonely scholar in 2119 searching for the poem as much of England has been submerged by rising seas. Registration is required - contact Mattie Ivy Leeds at 415-663-8375 or mattie.ivyleeds@marincounty.gov for more information. This event is suitable for adults and conducted in English.

events.title: Monday Meditation & Mindfulness
events.description: Join us for a series of mindfulness and meditation classes. Come practice meditation for 20 minutes and ask questions for 10 minutes with instructor Manisha.
events.event_detail: Monday Meditation & Mindfulness is a recurring weekly library event held every Monday from 7:00 PM to 7:30 PM at Woodland Branch Library. The event is part of a series of mindfulness and meditation classes led by instructor Manisha. Attendees can expect to practice meditation for approximately 20 minutes, followed by a 10-minute Q&A session. This event is suitable for teens, adults, and older adults. Accessibility accommodations are available, including ASL interpretation if requested at least 7 days in advance through the library's accessibility form. The event is free and open to the public, focusing on providing an accessible, welcoming space for anyone interested in learning or practicing meditation techniques.

events.title: Oakland's Free Town Biz Comedy Night w/ HellaFunny
events.description: Free comedy night celebrating Oakland culture
events.event_detail: TownBiz Comedy Night in Oakland's Temescal neighborhood is a free comedy show hosted by HellaFunny at Mesa Maguey, an upscale agave bar and Oaxacan restaurant at 4031 Broadway. The 70+ minute showcase features 4-5 comedians with credits from Cobbs, Punchline, SF Sketchfest, Thrive City, and The Function, hosted by Bryant Hicks. Free admission with RSVP for the first 50 people. Takes place every Monday and Tuesday at 7pm. Food and drinks available for purchase—menu includes mezcal cocktails, mole, tacos, and other Oaxacan dishes around $20 and under. Perfect date-night spot for comedy lovers.

events.title: Poetry Open Mic
events.description: Come share poetry. Come hear poetry. You do not have to be a poet to attend! Presented by Poetry Los Altos.
events.event_detail: Poetry Open Mic is an arts and culture event at Los Altos Library where participants can share their own poetry or simply listen to others read their work. No prior poetry experience is required to attend. The event takes place from 7:00 PM to 8:00 PM in Pod D at the Los Altos Library. It is presented by Poetry Los Altos and is suitable for teens, adults, and older adults. ASL interpretation is available upon request with 7+ days notice.

events.title: Motown On Mondays DJ Night
events.description: Free before 8pm, $5 after
events.event_detail: Motown On Mondays is a weekly DJ night held every Monday at Madrone Art Bar in San Francisco's NoPa neighborhood. Doors open at 7 pm and the event runs until 2 am. Hosts DJ Gordo Cabeza and guest DJs spin original Motown songs, exclusive remixes, and related music for dancing. The venue is located at 500 Divisadero Street at Fell Street. Admission is FREE before 8 pm, then a $5 cover charge applies after that time. This is a 21+ event where attendees can dance the night away to classic Motown hits and funk soul classics.

events.title: Best Medicine Presents Haight Laughsbury Comedy Show
events.description: Free - Every Mon event at O'Reilly's Pub
events.event_detail: Haight Laughsbury Comedy Show is a free weekly comedy event held every Monday (except the 4th) at O'Reilly's Irish Pub in San Francisco's Haight-Ashbury neighborhood. Doors open at 7:15PM. The show features bold stand-up comedy and fresh storytelling from nationally touring comedians as well as Bay Area favorites, including performers who have appeared on Late Night, Comedy Central, Don't Tell Comedy, and SF Sketchfest. It's a 21+ event where you can expect unfiltered creative energy and the weird, funny spirit that the neighborhood has always been known for. Come solo, with friends, or on a date to shake off the start of the week and actually look forward to Monday.

events.title: Mirthquake: Monday Live Comedy in the Richmond
events.description: Monday comedy with $5 drinks
events.event_detail: Mirthquake is a free weekly live stand-up comedy show held every Monday at 8:00 pm at Abbey Tavern (4100 Geary Blvd) in San Francisco's Richmond District. The show features a rotating cast of top comedians from the Bay Area and beyond, including performers with credits on HBO, Netflix, Late Night, and major comedy clubs. The event is hosted by Ben Kolina, Andrew Holmgren, and Jesse Hett. Drink specials include $5 well drinks all night, $5 Micheladas, and $2.50 bottled beers from 7-9 pm. Admission is free with RSVP required to ensure a spot. This 21+ event offers a welcoming atmosphere and is a perfect way to kick off your week with non-stop laughter and good times with friends.
