events.title: Vinnies Bar & Grill - Open Mic Night!
events.description: Every Monday night! Open mic at Vinnie's Bar & Grill. Ultimate destination for relaxation, good food, and unbeatable entertainment. 2045 Mt. Diablo Street between Salvio Street and Pacheco Street in downtown Concord.
events.event_detail: Vinnies Bar & Grill Open Mic Night is a recurring weekly event held every Monday from 8:30 PM to 12:30 AM at Vinnies Bar & Grill located at 2045 Mt. Diablo Street in downtown Concord, CA. The venue is open daily from 11am to 2am and serves as a destination for relaxation, good food, and entertainment. Attendees can participate in open mic performances or enjoy watching local talent. The bar is easily accessible via BART at the Concord BART Station, with the venue being a short walk away. Free parking is available in the Salvio Street Garage. This is a free event open to the public where people can showcase their musical or performance talents, enjoy food and drinks, and socialize with the local community.

events.title: Call for Entries: Mill Valley Film Festival 49
events.description: Each year the festival welcomes more than 200 filmmakers, representing more than 50 countries
events.location: Christopher B. Smith Rafael Film Center
events.event_detail: Call for Entries for the Mill Valley Film Festival 49, presented by California Film Institute. This is a submission opportunity for filmmakers to have their work considered for the festival. Deadlines: Early Deadline April 20, Final Deadline May 11, Late Deadline June 1. Notification Date: September 1. Festival Dates: October 1-11. The festival takes place at Christopher B. Smith Rafael Film Center in San Rafael, CA. For nearly five decades, MVFF has been a place where filmmakers feel genuinely welcomed and films are embraced by thoughtful, curious audiences. As the oldest fall film festival in California, it offers a high-profile platform while keeping the atmosphere intimate, engaged, and filmmaker-first. Over 300 filmmakers and special guests from more than 50 countries attend annually, fostering conversations and connections. MVFF has long been recognized for launching films into the U.S. market and creating early momentum in the awards season conversation.

events.title: Spin the Wheel at Pearl Branch Library!
events.description: Stop by the Pearl Avenue Branch Library to spin the wheel and get some fun prizes!
events.event_detail: Spin the Wheel at Pearl Branch Library is a Summer Learning celebration event at the Pearl Avenue Branch Library where children and teens under 18 can spin a prize wheel to win fun rewards after reaching reading milestones. Participants earn one spin for every 8 hours of reading or 8 books read, with prizes including mini toy cars, pencils, stickers, and animal squishy toys. The event runs throughout the summer during regular library business hours, with a maximum of one spin per child per day and a limit of 8 prizes per participant. Attendees are encouraged to log their reading on Beanstack for automatic Grand Prize entries. This activity is sponsored by Friends of Pearl Avenue Branch and is part of San Jose Public Library's Summer Learning program.

events.title: Oil Painting Exhibit
events.description: Bing Weng's oil paintings will be on display at the Los Altos Library for the month of June. A reception open to the public will be held on June 6, 2-3:30pm in the Orchard Room.
events.event_detail: Bing Weng's oil paintings will be on display at the Los Altos Library throughout the month of June. A public reception will be held on June 6 from 2-3:30pm in the Orchard Room. Attendees can view the...

events.title: Take-and-Make Summer Reading Craft
events.description: Plant a Seed, and Grow with a at-home craft every week this Summer! One kit per patron, while supplies last. For children ages 3-9. Don't forget to mark off your Summer Reading Passport!
events.event_detail: Take-and-Make Summer Reading Craft event at the Lafayette Library in Contra Costa County. This is an all-day event on Monday, June 1, 2026. The craft features a "Plant a Seed, and Grow with" theme with a different at-home craft kit offered every week during summer. One kit per patron is available while supplies last, designed for children ages 3-9. The event takes place in the Children's Area of the Lafayette Library, located at 3491 Mt. Diablo Boulevard, open from 10:00am to 8:00pm. Participants can pick up their craft kit and also participate in the Summer Reading Passport program. The program is made possible by support from the Friends of the Lafayette Library and the Lafayette Library and Learning Center Foundation.

events.title: Summer Reading Challenge 2026 - Camp-Y-Bara
events.description: Annual Summer Reading Challenge begins June 1st! All ages can participate. Track reading from June 1 - July 31 on a gameboard. Prizes awarded for milestones. Free program.
events.event_detail: Solano County Library's annual Summer Reading Challenge runs from June 1 to July 31, 2026, with the theme "Camp-Y-Bara" (capybara summer camp). This free reading program welcomes participants of all ages—babies, kids, teens, and adults. To participate, sign up in-person at any Solano County Library branch or online. Readers track their progress on a gameboard, advancing one stone for every 20 minutes of reading. Pre-readers track activities completed. Visit the library to claim prizes each time you reach a badge. Major prizes are awarded at the halfway point and upon completing the challenge. Earn prizes for every 200 minutes of reading, with Sacramento River Cats tickets at the halfway point and a Camp-Y-Bara plushie and free book upon completion. Weekly raffle prizes include wine tastings, meals, ferry passes, baseball tickets, and grocery gift cards, donated by local Solano County businesses. Prizes must be picked up in person at a library branch.

events.title: Spice Up Your Life Kit / Kit de especias
events.description: Stop by Gilroy Library's upstairs Information Desk and ask for a Spice Up Your Life Kit! Nepal is the world's largest mustard seed producer. Mustard seeds are the small round seeds of various mustard plants, a member of the Brassica family.
events.event_detail: Pick up a free Spice Up Your Life Kit at Gilroy Library's upstairs Information Desk. This kit contains a sample of mustard seeds along with tasty recipes and book recommendations. Mustard seeds are small round seeds from various mustard plants, a member of the Brassicaceae family which includes cabbage, broccoli, and radishes. Nepal is the world's largest mustard seed producer. The kit is available all day during library hours while supplies last. Suitable for teens, adults, and older adults (ages 13+). No registration required—simply visit the Information Desk to request your kit.

events.title: Summer Concert Series
events.description: Outdoor summer concert series in downtown Napa.
events.event_detail: Summer Concert Series - A recurring outdoor music event held during the summer months in Napa. This community event features live musical performances in a public outdoor setting. Attendees can expect to enjoy various genres of music in a relaxed, family-friendly atmosphere. Typically held in the evening or on weekends during warmer months. Bring your own seating, food, and beverages for a comfortable experience. Check the city website for specific dates, times, and featured performers for each event in the series.

events.title: Teen Library Penpal Club
events.description: To celebrate National Penpal Day on June 1st, we are launching our Teen Library Penpal Club in collaboration with the Rodeo branch! Any teen or tween patron of the Danville Library can write and receive notes from teens in Rodeo.
events.event_detail: Teen Library Penpal Club is a writing and poetry event for teens and tweens celebrating National Penpal Day on June 1st, 2026. The club connects young patrons of the Danville Library with pen pals from the Rodeo branch across the county. Attendees can visit the front desk at the Danville Library to pick up a Penpal Starter Kit or fill out a penpal interest form to be matched with a pen pal. Shipping and supplies are provided by the library, making it easy for participants to join. This is a great opportunity for teens to make new friends, practice writing skills, and learn about correspondence in a fun, low-pressure environment. The event runs all day at the Danville Library, open from 10:00am to 8:00pm.

events.title: Onsite Marketplace at Point Reyes Farmstead Cheese (Open Monday - Saturday)
events.description: Onsite marketplace open Monday through Saturday.
events.event_detail: Onsite Marketplace at Point Reyes Farmstead Cheese Company offers a relaxed, self-guided cheese tasting experience set against the scenic backdrop of Tomales Bay in West Marin. Guests can reserve a table on the farm's patio and enjoy a curated cheeseboard featuring the creamery's award-winning cheeses. The marketplace is open Monday through Saturday, with sessions typically running from 11:00am to 4:00pm. Visitors can pick up their handcrafted cheeseboards and enjoy them at their own pace while taking in the views. Additional accompaniments like artisanal jams, crackers, and charcuterie are available for purchase. Each reservation includes a dedicated table for approximately one hour. Price starts at $45 per person, and advance reservations are recommended as space is limited. This is an ideal stop for a casual yet memorable food experience in the beautiful Marin County countryside.

events.title: Stewart Trail Guided Horseback Ride at Five Brooks Ranch
events.description: Stewart Trail guided horseback ride at Five Brooks Ranch.
events.event_detail: Stewart Trail Guided Horseback Ride at Five Brooks Ranch is a one-hour guided horseback riding experience through Point Reyes National Seashore near Olema, California. Scheduled for Monday, June 1, 2026, this easy-paced ride winds through shaded forest and open pasture, making it ideal for beginners, families, and those new to horseback riding. Participants are led by experienced wranglers who guide them through Marin's scenic landscapes. The ride costs $70 per person and reservations are required. Riders should arrive at Five Brooks Ranch located at 8001 Highway One in Olema. This outdoor activity offers a peaceful way to enjoy natural beauty while receiving guidance from professional horseback riding staff.

events.title: Martini Monday - 12 Classics Served All Day $7
events.description: 13 classic Martinis, including Gibson, Rob Roy, Negroni, Mandarin Cosmo, Orange Drop, Salted Caramel, and More!
events.event_detail: Martini Monday event at Smith's Landing Seafood Grill offering 13 classic martinis all priced at $7, served all day every Monday from June 1 through July 6, 2026. This waterfront restaurant is located at #1 Marina Plaza in Antioch at a beautiful marina setting where guests can watch large ships sail past while enjoying their drinks. The event features classic martini varieties including Gibson, Rob Roy, Negroni, Mandarin Cosmo, Orange Drop, and Salted Caramel among others. Attendees can also order from the full menu including appetizers, lunch, or dinner to accompany their beverages. The restaurant offers additional deals like Happy Hour pricing and Wine Wednesday specials.

events.title: SF Pirate Scavenger Hunt: Free Family Adventure
events.description: Free pirate scavenger hunt for families
events.event_detail: Free pirate-themed scavenger hunt for families in San Francisco's Mission District. Pick up a map at the Pirate Supply Store (826 Valencia St) or download it online. Solve five clues to be admitted to the Freebooter Secret Pirate Society. New recruits receive a mysterious reply by snail mail with a secret code. No screens needed - just imagination, mystery and mischief. The event is free and takes place all day on Monday, June 1, 2026. Perfect for adventurous kids looking for a fun summer activity. The scavenger hunt encourages exploration of the neighborhood while solving creative clues.

events.title: Read and Grow Seek & Find
events.description: Plant a Seed, Read! Fruits and veggies are growing all over the Children's Area. Find them all and complete the secret message to receive a prize. Pick up a game sheet at the front of the library or at the Study Center.
events.event_detail: Read and Grow Seek & Find is a children's library scavenger hunt game taking place throughout June 2026 at Clayton Community Library. Participants search for fruits and vegetables hidden throughout the Children's Area to find a secret message. When completed, children receive a prize. To play, visitors pick up a game sheet at the library's front desk or at the Study Area/Discovery Zone counter. One entry per month is allowed. This event is designed for children ages 3-9 years old and runs all day during library operating hours throughout the month. The program is sponsored by the Clayton Community Library Foundation.

events.title: Prize Puzzler for Teens
events.description: Try a new puzzle challenge each Tuesday in the Teen/Young Adult book area. Solve the puzzle to uncover a hidden four-digit code, then visit the Prize Puzzler box near the 3D printer by the Service Desk.
events.event_detail: Prize Puzzler for Teens is a monthly puzzle challenge event at the Clayton Branch of Contra Costa County Library. Running throughout June 2026, this program offers a new puzzle challenge each Tuesday in the Teen/Young Adult book area. Participants solve puzzles to uncover a hidden four-digit code, then visit the Prize Puzzler box near the 3D printer by the Service Desk to enter the code and win two fun prizes. Open to students in grades 9-12. Location: Clayton Branch, 6125 Clayton Road, Clayton, CA 94517.

events.title: Call for Entries — Art + Water: Artist Residency Opportunity
events.description: Art + Water is a free artist residency, exhibition space, and public programming hub opening in SF
events.event_detail: Art + Water is a free artist residency, exhibition space, and public programming hub opening at historic Pier 29 in San Francisco. The inaugural residency offers 30 working artists a fully supported, seven-month atelier-style residency with free studio space, alongside vibrant evening and public programming. Applications are open through June 1, 2026, with the pilot cohort beginning January 2027. The program is free and open to artists 21+ living in any of seven eligible Bay Area counties. This opportunity aims to support artists with real resources, not just encouragement, reversing the trend of artists leaving the Bay Area. To apply, artists should submit portfolios between February 27 and June 1, 2026, with in-person interviews in July and the first cohort announced August 1, 2026.

events.title: Fruits & Veggies Search-and-Find
events.description: Kick off Summer Reading at Lafayette Library! Find all the fruits and veggies hiding around the Children's Area. Complete the search-and-find and receive a prize!
events.event_detail: Fruits & Veggies Search-and-Find is a children's activity at the Lafayette Library running from June 1 to July 4, 2026. Part of the Summer Reading program, children ages 3-9 search the Children's Area to find all the hidden fruits and vegetables displayed around the library. Completing the search-and-find activity earns participants a prize. This is an all-day event with no specific time slot, allowing families to participate at their convenience during library hours.

events.title: Aloha Hour at Pacific Catch
events.description: Aloha Hour at Pacific Catch restaurant.
events.event_detail: Aloha Hour at Pacific Catch is a daily happy hour event at a seafood restaurant featuring tropical cocktails and fresh bites at discounted prices. The event runs weekdays 3pm-6pm and weekends 3pm-5pm at 133 Corte Madera Town Center in Corte Madera, CA. On Fridays, guests who wear Aloha shirts receive their first Mai Tai for $6. This is a casual dining experience where guests can unwind island-style with vacation vibes.

events.title: Storytime Programs
events.description: Early literacy classes and storytimes for children up to 6 years old. Includes Babytime (0-18 months), Baby-Toddler Storytime (0-36 months), Toddler Storytime (18-36 months), Preschool Storytime (3-6 years), Family Storytime, and Bilingual Storytime.
events.event_detail: Sonoma County Library offers early literacy storytime programs for children up to 6 years old. Programs include Babytime (0-18 months) with bouncing rhymes and songs, Baby-Toddler Storytime (0-36 months) with language-rich activities, Toddler Storytime (18-36 months) with movement and participation, Preschool Storytime (3-6 years) often ending with crafts, Family Storytime for multiple ages, and Bilingual Storytime in English and Spanish. Sessions typically last 20-30 minutes followed by playtime. Storytimes are held at various library branches throughout Sonoma County. Check the events calendar for specific schedules and locations near you. Can't attend in person? Recorded storytimes are available on the library's YouTube channel or via the Dial-a-Story service.

events.title: Angel Island Ferry Service
events.description: Ferry service to Angel Island for hiking, biking, and exploring historic sites.
events.event_detail: Angel Island Ferry Service provides roundtrip transportation from Tiburon to Angel Island in San Francisco Bay. Ferries depart Tiburon daily with varying schedules: Monday-Friday at 10am, 11am, and 1pm (plus 3pm for campers only). Weekend and holiday service adds departures at 2pm, 3pm, and 4pm. Return trips depart Angel Island 20 minutes after departure. Roundtrip fares are $18 for adults, $16 for seniors, $15 for children ages 6-12, and $6 for young children ages 3-5. Tickets can be purchased online. The ferry departs from 21 Main Street Tiburon, CA 94920. Once on Angel Island, visitors can enjoy hiking trails, camping, historic sites, and panoramic views of the San Francisco Bay skyline. The 5pm Saturday/Sunday departure is exclusively for campers.

events.title: Children's Summer Reading Events
events.description: Summer Reading events for children ages 0-5 and 5-12. Free cultural performances, educational workshops, and hands-on fun at libraries across the county.
events.event_detail: Children's Summer Reading Events at Sonoma County Library branches. These are summer reading programs designed for children (ages 6-12), typically running throughout June 2026. Programs encourage kids to read during summer break through activities, reading challenges, incentives, and fun educational programs. Events may include storytime, craft activities, reading games, author visits, and prize drawings. Held at various Sonoma County Library locations. Parents or caregivers should check specific branch schedules for exact times. Children earn rewards for reading books and can participate in special events and activities throughout the summer to prevent learning loss and maintain literacy skills during school break.

events.title: Marin Symphony Presents Masterworks 4: Hogarth Conducts Firebird at James Dunn Theatre
events.description: Marin Symphony Masterworks 4 featuring Firebird conducted by Hogarth.
events.event_detail: Marin Symphony Presents Masterworks 4: Hogarth Conducts Firebird at James Dunn Theatre. This classical music concert takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026 at 3:00pm at the College of Marin's James Dunn Theatre in Kentfield, California. The program features conductor Brad Hogarth and violinist Ani Bukujian performing works by Handel (Overture from Music for the Royal Fireworks), Prokofiev (Violin Concerto No.1), Ravel (Ma mère l'Oye Suite), and Stravinsky (Firebird Suite). This season finale performance showcases the Marin Symphony's fourth Music Director finalist in a program that spans centuries of classical repertoire. Ticket prices range from $40-$83 for single tickets with youth tickets available for $20. The concert offers attendees an evening of world-class orchestral music featuring exceptional solo performances in an intimate theater setting.

events.title: Summer Reading Challenge 2026
events.description: Plant a Seed, Read - All ages Summer Reading Challenge. Sign up online at sonomalibrary.beanstack.org or paper logs available at all libraries starting June 1. Earn prizes and discover new books.
events.event_detail: Summer Reading Challenge 2026 is an all-ages reading program running June 1 through August 1, 2026 at Sonoma County Library locations countywide. The theme 'Plant a Seed, Read' encourages participants to read daily and complete library activities to earn prizes. Children and teens (ages 0-18) aim for 20 minutes of daily reading, earning prizes at 1 hour and 15 hours of reading, plus entries into grand prize drawings for t-shirts, plush toys, earbuds, and phone stands. Adults (18+) complete mini-challenges of 4 activities each, earning enamel pins and prize books, with a chance to win one of five $200 grocery gift cards. Pre-registration opens May 1, and paper logs are available at all libraries starting June 1. Free events including cultural performances, educational workshops, and hands-on activities are scheduled at libraries throughout the county. Participants can track progress online via Beanstack or using paper logs.

events.title: Daily Tastings at the Marin French Cheese Shop
events.description: Daily tastings at Marin French Cheese Shop.
events.event_detail: Daily tastings at Marin French Cheese Shop, the country's oldest cheese company, located on a historic ranch in West Marin. Guests can enjoy complimentary cheese samples at the counter daily from 10am to 4pm. The event also features a cafe serving food and picnic supplies. Visitors can relax outdoors by a scenic pond surrounded by nature and wildlife. No reservations are required for individual tastings or single picnic table use. Group reservations can be arranged by contacting the shop. The tasting experience takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026 from 10:00am to 4:00pm at 7510 Pt. Reyes - Petaluma Rd, Petaluma, CA 94952.

events.title: Summer Learning Scavenger Hunt
events.description: Grr, grr, grizzly bears in the stacks, oh my! To celebrate SJPL's Summer Learning program, the staff at Biblioteca Latinoamericana invite you to visit and play our California grizzly-themed scavenger hunt.
events.event_detail: Summer Learning Scavenger Hunt at Biblioteca Latinoamericana branch of San Jose Public Library. This free, no-registration-required event invites participants of all ages to explore the library stacks while searching for California grizzly bear-themed decorated paper animals hidden throughout. The scavenger hunt runs all day and celebrates SJPL's Summer Learning program. Children may need assistance from family or friends. Find all the decorated paper pals to win a prize! Inquiries about other Summer Learning activities can be made to staff at the branch. The event is part of SJPL's games and family entertainment programming, suitable for young children, kids, pre-teens, and teens.

events.title: Bay Area Comics and Comix Exhibition
events.description: The California Room's exhibit Bay Area Comics and Comix presents the history of American comic books, highlighting the participation of the San Francisco Bay Area.
events.event_detail: The Bay Area Comics and Comix Exhibition is a California Room exhibit at King Library in San Jose that presents the history of American comic books, highlighting the San Francisco Bay Area's significant participation. The exhibit displays comic books and materials illustrating the journey from 1842's The Adventures of Obadiah Oldbuck to the arrival of modern comic books in the 1930s, the 1950s backlash against comics that resulted in comic book regulation, and the 1960s explosion of underground comics which were largely a Bay Area phenomenon that opened the door to the modern graphic novel and alternative comics. A kickoff event is scheduled for Saturday June 6th. The exhibit is suitable for adults, teens, and seniors. Parking is available at the SJPark Fourth Street Garage with the first 90 minutes free.

events.title: Celebrate Pride Month in Downtown San Rafael
events.description: Pride Month celebration in downtown San Rafael.
events.event_detail: Celebrate Pride Month in Downtown San Rafael with the 3rd Annual Pride Art Walk Puzzle, running throughout June 2026. This event is organized by the San Rafael Business Improvement District and celebrates Pride, art, and local history. Downtown storefronts will feature Pride-themed window displays, each hiding a secret word. Participants collect the hidden words using a map to reveal an inspiring quote from Harvey Milk, one of the first openly gay elected officials in the United States and LGBTQ+ civil rights icon. Once you complete the rainbow journey and solve the quote, turn in your map for a chance to win prizes including tickets to the California Film Institute's Pride Series and other giveaways from local businesses. The event is perfect for art enthusiasts, history buffs, and puzzle lovers. It's a colorful, educational, and fun way to support the local business community while celebrating Pride. Visit the event website for participating locations and more details.

events.title: Novato Pride Flag Ceremony & Celebration
events.description: Pride flag ceremony and celebration in Novato.
events.event_detail: The City of Novato invites the community to a Pride Month Flag Raising Ceremony on Monday, June 1, 2026 at 6:00pm. The event takes place on the steps of Novato City Hall, located at 901 Sherman Avenue in Novato. Attendees can expect a brief ceremony celebrating and recognizing Pride Month with honors for inclusion, diversity, and community. All are welcome to attend this free event that marks the beginning of Pride Month celebrations in the area.

events.title: It's a Bird! It's a Plane! It's a Pipe Cleaner Superhero!
events.description: Using pipe cleaners, straws, and a wood bead, children can make their own pipe cleaner superhero.
events.event_detail: It's a Bird! It's a Plane! It's a Pipe Cleaner Superhero! is a free craft event for kids ages 5-10 and pre-teens ages 10-12. Children can make their own pipe cleaner superhero using pipe cleaners, straws, and a wood bead provided in a grab & go kit. Pickup is at the Information Desk during the month of June while supplies last. One kit per child. No registration required. This event is part of SJPL's annual Graphic Novel Making Contest.

events.title: Catch a Movie at The Rafael
events.description: Movie screenings at The Rafael Theater.
events.event_detail: Catch a Movie at The Rafael is a film screening event held at The Christopher B. Smith Rafael Film Center in San Rafael, Marin County. The event takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026, with showtimes varying throughout the day. The Rafael is an elegant, state-of-the-art movie theater operated by the California Film Institute, featuring three modern auditoriums. Attendees can enjoy first-run independent films, foreign-language movies, documentaries, and special presentations by filmmakers and industry experts. The theater is known for its comfortable seating and sophisticated atmosphere, making it ideal for film enthusiasts looking to see quality cinema outside of mainstream commercial venues. For showtimes and current film listings, visitors can call the info-line or check the theater's website.

events.title: Finals Frenzy Study Hall
events.description: Get Ready for Finals at the Library! Need a quiet place to focus? Join us for Finals Frenzy! We are providing a dedicated study space to help you power through your exams. Perks: Free snacks, Free water, A quiet, structured study environment.
events.event_detail: Finals Frenzy Study Hall is a dedicated study session for teens (ages 13-18) offered by Contra Costa County Library to help students prepare for finals exams. The event provides a quiet, structured study environment where attendees can focus on their coursework. Free snacks and water are provided. The study hall runs on multiple dates throughout late May and early June 2026 (May 26-30 and June 2-4). The event takes place at Dougherty Station branch library, located at 17017 Bollinger Canyon Road in San Ramon. Participants can expect a distraction-free space ideal for concentrated studying, with all the essentials taken care of so they can focus on their exam preparation.

events.title: Taste of Napa
events.description: Taste of Napa event featuring local food and wine.
events.event_detail: Taste of Napa is a community food tasting event celebrating local cuisine and wineries in the Napa Valley region. The event showcases various local restaurants, wineries, and food vendors offering samples and tastings. Attendees can expect to explore diverse culinary offerings, sample wines from local vineyards, and experience the region's rich food and drink culture. The event typically takes place outdoors or in a designated venue space and provides an opportunity for residents and visitors to discover local flavors and support community businesses.

events.title: "Sick Day" Kayak Tours on Tomales Bay with Point Reyes Adventure Co.
events.description: Kayak tours on Tomales Bay with Point Reyes Adventure Co.
events.event_detail: "Sick Day" Kayak Tours on Tomales Bay with Point Reyes Adventure Co. are guided 3-hour midweek kayak tours on Tomales Bay in West Marin, designed to help visitors unplug and enjoy the quieter side of Marin without weekend crowds. The event takes place on Monday, June 1, 2026 at 10:00am. Tours include a coffee and tea bar with local pastries before launching. Different days feature various themes: Marshall Mondays include oyster and chowder tastings, Tuesday tours visit Hog Island Oyster Co., Wednesdays offer waterfront dining at Nick's Cove, Thursdays include mead tasting at Heidrun Meadery, and Fridays feature brunch or happy hour at Mable's Restaurant. The experience supports small West Marin businesses while providing a relaxed paddle through Tomales Bay. Tours are $135 per person. For reservations, call (415) 663-5577 or visit pointreyesadventureco.com.

events.title: Pride Flag Colors Search & Find
events.description: Celebrate Pride month with us! When Gilbert Baker created the first pride flag, each of the colors he chose had a deeper meaning. We've hidden 7 images, one for each color and their meaning, throughout Children's Wing.
events.event_detail: Celebrate Pride month with this fun library scavenger hunt! This children's activity runs throughout June 2026 at the Walnut Creek Library. When Gilbert Baker created the first pride flag, each color had a deeper meaning. The library has hidden 7 images throughout the Children's Wing, one for each color and its meaning. Children can pick up a game sheet at the library and check off each item as they find it. Once completed, bring the list to the information desk to receive a small prize. This program is designed for children ages 3-9 and is sponsored by the Walnut Creek Library Foundation.

events.title: Teen Summer Reading Events
events.description: Summer Reading events for teens grades 6-12. Includes reading challenges with prizes and grand prize drawings.
events.event_detail: Teen Summer Reading Events at Sonoma County Library branches during June 2026. This is a summer reading program designed specifically for teenagers (age 16+). The events occur monthly and are filtered by the teen age group and a specific program type (137). Participants can expect to engage in reading activities, potentially earn prizes or incentives for completing reading goals, and connect with other teen readers. These programs typically encourage teens to maintain reading habits over summer break. The events take place at various Sonoma County Library locations. Specific dates, times, and branch locations vary by individual event within this series.

events.title: Spin the Wheel At Cambrian
events.description: Spin to win! Children and teens ages 18 and under who are participating in Summer Learning can spin Cambrian Branch's prize wheel.
events.event_detail: Spin to win! This is a Summer Learning celebration event at Cambrian Branch Library where children and teens ages 18 and under who have completed the 8-hour or 8-book milestone can spin the prize wheel. Participants can win prizes like bubbles, pencils, stickers, animal keychains, and more. The event runs all day during library hours at the Cambrian Branch. Attendees should remember to log their reading in their Summer Learning account on Beanstack to become eligible for grand prize drawings. The event is sponsored by Friends of Cambrian Library and offers fun incentive rewards for completing reading goals during the summer break.

events.title: Propagation Swap Station
events.description: Trade propagation cuttings with community members at the San Ramon Library, located under our Seed Library. Grow your love of plants. We are currently only taking water propagated plants, no soil or potted plants to reduce pests.
events.event_detail: Propagation Swap Station is a community plant cutting exchange event held at the San Ramon Library, located in front of the Circulation Desk under the Seed Library. Running all day from June 1, 2026 through August 1, 2026, this event allows attendees to trade water-propagated plant cuttings with other community members. Participants can grow their love of plants by exchanging cuttings and learning about plant propagation. Only water-propagated plants are accepted—no soil or potted plants—to help reduce pests and plant diseases. The event is sponsored by the San Ramon Library Foundation and is part of the Summer Reading program. All ages are welcome to participate in this free community event.

items.name: clear reusable bag for transporting cuttings
small spray bottle for keeping cuttings moist

events.title: Adult Summer Reading Events
events.description: Summer Reading events for adults ages 18+. Complete library-related activities to earn prizes and entries for $200 grocery gift card grand prize drawings.
events.event_detail: Sonoma County Library's Adult Summer Reading Challenge 2026 runs from June 1 through August 1, 2026, with the theme 'Plant a Seed, Read.' This county-wide reading program invites adults to sign up, complete reading activities, earn prizes, and discover new books. Participants can access booklists, complete mini-challenges, and enjoy free events at various library branches throughout Sonoma County. The program encourages adults to nourish their minds through reading, just as a garden nourishes the body. Registration opens June 1, and participants can track their reading progress to unlock rewards and incentives.

events.title: Election - Vote Center
events.description: Fremont Main Library is an 11-day Vote Center for the June 2, 2026 election. Election Day voting hours: 7:00am to 8:00pm.
events.event_detail: Fremont Main Library Election - Vote Center for the June 2, 2026 election, operated by the Alameda County Registrar of Voters. The library's Meeting Room serves as an 11-day Vote Center for in-person voting. Early voting runs May 23 - June 1 from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Election Day (June 2) hours are 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM. Registered voters can cast their ballots in person without an appointment. Attendees can expect a streamlined voting process in a familiar library setting with accessibility accommodations. The event is suitable for adults and open to all eligible voters in the area.

events.title: Election - Vote Center
events.description: Newark Library is an 11-day Vote Center for the June 2 primary election. Election Day voting hours: 7:00am to 8:00pm.
events.event_detail: Newark Library is serving as an 11-day Vote Center for the June 2, 2026 primary election. The Alameda County Registrar of Voters will have in-person voting available in the library Meeting Room. Vote Center hours are May 23 through June 1, 2026 from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM, with extended hours on Election Day (June 2, 2026) from 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM. Voters can visit to cast their ballots in person for the primary election. This event is suitable for adults and is related to citizenship activities.

events.title: Election - Vote Center
events.description: Vote at your Library! Election Day: Tuesday, June 2, 7:00am to 8:00pm.
events.event_detail: Vote Center at Castro Valley Library. The library serves as a 4-Day Voter Accessible Location for the election. Early voting is available Saturday May 30 through Monday June 1 from 9:00am to 5:00pm. Election Day voting is on Tuesday June 2 from 7:00am to 8:00pm. Attendees can cast their vote in person or drop off their completed ballot in the secure official ballot box located to the left of the library entrance. For voter registration information, polling times at other locations, and complete election details, attendees should check the Alameda County Registrar of Voters website.

events.title: Explore Blake Garden
events.description: Explore Blake Garden - free admission, 9am-4pm
events.event_detail: Explore Blake Garden is a free public event at a 10.6-acre garden in Kensington featuring stunning hill views of the San Francisco Bay and Golden Gate Bridge. The garden showcases native plants and unique structures. Kids can enjoy the reflection pool, flower garden, and Create-with-Nature Zone. The garden is open to the public Tuesdays through Fridays from 9 AM to 4 PM. Free parking is available on-site. This recurring event is suitable for all ages including babies, toddlers, preschoolers, and grade schoolers. Attendees can explore the natural beauty, take photos of the views, and let children play in the designated nature areas.

events.title: Tutorial: Meet One-on-One with a Financial Counselor
events.description: One-on-one financial counseling sessions
events.event_detail: Tutorial: Meet One-on-One with a Financial Counselor at the San Francisco Public Library Main Branch. This free, confidential financial counseling session takes place on Tuesday, June 2, 2026 from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM in Study Room 439 at Main Library, 100 Larkin Street. Individual 30-45 minute sessions provide basic financial guidance for anyone living, working, or receiving services in San Francisco regardless of citizenship status. Coaches fluent in English, Spanish, and Mandarin (with additional translation services as needed) can help with credit scores, savings, opening bank accounts, public benefit assessments, income and expense management, debt management, and communication with loan servicers and debt collectors. Sessions available in-person (Main Library) or virtually Monday-Thursday; virtual-only on Fridays. Registration required through sfgov.org/ofe/counseling.

events.title: Preschool & Family Storytime
events.description: Tuesdays and Thursdays, 9:30-10:00am. Join us for stories, movement, songs and rhymes for children ages 0-5! Afterwards, children and their families can gather for Stay and Play in the Children's Room.
events.event_detail: Preschool & Family Storytime at the Civic Center branch of Marin County Free Library. This event takes place on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 9:30-10:00am. The session includes stories, movement, songs, and rhymes designed for children ages 0-5. After the storytime, children and their families can stay for Stay and Play in the Children's Room. This is a family-oriented early literacy event suitable for babies, toddlers, preschoolers, and their caregivers. Note: This event is currently canceled. The venue is located in San Rafael, Marin County.

items.name: Small stuffed animal or comfort toy

events.title: Legion of Honor Museum Free Day (First Tuesdays)
events.description: Free admission to general galleries
events.event_detail: The Legion of Honor Museum Free Day occurs on the first Tuesday of every month from 9:30 am to 5:15 pm at the Legion of Honor, located at 100 34th Avenue in San Francisco. Normally, general admission costs $20 for adults, but on first Tuesdays admission is free for the permanent collection galleries featuring 4,000 years of ancient and European art in an exquisite Beaux-Arts building with stunning views of the Golden Gate Bridge. Visitors can explore the museum's extensive collection of paintings, sculptures, and decorative arts. Special exhibitions require separate paid admission. Advanced timed tickets are recommended to secure your preferred entry time.

events.title: de Young Museum Free Day (First Tuesdays)
events.description: Free admission to general galleries
events.event_detail: The de Young Museum offers free admission to its permanent galleries on the first Tuesday of every month from 9:30 am to 5:15 pm. Located at 50 Hagiwara Tea Garden Drive in Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, the museum features art from the 17th through 20th centuries including works from the Americas, textile arts, and art of Africa and Oceania. Visitors can explore priceless collections and also access the free Hamon Observation Tower for 360-degree panoramic views of downtown San Francisco, the Bay, and Marin headlands, as well as the Barbro Osher Sculpture Garden with modern sculptures. Note that special exhibition fees still apply and timed tickets are required.

events.title: Family Storytime
events.description: Join us for stories, movement, songs and rhymes for children ages 0-5.
events.event_detail: Family Storytime is a library program for children ages 0-5 featuring stories, movement, songs, and rhymes. The event takes place at the Corte Madera branch of Marin County Free Library in Marin County. It runs from 9:30 AM to 10:00 AM, with recurring sessions typically scheduled weekly or on specific days (check the library events calendar for current schedule). Families can expect interactive storytelling, musical activities, and early literacy engagement suitable for babies, toddlers, and preschoolers. The program is conducted in English, free to attend, and accommodates families on a drop-in basis. Parents and caregivers should arrive a few minutes early to help children settle in before the session begins.

events.title: Bookmobile: Swing Into Stories at Garfield Square Playground
events.description: Bookmobile storytime at Garfield Square Playground
events.event_detail: Bookmobile: Swing Into Stories at Garfield Square Playground is a children's bookmobile service held at Garfield Square Playground in San Francisco. The event takes place on Tuesday, June 2, 2026, from 9:30 AM to 12:00 PM, with outdoor storytime scheduled from 10:30 to 11:00 AM. This program is designed for children ages 5 and younger and is a partnership between the San Francisco Public Library and San Francisco Recreation & Parks. Attendees can expect to browse books from the mobile library and participate in an outdoor storytime session. The event is drop-in with no registration required.

events.title: English Language Learners Group
events.description: Join us weekly at the REACH/Ashland Youth Center where you can chat with other adult English language learners to improve your English conversational skills, improve your employment possibilities, and MAKE NEW FRIENDS!
events.event_detail: English Language Learners Group is a weekly event held every Thursday from 9:30 AM to 10:30 AM at the REACH/Ashland Youth Center. This program, hosted by Alameda County Library, is designed for adult English language learners who want to improve their conversational English skills in a friendly, supportive environment. Attendees can expect to chat with fellow learners, practice speaking, enhance their employment opportunities through improved language abilities, and make new friends. The group provides an excellent opportunity for adults to practice English in a low-pressure setting. No registration is required to attend this free community event.

events.title: Family Storytime
events.description: Come along on an imaginary adventure. Hear new stories, sing songs, and learn wiggles that the whole family can enjoy together.
events.event_detail: Family Storytime is a library event designed for families to enjoy together, featuring an imaginary adventure through new stories, songs, and interactive wiggles suitable for all ages from toddlers to grown-ups. The event takes place at the Half Moon Bay branch of San Mateo County Libraries, running from 10:00 AM to 10:30 AM. Attendees can expect a fun, engaging storytime experience with music and performance elements that encourage family participation. The event is specifically recommended for preschoolers ages 0-5, children ages 6-11, and families looking for a free, entertaining activity. No registration is required, making it accessible for drop-in attendance.

events.title: Social: Job Seeker Meetup
events.description: Job seeker networking meetup
events.event_detail: Social: Job Seeker Meetup is an in-person peer support gathering for job seekers held at the Main Library in San Francisco. The event takes place on Tuesday, June 2, 2026, from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM in the Jobs and Career Center on the 4th floor. This relaxed, welcoming space allows attendees to talk openly about their job search experience, swap advice and leads, build a supportive community with others who understand the challenges, and connect with local organizations offering free job seeker resources. Career coach Kaitlyn Lynch will share practical job search tips. Whether you're between jobs, changing careers, or figuring out your next step, all job seekers are welcome. The event is drop-in with no registration required.

events.title: SF's Conservatory of Flowers Free First Tuesdays
events.description: Free admission on first Tuesday of month
events.location: Conservatory of Flowers, Golden Gate Park
events.event_detail: SF's Conservatory of Flowers offers free admission on the first Tuesday of every month at Golden Gate Park. The historic greenhouse, opened in 1879, is the oldest existing conservatory of its kind in the Western Hemisphere. Visitors can explore nearly 2,000 species of rare, exotic, and endangered plants from more than 50 countries. Hours are 10am-4:30pm (last entry at 4pm). Admission is normally $12 for non-SF residents, but free for everyone on free days. The venue also offers additional free or reduced admission through Museums for All for San Francisco residents on public benefits, plus free admission for Military, Veterans, and children 4 and under. A winter light show called Photosynthesis is also available free every night.

events.title: Free English Class | Clase de inglés gratuita
events.description: Learn English in this free in-person class taught by a certified instructor.
events.event_detail: Free English Class (Clase de inglés gratuita) at San Mateo County Libraries, held at the Half Moon Bay branch. Runs from 10:00 AM to 11:30 AM. This in-person class is taught by a certified instructor and is open to adults (19+). Participants will learn and practice English helpful for everyday life situations. The event is bilingual, with descriptions provided in both English and Spanish. No registration required. Bring a notebook and pen to take notes during the lesson.

events.title: Open Sewing
events.description: Join us for open time to use the library's sewing machines. Bring your own project or use some of our supplies to make your own.
events.event_detail: Open Sewing is a drop-in crafting event at the Half Moon Bay library branch where attendees can use the library's sewing machines during open studio time. The event runs from 10:00 AM to 2:00 PM. Participants can bring their own sewing project or use supplies available at the library. There is no formal instruction, but library staff will provide assistance with the machines if needed. This event is suitable for all ages including children (6-11), teens (12-18), and adults (19+). Available in English and Spanish.

events.title: Veterans Resource Tabling
events.description: Have you served in the military or know someone who has? Stop by the library to meet with the County Veterans Services Office.
events.event_detail: Veterans Resource Tabling is an event where veterans and their family members can meet with staff from the County Veterans Services Office. The event takes place from 10:00 AM to 2:00 PM at Pacifica Sharp Park library branch. Staff provide consultations, referrals, and information on general issues and VA benefits. Veterans can get help navigating the VA system and schedule appointments to file claims. No appointment is needed to attend this event. Suitable for adults (19+) and is 55+ friendly. The event focuses on community resources, life skills, social support, and is conducted in English.

events.title: Open Sewing
events.description: Join us for open time to use the library's sewing machines. Bring your project or use some of our supplies to make your own.
events.event_detail: Open Sewing is a free drop-in crafting event held at San Mateo County Libraries in Foster City. Participants can use the library's sewing machines during open studio time from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM. Attendees may bring their own sewing project or use available library supplies to create something new. No formal instruction is provided, but staff assistance with the machines is available as time permits. This event is suitable for children ages 6-11, teens, and adults. Children 7 and younger must be accompanied by a caregiver. No registration is required. It's a great opportunity for beginners to try sewing or for experienced sewists to work on personal projects in a supportive environment.

events.title: 教程: 基本科技協助 (中文和英文) / Tutorial: English and Chinese Tech Drop-In
events.description: Bilingual tech help in English and Chinese
events.event_detail: Tech drop-in tutorial providing one-on-one basic technology assistance in English, Cantonese, and Mandarin. In collaboration with Community Living Campaign, this event helps seniors and people with disabilities learn computer skills and how to use Apple and Android devices. Takes place Tuesday, June 2, 2026 from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM at the Main Library's Computer Training Center on the 5th floor. Each session is 20 minutes long. This is a drop-in program with no registration required. The event aims to bring greater joy, health, and connectedness to the community through technology education. Wheelchair accessible location at 100 Larkin Street, San Francisco.

events.title: Storytime: For Babies
events.description: Baby storytime at Merced
events.event_detail: Storytime: For Babies is a free library program for infants and their caregivers. The event features songs, rhymes, and reading of books in a group setting. It takes place on Tuesday, June 2, 2026 from 10:15 to 10:45 AM at the Merced branch patio (155 Winston Drive, San Francisco, CA 94132). This is a drop-in program with no registration required. Attendees can expect a short, engaging 30-minute session designed for babies, including interactive songs and stories. The program is sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library and is part of SFPL's storytime offerings.

events.title: Baby Bounce & Playtime
events.description: Bring your babies to the library for songs, books, and socializing! This event is best for parents or caregivers with babies from birth to 18 months.
events.event_detail: Baby Bounce & Playtime is a library storytime program designed for babies from birth to 18 months and their parents or caregivers. The event runs from 10:15 AM to 11:15 AM and takes place at the Golden Gate Branch of the Oakland Public Library. Attendees can expect to participate in songs, shared reading of books, and socializing opportunities with other parents and babies.
