events.event_detail: Jazz on the Silver Screen is a free multimedia concert celebrating the debut of Byer Square at the San Francisco Campus for Jewish Living. The event features New York City's Gabriel Schillinger-Hyman Quartet exploring jazz music that originated in film. The program spans a wide range of film styles and eras including silent films, early talkies, animation, noir, gothic horror, romance, musicals, Hollywood classics, independent and arthouse cinema, and avant-garde works. Special emphasis is placed on the contributions of Jewish composers, whose influence on 20th-century film and popular music is profound and lasting. The event takes place on Tuesday, June 2, 2026 at 5:00 PM at 302 Silver Avenue, San Francisco. Registration is required but admission is free. Attendees can expect an engaging performance that combines live jazz with visual media presentations.

events.title: Family Movie: DC League of Super-Pets
events.description: Join us for a family friendly movie. Bring a blanket to watch on the floor the movie DC League of Super-Pets. Krypto the Super-Dog and Superman are inseparable best friends, sharing the same superpowers and fighting crime side by side.
events.event_detail: Family movie showing of DC League of Super-Pets at the Dublin library branch. The event runs from 5:00 PM to 7:00 PM as part of the Summer Adventure program. Attendees are encouraged to bring a blanket to sit on the floor while watching the film. The movie follows Krypto the Super-Dog and Superman as they fight crime in Metropolis, with Krypto needing to master his own powers when Superman is kidnapped. This is a family-friendly event suitable for adults, teens, kids, and everyone. The library may take photos or recordings during the event. ASL interpreter or closed captioning available upon request with 7 days advance notice.

events.title: Workshop: Recording Studio Orientation
events.description: Recording studio orientation workshop
events.event_detail: Workshop: Recording Studio Orientation at The Mix, the music recording studio at San Francisco Public Library's Main Library. This free orientation takes place on Tuesday, June 2, 2026, from 5:00 to 6:00 PM in the Mix: Audio section on the 2nd floor. Participants will learn studio safety guidelines, behavior expectations, and usage policies. Teens will get hands-on experience with music software and hardware, learning to create their own songs and music. Topics covered include making beats and loops, using samples, editing audio files, and recording live vocals and instruments. After completing this orientation, teens gain the ability to reserve and access the recording studio independently for their creative projects. The program is drop-in with no registration required and is sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library.

events.title: South Beach Coastal Resilience Project Open House
events.description: Almost full - Community open house event
events.event_detail: South Beach Coastal Resilience Project Open House hosted by the Port of San Francisco. This community open house takes place on Tuesday, June 2 from 5:30 PM to 7:30 PM at the Ferry Building Grand Hall (Second Floor), San Francisco, CA 94105. Attendees will learn about the South Beach Coastal Resilience Project which aims to advance waterfront resilience along the Embarcadero between Harrison and Townsend Streets. The project addresses seismic risks in one of the oldest wharf areas and supports major developments at Pier 30/32 and Pier 38/40. The project will deliver earthquake-stable seawall and wharves while enhancing the public promenade for recreation and mobility. This is an opportunity for community members to learn about the project, view plans and displays, and provide their input. The event is free and family-friendly, lasting approximately 2 hours. Refreshments may be available.

events.title: First Tuesday ArtWalk
events.description: Art exhibits in Mill Valley, with receptions 5:30 - 7:30 pm
events.event_detail: First Tuesday ArtWalk is a free monthly art event presented by the Mill Valley Arts Commission where attendees take a stroll through town to view exciting exhibits featuring a wide range of art by local artists. The event occurs on the first Tuesday of every month from 5:30 pm to 7:30 pm. 2026 dates include 2/3, 3/3, 4/7, 5/5, 6/2, 7/7, 8/4, 9/1, 10/6, 11/3, and 12/1. Venues vary throughout Mill Valley - attendees should check the monthly ArtWalk guide for specific locations. Art receptions run during the event hours. The event is free admission and open to all. Visitors can expect to see local artist exhibitions, meet gallery representatives, and explore various venues throughout downtown Mill Valley.

events.title: South Beach Coastal Resilience Project Open House
events.description: Community open house about coastal resilience project
events.event_detail: Join the Port of San Francisco for a community open house about the South Beach Coastal Resilience Project. Learn about waterfront resilience along the Embarcadero between Harrison and Townsend Streets, an area facing seismic risks with some of the oldest wharves. The project will support developments at Pier 30/32 and Pier 38/40 while delivering earthquake-stable seawall and wharves and enhancing the public promenade for recreation and mobility. Attendees can expect to learn about project details, view displays, and provide their input on the plans. The event takes place on Tuesday, June 2 from 5:30 PM to 7:30 PM at the Ferry Building Grand Hall, Second Floor in San Francisco. The event is 2 hours and in person.

events.title: Reception — Everyday Sacred
events.description: Everyday Sacred at Mill Valley Chamber of Commerce Opening June 2, 5:30-7:30 at 85 Throckmorton
events.location: Mill Valley Chamber of Commerce & Visitor Center
events.event_detail: Opening Reception for Everyday Sacred, a solo show by contemporary realist artist Chris Adessa. The exhibition honors overlooked details of daily life through monochrome artwork, exploring the sacred in everyday moments. Free admission, open to the public. Takes place Tuesday, June 2, 2026, 5:30 pm - 7:30 pm at Mill Valley Chamber of Commerce & Visitor Center, 85 Throckmorton Avenue, Mill Valley. The artist works from Sausalito and her work has been shown in museums and galleries across the United States. The reception is part of the First Tuesday ArtWalk.

events.title: Film: The Rocky Horror Picture Show
events.description: Film screening of The Rocky Horror Picture Show
events.event_detail: Film screening of The Rocky Horror Picture Show as part of the Milk Memorial Movie Series. The movie is part campy musical, part horror film, following the adventures of a squeaky-clean couple stranded at a creepy castle. Rated R, 100 minutes, 1975, with closed captions in English. This is part of a seven-film LGBTQIA+ Pride film series running from June to August at the library. Takes place on Tuesday, June 2, 2026 from 5:30-7:30 PM at the Eureka Valley/Harvey Milk Memorial Branch, 1 Jose Sarria Court, San Francisco. Drop-in program, no registration required. All SFPL locations are wheelchair accessible. Sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library.

events.title: Beyond D&D: roleplaying game night
events.description: Tired of the same old mimics and gelatinous cubes? Join us to discover the games beyond D&D! Players can expect short campaigns featuring interesting TTRPG systems.
events.event_detail: Beyond D&D: roleplaying game night is a weekly library gaming event held at Oakland Public Library's Main Library from 5:30 PM to 7:30 PM. The event invites players tired of traditional D&D to discover alternative tabletop roleplaying game (TTRPG) systems. Players can expect short campaigns featuring innovative and interesting systems led by an experienced Dungeon Master. The event focuses on collaborative storytelling and problem solving, suitable for both beginners and seasoned players. All materials are provided by the library. Attendees should bring a positive mental attitude, be ready to meet new people, and arrive on time prepared to commit to the full session. Currently featuring 'Girl by Moonlight,' a magical girl TTRPG exploring themes of self-discovery and queer identity. Drop-ins are welcome but space may be limited. This session is intended for adults 18 and older. Mask wearing is appreciated.

events.title: Free Technology Help
events.description: Do you need help setting up your cell phone? Or have a question about your laptop? Free Tech Assistance is available. Sign up for a 30 minute session.
events.event_detail: Free Technology Help is a free library program offering one-on-one computer, tablet, phone, and device assistance to adults and seniors. Volunteers help with tasks like setting up cell phones, using laptops, and other technology questions. Sessions are 30 minutes long. To attend, call the Dimond Branch at 510-482-7844 to schedule an appointment. Walk-in help may be available on a first come, first served basis if appointments are not full. The event takes place on select evenings from 5:30 PM to 7:30 PM. No registration is required for walk-ins, but calling ahead is recommended to secure a time slot. Attendees should bring their device (phone, laptop, tablet) that needs assistance.

events.title: Tuesdays in the Plaza: Ariel Marin Band
events.description: Funk, Soul, Motown performance
events.event_detail: Tuesdays in the Plaza is a weekly summer concert series featuring free live music at Healdsburg Plaza. This specific event features Ariel Marin Band performing Funk, Soul, and Motown music. The event runs from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. on Tuesday, June 2, 2026. Food vendors offering locally sourced food begin at 5:00 p.m. The concert is held outdoors in the plaza. Ariel Marin is an eclectic inspirational singer from the Bay Area known for her angelic voice, drawing influences from folk, rock, R&B, gospel, classical, and pop styles. The event is free and open to all ages, making it a family-friendly community gathering.

events.title: Teen Volunteer Orientations
events.description: Help us at the library this summer. We need teen volunteers and we'd love to work with you. Make friends, serve your community, and work with youth.
events.event_detail: Teen Volunteer Orientations at the Oakland Public Library Rockridge Branch. This is an orientation session for teens interested in volunteering at the library during the summer. Attendees can expect to learn about volunteer opportunities, meet library staff, and sign up for volunteer positions. Multiple orientation sessions are available: Saturday 5/16/26 from 2-3pm, Tuesday 5/19/26 from 6-7pm, Tuesday 6/2/26 from 6-7pm, and Saturday 6/6/26 from 2-3pm. The event is suitable for teens and focuses on leadership development through community service. Teens will have the opportunity to make friends, serve their community, and work with other youth. No registration appears to be required based on the event page.

events.title: Pajama Storytime
events.description: Come get cozy and listen to some stories before bedtime! This storytime is designed for preschool and elementary school children, but the whole family is welcome.
events.event_detail: Pajama Storytime is a cozy evening storytime program at the library where children and families gather to listen to stories before bedtime. The event takes place from 6:00 PM to 6:30 PM at the San Lorenzo branch of Alameda County Library. This storytime is designed for preschool and elementary school children, though the whole family is welcome and younger siblings will still find fun. Attendees are encouraged to wear something cozy and bring a blanket and stuffed animal for added comfort. Parents are encouraged to participate alongside their children, and all children under age 8 must be accompanied by a parent. No registration is required. The program also offers ASL interpretation or closed captioning if requested at least three business days in advance.

events.title: The Black Studies Collective Community Reading and Discussion Series
events.description: The West Oakland Branch Library is excited to announce that the Black Studies Collective is back! This series invites community members to reflect on how the ideas and traditions of Black Studies continue to shape our communities.
events.event_detail: The Black Studies Collective Community Reading and Discussion Series is a four-part book discussion series hosted at the West Oakland Branch Library. The second cohort is reading 'The Black Antifascist Tradition: Fighting Back From Anti-Lynching to Abolition' by Jeanelle K. Hope and Bill Mullen. An orientation session takes place on Tuesday, June 2, 2026 from 6:00-7:15 PM. The monthly discussion meetings then continue on the first Tuesday of each month from July through October 2026, also from 6:00-7:15 PM. Participants can pick up reading materials at orientation, and a limited number of books are available for distribution. This small, discussion-based group encourages attendees to participate in at least 3 of the 4 sessions. Registration is required (in person or by phone). The series celebrates Black Studies as a living, community-centered tradition and continues West Oakland's legacy of collective learning and cultural engagement. Suitable for adults.

events.title: Tutorial: Basic Tech Help
events.description: Basic tech help tutorial
events.event_detail: Tutorial: Basic Tech Help is a free one-on-one tech assistance session with SFPL librarians held on Tuesday, June 2, 2026 from 6:00 to 6:30 PM at the Excelsior branch library (4400 Mission Street, San Francisco, CA 94112). The 30-minute sessions cover basic computer skills, email setup, Google Docs, Microsoft Office, and eResources. Help is available in English or Cantonese. Space is limited and reservations are required—call 415-355-2868 to book. Attendees can expect personalized guidance on technology topics tailored to their needs. This event is part of the Tech Time program series sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library.

events.title: Plot Twists & Page Turners: A Piedmont Branch Book Club
events.description: Do you need to talk to someone about your latest read? Are you in a reading slump? Come together with your fellow book lovers.
events.event_detail: Plot Twists & Page Turners is a monthly book club meeting at the Piedmont Avenue Branch of Oakland Public Library. Held every 1st Tuesday at 6:00 PM to 7:15 PM, this casual gathering is for adults who love reading and want to discuss their latest books, get recommendations, and connect with fellow book lovers. Facilitated by Angie McGowan, the event welcomes everyone whether you have a specific book to share or just want to hang out and chat about literature in general. No registration required.

events.title: Butter and Fresh Cheese with Honey Grace Lopez
events.description: Fresh cheese & butter class w/ Honey Grace Lopez: make cheeses, butter & whey flatbread
events.event_detail: Butter and Fresh Cheese with Honey Grace Lopez is a cooking class at Homeward Bound of Marin in Novato, CA. On Tuesday, June 2, 2026 from 6:00 pm to 8:30 pm, instructor Honey Grace Lopez (trained at Ireland's renowned Ballymaloe Cookery School) will guide participants in making a variety of fresh cheeses from a single base and creating rich, flavorful butter. Attendees will also observe a step-by-step demonstration for preparing whey flatbread. The class concludes with participants enjoying their fresh creations together. Admission is $75.

events.title: Beginning Drawing
events.description: Beginner drawing class: train your eye and draw from nature with confidence.
events.event_detail: Beginning Drawing is a beginner-friendly art class held at Mystic studio in Mill Valley, CA on Tuesday, June 2, 2026 from 6:00 pm to 8:00 pm. Discover the art of drawing what you truly see through close observation of nature. This two-hour class helps you build confidence and learn to see like an artist by training your eye to notice shapes, proportions, textures, and subtle details with greater accuracy. You will explore guided observational exercises using natural objects such as leaves, flowers, and rocks. The focus is on slowing down, practicing careful looking, and building drawing skills through repetition and experimentation in a relaxed, supportive environment. No prior experience required. Admission is $65 per person. Supplies not included - participants should bring a sketchbook or drawing paper (9x12 inches or larger), graphite pencils (HB and 2B), eraser, colored pencils, and something to draw found in nature.

events.title: Author Talk: Scandinavian Everyday with Nichole Accettola
events.description: Chef and IACP award-winning author Nichole Accettola presents contemporary Scandinavian cooking.
events.event_detail: Author talk event featuring chef and IACP award-winning author Nichole Accettola presenting her cookbook Scandinavian Everyday: Vibrant, Simple Meals from Northern Europe (Ten Speed Press). The event takes place on Tuesday, June 2, 2026, from 6:00 pm to 7:15 pm at Belvedere Tiburon Library in Tiburon, CA. Accettola, a CIA trained chef and owner of Kantine restaurant in San Francisco, presents contemporary Scandinavian cooking as it is truly lived: uncomplicated, practical, and deeply connected to daily life rhythms. The book draws inspiration from Danish, Norwegian, and Swedish cuisines, offering bright, pared-back recipes made with whole grains, vegetables, and thoughtfully sourced meat and fish, all adapted for American kitchens and grocery stores. Attendees can expect to learn about Scandinavian culinary traditions, practical cooking techniques, and how to incorporate Nordic-inspired meals into everyday cooking.

events.title: Free Author Talk: Even the Darkest Night Memoir
events.description: Author talk about memoir
events.event_detail: Free Author Talk featuring Christopher G. Choukalas, MD discussing his memoir "Even the Darkest Night" which explores the hidden struggles of fatherhood and challenges the silence surrounding men's mental health. The event takes place on Tuesday, June 2, 2026 at 6:00 pm at Book Passage bookstore in Corte Madera. Choukalas will be joined in conversation by Dominican University trustee Katy McGovern. Attendees can expect an engaging discussion about the book, fatherhood, identity, and healing. The event is free and open to the public. Books will likely be available for purchase and signing.

events.title: Cascada de Flores
events.description: Cascada de Flores combines music, dance, and story to create a dynamic, participatory, bilingual experience for the whole family.
events.event_detail: Cascada de Flores is a Spanish music, dance, and story experience for the whole family. This dynamic, participatory, bilingual event combines music, dance, and storytelling to engage children and adults alike. The program takes place at the Dimond Branch of the Oakland Public Library from 6:30 PM to 7:15 PM. Suitable for children from birth to 5 years old, toddlers, preschoolers, grade schoolers, tweens, and families. The event is part of the OPL Summer programming and is presented in both English and Español. Attendees can expect an interactive experience where participants may be encouraged to move, dance, and engage with the stories and music.

events.title: 2026 Summer Reading Program: Learning Chinese language and culture
events.description: Join us for an interactive program designed to help participants learn basic Chinese language skills and develop an appreciation for Chinese culture through fun and engaging activities. All materials will be provided.
events.event_detail: A free 4-week Chinese language and culture learning program for adults held at Campbell Library. The program runs June 2-27, 2026, with sessions twice per week: Tuesdays and Wednesdays from 6:30-8:30 PM, and Saturdays from 10:30 AM-12:30 PM. Participants must commit to attending all sessions. The program teaches basic Chinese language skills and Chinese culture appreciation through fun, interactive activities. All materials are provided. Classes are taught by Linda Chen, a Mandarin teacher at Branham High School with over 20 years of experience. This is a partnership between TECO (Education Division of the Taipei Economic Cultural Office) and Campbell Library. Registration is required, and space is limited.

events.title: One Village, One Book
events.description: Our book club meets monthly at the library to discuss books set in Oakland and the Bay Area or by Bay Area authors.
events.event_detail: One Village, One Book is a monthly book club hosted at the Montclair Branch of Oakland Public Library. The group meets on the first Tuesday of each month from 6:30-7:30 PM to discuss books set in Oakland and the Bay Area or written by Bay Area authors. The club selects books from a variety of genres and eras, alternating between fiction and non-fiction. The 2026 reading list includes titles like Sourdough by Robin Sloan, Family Style by Thien Pham, Deep Care by Angela Hume, Moonglow by Michael Chabon, Automatic Noodle by Annalee Newitz, Moneyball by Michael Lewis, and others. No pre-registration or commitment is required to attend. Attendees should have read at least some of the current book and be ready to discuss it. Participants can expect to meet neighbors, learn more about the city, and engage in thoughtful literary discussions with other book enthusiasts. The club welcomes new members to attend one discussion or many.

events.title: Mystery Book Club
events.description: Meet with your neighbors and fellow mystery lovers on the first Tuesday night of each month for a lively discussion of classic and current mysteries. Read this month's selection, drop in and join the fun!
events.event_detail: Mystery Book Club is a monthly book discussion group held at Alameda County Library. The club meets on the first Tuesday of each month from 6:30 PM to 8:00 PM. Attendees can meet with neighbors and fellow mystery lovers to engage in lively discussions of both classic and contemporary mystery novels. The June 2nd meeting will feature discussion of 'Listen for the Lie' by Amy Tintera, a thriller about Lucy Chase who returns to her Texas hometown to solve her best friend's murder. Participants should read the current month's selection beforehand and drop in to join the fun. The event is suitable for adults.

events.title: Ventriloquist! - Marc Griffiths
events.description: We are excited to welcome a ventriloquist for this year's Summer Reading Program. Experience ventriloquism with a cast of puppets.
events.event_detail: Ventriloquist! - Marc Griffiths is a family-friendly puppet show held at the Rockridge Branch of Oakland Public Library. The event runs from 6:30 PM to 7:15 PM as part of the Summer Reading Program. Attendees can expect an engaging, laugh-out-loud performance featuring a ventriloquist and his cast of puppets. The show is suitable for kids, grade schoolers, preschoolers, and families. No tickets or registration required - just show up to enjoy the entertainment.

events.title: Oakland's Mezcal & Mole Comedy Night
events.description: HellaFunny comedy show in Temescal
events.event_detail: Oakland's Mezcal & Mole Comedy Night is a weekly live comedy show hosted by HellaFunny at Mesa Maguey, an upscale agave bar and Oaxacan restaurant in the Temescal neighborhood. The event takes place every Monday and Tuesday at 7pm, featuring a 70+ minute show with 4-5 professional comedians who have credits from venues like Cobbs, Punchline, SF Sketchfest, and ABC/NBC. Admission is free with RSVP (first 50 people get in free), though food and drinks are available for purchase. The venue offers delicious Oaxacan dishes including mole, tacos, enchiladas, and ceviche, with most plates around $20. It's described as a perfect date-night spot with a welcoming dining room and bar atmosphere. The address is 4031 Broadway, Oakland, CA.

events.title: The Godmother of Silicon Valley: Film Screening and Q&A
events.description: Film screening with live Q&A
events.event_detail: The Godmother of Silicon Valley is a free documentary film screening and live Q&A event at the Computer History Museum in Mountain View, CA. The event takes place on Tuesday, June 2, 2026, from 7:00 pm to 8:15 pm. The 37-minute documentary short explores the life and influence of Esther Wojcicki, a trailblazing educator, journalist, and mother of tech leaders including Susan Wojcicki (YouTube/Google), Janet Wojcicki (UCSF), and Anne Wojcicki (23andMe). The film reveals how her radical teaching methods encouraged curiosity, independence, and resilience in students, with effects that rippled far beyond the classroom into global technology. After the screening, attendees can participate in a live Q&A featuring Esther Wojcicki and one of the filmmakers. Admission is free.

events.title: FREE: SF's Laugh GPT AI-Powered Comedy Night
events.description: AI-powered comedy night
events.event_detail: Laugh GPT is an AI-powered comedy show held every Tuesday at The Function, a black-owned comedy club in San Francisco's Mid Market/Hayes Valley area. Shows run from 7:30pm to 9:00pm, featuring 4-5 comedians who use AI assistance to craft and deliver jokes. The event was recently featured in the Washington Post. Attendees can expect a 70-90 minute show with comics who have performed at venues like Cobbs, Punchline, SF Sketchfest, Clusterfest, and Outside Lands. The show is free with RSVP (first 50 people get free tickets), though donations are appreciated and there is a two-drink minimum to support the bar. Arrive early to enjoy happy hour from 5-7pm before the show. The club features colorful murals, cozy seating, and an electric atmosphere where audiences help determine whether humans or AI are funnier.

events.title: $1 Margaritas & Disco Taco Tuesday at Underdogs (SoMa)
events.description: No admission charge
events.event_detail: Disco Taco Tuesday at Underdogs Cantina is a weekly nightlife event held every Tuesday from 7:30pm to 10:00pm at 128 King St. in San Francisco's SoMa neighborhood (across from the ballpark). The main draw is $1 margaritas available from 7:30pm to 8:00pm, with happy hour prices all night long. The venue features 25+ TVs for sports viewing, arcade games for entertainment, and a capacity of 300+ people. There's no cover charge for admission. Attendees can enjoy discounted drinks, tacos, and a lively bar atmosphere with disco-themed entertainment. It's a great option for affordable nightlife in SF, particularly during baseball season due to its proximity to the ballpark.

events.title: First Tuesdays Free Comedy Showcase & Happy Hour
events.description: Free comedy showcase with RSVP required
events.event_detail: First Tuesdays Free Comedy Showcase & Happy Hour is a free comedy event held on the first Tuesday of each month at The Layover, 1517 Franklin Street in Oakland. Shows run from 8pm to 10pm and feature professional comedians who have appeared on HBO, Showtime, Comedy Central, and late night TV. Happy hour drink specials are available until show time. Free admission with RSVP required. Hosted by Lyall Behrens, Francesca Fiorentini, and Josef Anolin, this monthly event offers a fun night out with top comedians and drink specials in a bar venue setting.

events.title: Vinnies Bar & Grill - Country Night!
events.description: Every Tuesday Night! Free lessons, free admission, country line dancing from 8pm til 11pm. Vinnie's Bar & Grill in downtown Concord, one block from Todos Santos Park.
events.event_detail: Country Night at Vinnies Bar & Grill is a free weekly line dancing event held every Tuesday from 8:00 PM to 11:00 PM. The event features free dance lessons and free admission, making it accessible for beginners and experienced dancers alike. Located at 2045 Mt. Diablo Street in downtown Concord, the venue is one block from Todos Santos Park. Attendees can take BART to the Concord BART station for easy access, or drive and park for free in the Salvio Street garage. Vinnies Bar & Grill offers food and drinks for purchase. Country line dancing is the main activity, with a welcoming atmosphere for dancers of all skill levels. The recurring event runs throughout the summer and fall months with dates listed through late November.

events.title: $6 Drive-In Movie Night in Concord & San Jose
events.description: $6 for adults on Tuesday nights. Kids are $2
events.event_detail: $6 Drive-In Movie Night at West Wind Drive-In theaters in Concord and San Jose. Every Tuesday night is "Family Fun Night" with discounted admission at $6 per adult and $2 for kids. Shows start at 8:30 pm. The Concord location is Solano Drive-In at 1611 Solano Way. The San Jose location is Capitol Drive-In at 3630 Hillcap Ave. Occasionally screens show double features, giving you two movies for the price of one. This is a socially-distant, old-fashioned outdoor movie experience where you watch from your car. Regular pricing is $9 for adults and $2 for kids ages 5-11, with kids 4 and under free.

events.title: Live Music with Todos Santos at Nick's Cove
events.description: Live music with Todos Santos at Nick's Cove.
events.event_detail: Live music event featuring Todos Santos at Nick's Cove waterfront restaurant. The event takes place on Tuesday, June 2, 2026, from 5:00pm to 8:00pm. This is a Local's Night event at Nick's Cove, a waterfront dining venue on Highway One in Marshall. Attendees can enjoy live acoustic music by the local band Todos Santos while dining at the restaurant. The venue offers food and drinks for purchase. Nick's Cove is a popular destination along the Tomales Bay shoreline, known for its scenic water views. Guests can expect a relaxed, casual evening atmosphere with local live entertainment.

events.title: Farmers Market at Strawberry Village (Every Tuesday)
events.description: Farmers market at Strawberry Village every Tuesday.
events.event_detail: Farmers Market at Strawberry Village is a weekly outdoor market held every Tuesday at the Strawberry Village shopping center in Corte Madera. The market runs from 10:00am to 2:30pm and features all-local and all-organic produce, baked goods, flowers, and artisan foods. Shoppers can browse and purchase fresh, locally-grown produce directly from farmers, discover unique handcrafted items, and enjoy a pleasant outdoor shopping experience. The event takes place along the frontage road between West Elm and Starbucks. This recurring weekly event provides an opportunity to support local farmers and enjoy fresh, sustainable foods in a community setting.

events.title: House Made Pasta Lunch at Il Davide
events.description: House made pasta lunch special at Il Davide.
events.event_detail: House Made Pasta Lunch at Il Davide is a dining event featuring a variety of delicious house made pastas at one of Marin County's leading Italian restaurants. The lunch takes place on Tuesday, June 2, 2026, from 11:30am to 4:00pm at Il Davide, located at 901 A Street in San Rafael, CA 94901. Founded in 1995, Il Davide has been serving the community for decades and continues to attract both loyal customers and new visitors. Guests can expect to enjoy freshly made pasta dishes in a welcoming restaurant setting. The restaurant is open for lunch Tuesday through Saturday from 11:30am to 4:00pm and dinner service Tuesday through Sunday from 4:00pm to 9:00pm. For menu details and reservations, guests are encouraged to visit the restaurant's website.

events.title: Prix-Fixe Dinner at Petite Left Bank
events.description: Prix-fixe dinner at Petite Left Bank.
events.event_detail: Prix-Fixe Dinner at Petite Left Bank is a three-course French dining experience held on Tuesday, June 2, 2026 from 4:00pm to 6:00pm. The prix fixe menu is priced at $39.95 per person and features classic French dishes expertly prepared for a delightful evening out. The dinner is available Tuesday through Friday, offering guests an elevated dining experience with a curated selection of traditional French cuisine. Located at 1696 Tiburon Blvd in Tiburon, California, Petite Left Bank provides an intimate setting for savoring French culinary traditions. Reservations can be made by calling (415) 910-1010 or through the restaurant's website. This is an ideal opportunity for those seeking an elegant yet affordable French dining experience.

events.title: 1:1 Tech Mentor Appointment
events.description: Free. By appointment only. Call for availability. Same day booking not always possible. Offered in English, Espanol, or Vietnamese. Would you like to find out more about computers? Learn at your own pace!
events.event_detail: 1:1 Tech Mentor Appointment is a free, one-on-one computer help session offered by San Jose Public Library at the Seven Trees branch. Appointments are available throughout the day on an ongoing basis (call for specific availability; same day booking not always possible). Participants receive personalized assistance learning at their own pace. Topics covered include introduction to computer basics, account or device setup, Microsoft Office fundamentals, job search and resume help, and email navigation and organization. The service is available in English, Spanish, and Vietnamese. To schedule an appointment, contact Seven Trees at (408) 808-3056 or email tiffany.lam@sjlibrary.org. This program is designed for adults and seniors looking to build digital literacy skills.

events.title: Summer Celebration Activity Bags
events.description: Summer brings exciting things to our libraries including the Summer Reading Program! Celebrate Summer with our Summer Celebration Activity Bags filled with fun activity sheets, a craft, and other cool surprises to kick off the season.
events.event_detail: Summer Celebration Activity Bags event at the Danville Library. Pick up free activity bags filled with fun activity sheets, a craft, and other surprises to celebrate summer and kick off the Summer Reading Program. Bags available beginning at 10 am on Tuesday, June 2, 2026. Two bags per family while supplies last. Event runs all day. Open from 10am-8pm. Sponsorship by The Friends of the Danville Library. Perfect for children ages 3-9 years and families looking for free summer activities.

items.name: Reusable bag for carrying supplies home

events.title: "The Art of Public Service" Art Exhibit at Marin Civic Center Gallery Thru September 24th
events.description: Art exhibit on public service running through September 24th.
events.event_detail: Explore "The Art of Public Service" at the Marin Civic Center's 3rd Floor Gallery in San Rafael. This exhibition showcases the personal stories and creative expression of Marin County employees through painting, collage, and collaborative storytelling. The artists reflect on how identity, resilience, and belonging shape their personal experiences and work in public service, exploring creativity's role in building community connection and shared purpose. The exhibit runs May 14 through September 24, 2026, open Monday through Friday from 9:00am to 6:00pm. Located at 3501 Civic Center Drive. Admission appears free; visitors can view the artwork, learn about public service through an artistic lens, and experience the personal narratives of county employees.

events.title: eBook Help: For Seniors
events.description: Do you need help downloading an ebook, or accessing digital content? Get hands-on help with borrowing and downloading FREE library eBooks and eAudiobooks to your Kindle, Nook, iPad or smartphone.
events.event_detail: eBook Help: For Seniors is a free hands-on assistance program at Vineland Branch Library where seniors can get help downloading and borrowing free library eBooks and eAudiobooks to their personal devices like Kindle, Nook, iPad, or smartphone. Library staff also help with other digital resources such as article databases and online tutorials. The program requires pre-registration by calling the Vineland Branch Library to book a 30-minute session. Only one session per person per day is available. This event is specifically designed for seniors ages 65+ and provides individual attention in a supportive learning environment.

events.title: Spin the Wheel at Pearl Branch Library
events.description: Stop by the Pearl Avenue Branch Library to spin the wheel and get some fun prizes! After each milestone (8 hours/8 books), children or teens under 18 can spin our prize wheel to win mini toy cars, pencils, stickers, animal keychains.
events.event_detail: Spin the Wheel at Pearl Branch Library is a summer learning incentive program for children and teens under 18. After reaching reading milestones (8 hours or 8 books), participants can visit the Pearl Avenue Branch Library during regular business hours to spin a prize wheel and win fun items like mini toy cars, pencils, stickers, and animal squishy toys. Participants can return to spin again after each new milestone until reaching 64 hours or 64 books. One spin per child/teen per day, with a maximum of 8 prizes per participant. Prizes available while supplies last. Part of the Summer Learning program sponsored by Friends of Pearl Avenue Branch.

events.title: Catch a Movie at CAFILM Sequoia Cinema
events.description: Movie screenings at CAFILM Sequoia Cinema.
events.event_detail: Catch a Movie at CAFILM Sequoia Cinema - a movie theater experience featuring first-run independent, foreign-language, and documentary films. This event takes place on Tuesday, June 2, 2026 at various times throughout the day. The Sequoia is owned and operated by CAFILM (California Film Institute), the same non-profit organization that operates the Smith Rafael Film Center and produces the annual Mill Valley Film Festival. Attendees can expect a diverse schedule of quality films with opportunities for entertaining and insightful conversations, including special guest appearances relevant to the programs. For specific showtimes and film selections, visitors should check the venue's website.

events.title: Downtown Novato Community Farmers' Market (Every Tuesday) Thru October 27th
events.description: Community farmers market every Tuesday through October 27th.
events.event_detail: The Downtown Novato Community Farmers' Market is an outdoor weekly market held every Tuesday in downtown Novato. The market runs annually from May through October, with hours from 4:00pm to 8:00pm in the summer months (May-September) and 4:00pm to 7:00pm in October. Located on Sherman Avenue between Grant Avenue and De Long Avenue, right in front of City Hall, the market features fresh produce from local farmers, prepared and packaged foods to enjoy on-site or take home, local artisan booths, and activities for kids. Hosted by Agricultural Community Events Farmers Markets and the City of Novato, this community event provides an opportunity to support local agriculture, discover handmade goods, and enjoy an evening outdoors with family and friends.

events.title: Japanese Tea Garden Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
events.description: Free from 9-10am on Monday, Wednesday and Friday
events.event_detail: Japanese Tea Garden's Free Admission Hour at Golden Gate Park in San Francisco. Free entry for everyone (including non-residents) from 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. San Francisco residents with valid ID get free admission all other times. The garden features classic Japanese elements including an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, koi ponds, zen garden, and native Japanese plants. Cherry blossom trees bloom in March and April. Regular non-resident admission is $12-16 depending on season. Located at 75 Hagiwara Tea Garden Dr, Golden Gate Park. Open daily starting at 9am with last entry 30 minutes before closing. Visitors can explore the serene garden paths, view koi ponds, take photos, and enjoy the tranquil atmosphere.

events.title: Storytime: For Families at Salesforce Park Rooftop Garden
events.event_detail: Storytime: For Families at Salesforce Park Rooftop Garden is a free weekly storytime event held every Wednesday at 10:00 AM at Salesforce Transit Center Park in San Francisco. Families with toddlers...

events.title: Services: Aging and Disability Resources with Canon Kip Senior Center
events.event_detail: Aging and Disability Resources informational session held at the Main Library Atrium, San Francisco Public Library. Wednesday, June 3, 2026, 10:00 AM - 12:00 PM. This drop-in event is designed for older adults and people with disabilities to learn about services provided by Aging and Disabilities Resource Centers (ADRC) and Canon Kip Senior Center. Canon Kip Senior Center, located at 705 Natoma St., serves adults 60+ and adults with disabilities 18+. Key services include information and referrals for caregiver support, case management, in-home care, financial planning, medical care, and housing assistance. Library staff and partners will be available to answer questions. No registration required. Wheelchair accessible. Sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library.

events.title: SF Zoo Free Admission Day (June 2026)
events.description: Free admission offer only valid to San Francisco residents with valid ID
events.event_detail: The San Francisco Zoo offers free admission for San Francisco residents on specific days, typically the first or second Wednesday of each month. On June 3, 2026, from 10am to 5pm (last entry at 4pm), SF residents with valid ID can enjoy Northern California's largest zoological park featuring 250 animal species in naturalistic settings. The zoo is located on Sloat Blvd. and The Great Highway near the Pacific Ocean. Attendees can explore various animal exhibits, watch keeper talks, and enjoy the outdoor park setting. Free admission is subject to capacity. Residents must bring valid photo ID or a utility bill with their name and address. Parking in the main lot is $13, but free street parking is available along Sloat Blvd.

events.title: Wee Play: Drop-In Playtime
events.description: Wee Play drop-in playtime, 10am-1pm
events.event_detail: Alameda's Wee Play is a drop-in playtime program for children 6 months to 3 years old, requiring caregiver supervision. Held at Room 120 in the Alameda Veterans Memorial Building at 2203 Central Avenue, the sessions run from 10:00 am to 1:00 pm on multiple days throughout the week (Mondays, Wednesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays). Each session features developmental and exploratory play activities that are minimally structured, allowing children to explore at their own pace. Daily themes include arts & crafts, STEM/numbers/reading, and creative play/dance/music. The program costs $6 per child (daily fee at the door). Registration is encouraged for the first visit. Children must be accompanied by a parent or caregiver at all times. Volunteers can earn free entrance by assisting with setup/cleanup.

events.title: Dialogue: Mandarin Bilingual Conversation Club
events.event_detail: Dialogue: Mandarin Bilingual Conversation Club is a drop-in language practice event hosted by San Francisco Public Library at the Main Library, Chinese Center Exhibit Space on the 3rd floor. The event takes place on Wednesday, June 3, 2026, from 10:00 to 11:00 AM, and meets on the first and third Wednesday of every month. Attendees can practice their Mandarin in a fun, relaxed setting through casual conversation. This is not a grammar class but focuses on real talk, friendly vibes, and learning through conversation. The program is part of the Weaving Stories: Asian American, Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander Heritage celebration. No registration is required—all are welcome to join and build confidence through conversation.

events.title: Wiggles and Wonder Storytime
events.description: Join Ms. Amanda every Wednesday morning for a wiggly, giggly, all-ages, multilingual storytime! We'll read books, sing songs, share imaginative play, and learn something new every day. Open to ages 0-5 and caregivers.
events.event_detail: Wiggles and Wonder Storytime is a weekly storytime program for young children (ages 0-5) and their caregivers, held at the Marin City branch of Marin County Free Library. The event takes place every Wednesday from 10:15 AM to 11:00 AM. Led by Ms. Amanda, the program features reading books, singing songs, imaginative play, and learning activities. This multilingual storytime welcomes all ages and families. Note: The program ends for the year on December 17 and returns February 25.

events.title: Baby & Me
events.description: Baby & Me storytime, 10:30am
events.event_detail: Baby & Me is a free lap-sit program for infants through 2 years old and their caregivers. The event features songs, nursery rhymes, knee-bounces, and movement activities designed to develop pre-literacy skills. It runs on Wednesday mornings from April 29 through June 3, 2026, from 10:30 am to 11:00 am. The class is held at the West End Branch of the Alameda Free Library located at 788 Santa Clara Avenue, Alameda, CA 94501. No registration is required. Attendees participate in interactive activities with their babies while building early literacy skills together.

events.title: Storytime on the Lawn
events.description: Storytime on the Lawn, 10:30am
events.event_detail: Storytime on the Lawn is a free outdoor storytime event hosted by the North Branch of the Berkeley Public Library. The event features stories, songs, rhymes, and fun activities for children ages 2-5, lasting approximately 30 minutes. It takes place weather permitting on the lawn at the North Branch library located at 1170 The Alameda in Berkeley. The event runs every Wednesday from April 8 through June 3, 2026, from 10:30 am to 11:00 am. Attendees are encouraged to bring a blanket or mat to sit on. After the storytime concludes, children can stay for playtime with toys, soft blocks, and musical instruments, providing an opportunity for social interaction with other caregivers. The event is free to attend, and more information is available by calling 510-981-6250.

events.title: Storytime: For Babies
events.event_detail: Storytime for Babies is a library program for infants and their caregivers featuring songs, rhymes, and books designed to promote early literacy. The event takes place on Wednesday, June 3, 2026 from 10:30 to 11:00 AM at the West Portal branch of the San Francisco Public Library, located at 190 Lenox Way. This is a drop-in program (no registration required) but space is limited. Caregivers can expect to participate in interactive early literacy activities with their babies, including singing, rhythmic activities, and shared reading. The program is conducted in English and is wheelchair accessible.

events.title: Storytime: For Families
events.event_detail: Storytime: For Families is a drop-in family reading event held at the San Francisco Public Library's Excelsior branch. The event takes place on Wednesday, June 3, 2026 from 10:30 AM to 11:00 AM in the Excelsior Meeting Room located at 4400 Mission Street in San Francisco. This program features books, songs, rhymes, and fun activities suitable for children of all ages. Families can enjoy a shared reading experience with stories, music, and interactive elements designed to build early literacy skills while engaging young listeners. The program is drop-in with no registration required and is sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library. Parents and caregivers can expect a welcoming, inclusive environment where children participate in age-appropriate activities. All SFPL locations are wheelchair accessible, and accommodations like ASL interpretation can be arranged by contacting the library at least 3 business days in advance.

events.title: Storytime: For Toddlers
events.event_detail: Storytime: For Toddlers is a children's program at San Francisco Public Library's Main Library location. The event takes place on Wednesday, June 3, 2026 from 10:30 to 11:00 AM in the Children's Storytelling Room on the 2nd floor. The program features books, songs, movement and other interactive activities designed for toddlers ages 16 months through 2 years, along with their caregivers. This is a drop-in program with no registration required. Attendees can expect a fun, educational experience with stories, music and early literacy activities in a welcoming library setting. The program is sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library.

events.title: Storytime: For Babies
events.event_detail: Storytime: For Babies is a free early literacy program designed for infants and their caregivers. The event features songs, rhymes, and books shared in a group setting. It takes place on Wednesday, June 3, 2026 from 11:00 AM to 11:30 AM at the Eureka Valley Children's Area in the Eureka Valley/Harvey Milk Memorial branch library, located at 1 Jose Sarria Court, San Francisco, CA 94114. This is a drop-in program with no registration required. Attendees can expect a 30-minute session of age-appropriate activities including songs, finger plays, and reading aloud. The program is wheelchair accessible and sponsored by the Friends of the San Francisco Public Library. Caregivers and babies can enjoy this bonding experience while developing early literacy skills together.

events.title: Storytime: For Preschoolers
events.event_detail: Storytime: For Preschoolers is a free library program for children ages 3-5 offered by the San Francisco Public Library. The event takes place on Wednesday, June 3, 2026 from 11:00 AM to 11:30 AM at the Chinatown Meeting Room, located at 1135 Powell Street in San Francisco (Chinatown/Him Mark Lai branch). Attendees can expect books, songs, fingerplays, and other interactive early literacy activities designed for preschoolers. This is a drop-in program with no registration required. All SFPL locations are wheelchair accessible.

events.title: Storytime: For Toddlers
events.event_detail: Storytime for Toddlers is a drop-in program at the San Francisco Public Library designed for children 16 months through age 2 and their caregivers. The event takes place on Wednesday, June 3, 2026 from 11:00 to 11:30 AM in the Visitacion Valley Meeting Room at the Visitacion Valley branch (201 Leland Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94134). Attendees can expect books, songs, movement activities, and free playtime following the structured storytime session. No registration is required, and the program is wheelchair accessible. Parents and caregivers should note that the session may be photographed for library promotional materials.

events.title: Presentation: Understand Your Industry with IBISWorld
events.event_detail: Presentation on using IBISWorld, a research database available through the San Francisco Public Library, to understand your industry and make informed business decisions. The event takes place on Wednesday, June 3, 2026, from 11:00 AM to 12:00 PM as a virtual event via Zoom. Attendees will learn how to request and navigate IBISWorld reports through the Library's Business, Science & Technology Center, covering topics like industry performance, market size, trends, competitive landscape, and customer segments. The session is designed for entrepreneurs and small business owners who want to ground their business planning and market research in real data, whether they are launching a new venture or growing an existing one. Registration is required to attend.

events.title: SF's GLBT History Museum: Free First Wednesday
events.description: Free tickets not available for reservation online on free days
events.event_detail: SF's GLBT History Museum offers free admission on the first Wednesday of every month from 11:00 am to 5:00 pm at the GLBT Historical Society Museum located at 4127 18th St. in San Francisco's Castro District. Normally admission is $10, but on these free days everyone is welcome thanks to a grant from the Bob Ross Foundation. Free tickets cannot be reserved online on free days; entry is first-come, first-served based on capacity. The museum is the first full-scale, stand-alone museum of its kind in the United States, celebrating 100 years of the city's queer history through dynamic exhibitions and programming. Children 12 and under also receive free admission.

events.title: Free Admission Day at Yerba Buena Center for the Arts (YBCA)
events.description: Free admission
events.event_detail: Free Admission Day at Yerba Buena Center for the Arts (YBCA) offers complimentary entry to the galleries every Wednesday from 11:00 am to 5:00 pm, as well as on second Sundays. YBCA is a contemporary arts center founded in 1993, serving as the cultural anchor of San Francisco's Yerba Buena Gardens neighborhood in SoMa. The venue focuses on contemporary art, performance, film, civic engagement, and public life, centering artists as essential to social and cultural movement. Visitors can explore rotating exhibitions featuring visual art, installations, and multimedia works in the galleries, with additional programming including performances in the theater (700 Howard St). The main gallery entrance is at 701 Mission Street, across from SFMOMA and near the Moscone Convention Center. YBCA also hosts film screenings, lectures, and community events throughout the year.

events.title: Storytime: For Toddlers
events.event_detail: Storytime: For Toddlers is a free drop-in program at the San Francisco Public Library's Richmond branch. The event takes place on Wednesday, June 3, 2026, from 11:00 AM to 11:30 AM at Richmond 10th Avenue Park (351 9th Avenue, San Francisco). This outdoor storytime features books, songs, movement, and activities designed for toddlers aged 16 months through 2 years old, along with their caregivers. Some blankets and chairs are provided by the library, but attendees may bring their own seating for added comfort. In case of extreme weather, the program will move indoors. No registration is required, and all SFPL locations are wheelchair accessible.

events.title: Hora del cuento de Música y Movimiento con Colores del Español/ Music & Movement Storytime with Colors of Spanish
events.description: Música y Movimiento con Colores del Español! ¡Únete con nosotros para un momento de música, movimiento e historias con Colors of Spanish! ¡La maestra Guadalupe cantará, bailará y sorprenderá a bebés, niños y niñas pequeños y cuidadoras.
events.event_detail: Music & Movement Storytime with Colors of Spanish is a bilingual storytime event for families with babies, toddlers, and preschoolers. Teacher Guadalupe leads participants in singing, dancing, and stories in both English and Spanish. The event runs from 11:15 AM to 12:15 PM on the first and third Wednesday of each month at the South Novato branch of Marin County Free Library. Children ages 0-5 years along with their caregivers are welcome to attend this free interactive program that combines early literacy development with music and movement activities.

events.title: Storytime: For Babies
events.event_detail: Storytime: For Babies is a free library program designed for infants and their caregivers. The event features songs, rhymes, and reading of books appropriate for babies. It takes place on Wednesday, June 3, 2026, from 11:30 AM to 12:00 PM at the West Portal branch Children's Area, located at 190 Lenox Way in San Francisco. Space for this program is limited, so attendees should arrive early. This is a drop-in program with no registration required. All San Francisco Public Library locations are wheelchair accessible, and accommodations like ASL can be requested by contacting the library at least 3 business days in advance. The program is conducted in English and sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library. Caregivers can expect a cozy, interactive experience where they and their babies can enjoy age-appropriate stories and musical activities together.

events.title: Storytime: For Babies
events.event_detail: Storytime: For Babies is a library event for infants and their caregivers featuring songs, rhymes, and books. The event takes place on Wednesday, June 3, 2026, from 12:00 PM to 12:30 PM at the Bernal Heights Meeting Room within the San Francisco Public Library system. Space is limited, and tickets are available on a first-come, first-served basis at the door starting at 12:00pm. Playtime follows the storytime session. This program is sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library and is a drop-in style event with no registration required. All SFPL locations are wheelchair accessible.

events.title: Tutorial: Computer Basics
events.event_detail: Tutorial: Computer Basics is a free drop-in class at the San Francisco Public Library (Main Library) held every Wednesday from 12:00 to 1:00 PM. The class takes place in the Computer Training Center on the 5th floor. Attendees will learn essential computer skills including how to use a mouse and keyboard, browse the internet and search, set up and use email, fill out online forms, create and save documents, stay safe online, and navigate the library's website for resources. This beginner-friendly class is perfect for anyone working on reading, typing, job search, or school goals. No prior experience is needed. On the last Wednesday of each month, participants can take the Northstar Digital Literacy test to earn a certificate. The class is wheelchair accessible, and accommodations like ASL are available upon request.

events.title: Workshop: Legacy Planning
events.event_detail: A free virtual workshop on legacy planning and retirement readiness hosted by San Francisco Public Library. The event takes place on Wednesday, June 3, 2026 from 12:00 PM to 1:00 PM via Zoom. Attendees will learn practical strategies to protect their assets, strengthen their financial plans, and make informed decisions for themselves and their loved ones. The session is suitable whether you are just beginning your planning journey or looking to refine your existing approach. This workshop is presented in partnership with the San Francisco Financial Empowerment Center, Housing and Economic Rights Advocates (HERA), and Advisers Give Back. Registration is required via Zoom. Topics include estate planning, credit improvement, savings strategies, and navigating debt. The related workshop on writing your own obituary is also recommended.

events.title: Social: Book Exchange
events.event_detail: Social: Book Exchange is a casual community meetup for book lovers happening Wednesday, June 3, 2026 from 1:00 to 2:00 PM at Golden Gate Valley Meeting Room (1801 Green Street, San Francisco). The event is held in partnership with NEXT Village SF and is designed for older adults and community members to connect. Attendees can expect light refreshments including a variety of teas, coffee, and snacks, plus a simple book-related ice breaker game. Participants are encouraged to bring one or two books from their personal collection that they have read and want to pass on to a new reader. Books are then exchanged among attendees. This is a drop-in event with no registration required. All SFPL locations are wheelchair accessible.

events.title: Marc Griffiths Ventriloquist
events.description: Enjoy a fun magic show with ventriloquist Marc Griffiths. Get ready to laugh out loud at this family event!
events.event_detail: Marc Griffiths Ventriloquist is an indoor library event featuring professional ventriloquist and magician Marc Griffiths. The event takes place from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM at the Castro Valley branch of Alameda County Library as part of the Summer Adventure program. Attendees can meet the ventriloquist, enjoy magic entertainment, and be amazed by his ventriloquist skills while laughing along. The event is suitable for everyone and conducted in English. Library staff may take photos, videos, or audio recordings during the event.

events.title: Activity: Tai Chi for Beginners
events.event_detail: Tai Chi for Beginners is a free drop-in exercise and meditation class offered by the San Francisco Public Library. The event takes place on Wednesday, June 3, 2026 from 1:00 to 2:00 PM at the Western Addition branch back courtyard (1550 Scott Street, San Francisco). Taught by skilled instructor Richard Fong, this gentle, slow-moving practice is suitable for beginners. Tai Chi may help improve overall health, fitness, balance, flexibility, coordination, posture, and mental well-being. In 2020, Tai Chi was inscribed on UNESCO's List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. The class is wheelchair accessible, no registration is required, and all SFPL locations are accessible. Attendees should wear comfortable, loose-fitting clothing suitable for gentle movement.

events.title: Services: Asian Pacific American Community Center Office Hours
events.event_detail: Asian Pacific American Community Center (APACC) office hours at the Visitacion Valley Branch Library. This free drop-in service provides letter translation, application assistance, and other language needs. Help is available in English, Chinese (Cantonese and Mandarin), and Spanish. The event takes place on Wednesday, June 3, 2026 from 1:00 PM to 3:00 PM at Visitacion Valley Branch Library, 201 Leland Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94134. No registration required. The library is wheelchair accessible and all are welcome to attend.

events.title: Services: Employment for People with Disabilities
events.event_detail: This event provides employment services and information for people with disabilities. Held at the Main Library atrium on Wednesday, June 3, 2026 from 1:00 to 3:30 PM. Attendees can learn about services from Behavioral Health Services Vocational Programs, which offer job training and placement for people with mental health diagnoses. The event is free and open to eligible people with disabilities. No registration required. Wheelchair accessible. For accommodations like ASL, call 415-557-4557 or email accessibility@sfpl.org at least 3 business days in advance. Sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library.

events.title: Tutorial: Basic Tech Help
events.event_detail: Tutorial: Basic Tech Help is a free one-on-one technology assistance session at the San Francisco Public Library's Excelsior branch. Held on Wednesday, June 3, 2026 from 1:00 to 1:30 PM, this 30-minute session provides personalized help with basic computer skills, email setup, Google Docs, Microsoft Office, and eResources. A librarian will guide attendees through these topics in English. Space is limited and reservations are required—call 415-355-2868 to book your spot. This event is part of the Tech Time program series sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library. Attendees can expect hands-on assistance tailored to their skill level, making it ideal for beginners looking to build confidence with everyday technology.

events.title: Activity: Tai-Chi
events.event_detail: Activity: Tai-Chi is a drop-in wellness event at the San Francisco Public Library's Anza branch. The class takes place on Wednesday, June 3, 2026 from 1:30 to 3:00 PM in the Anza Meeting Room (550 37th Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94121). Guided by instructors Laura and Gary Smoot, participants learn and practice beginning Tai Chi using the Yang Style Long form, consisting of slow, circular, soft flowing movements designed to boost strength, balance, and circulation. The session is divided into two parts: a beginners class from 1:30 to 2:15 PM, and an intermediate class from 2:20 to 3:00 PM. This Health & Wellness program sponsored by the Friends of the San Francisco Public Library requires no registration and is wheelchair accessible.

events.title: Tutorial: Tech Savvy at 60+ (Cantonese)
events.event_detail: A free computer tutorial class teaching seniors (60+) how to use smartphones and tablets, conducted entirely in Cantonese. The event takes place on Wednesday, June 3, 2026, from 2:00 to 3:30 PM at the Richmond Meeting Room of the San Francisco Public Library (351 9th Avenue, San Francisco). The class covers essential topics including WiFi connectivity, basic internet skills, common icons and functions, installing and deleting apps, WeChat messaging, camera and photo usage, and SMS functions. Participants must bring their own Apple or Android devices. The instructor teaches fluently in Cantonese, and the class is provided by Self-Help for the Elderly (安老自助處). Seats are limited, and advance reservation is required by calling (415) 355-5600. This is part of the Tech Time program series designed to help seniors navigate the digital world.

events.title: Storytime: For Families
events.event_detail: Storytime: For Families is a drop-in program at San Francisco Public Library's Merced branch, held on the Merced Patio. The event takes place on Wednesday, June 3, 2026 from 2:00 to 2:30 PM. Families can expect books, songs, rhymes, and fun activities suitable for children of all ages. No registration is required. The program is wheelchair accessible, and accommodations like ASL can be arranged by contacting the library in advance. This free event is sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library.

events.title: Tutorial: Book a Librarian
events.event_detail: Tutorial: Book a Librarian is a one-on-one tech help session at the San Francisco Public Library Parkside branch. Scheduled for Wednesday, June 3, 2026 from 2:00 to 2:45 PM, attendees receive personalized assistance from a librarian learning basics like email, internet searching, and borrowing eBooks. Participants can use library computers or bring their own laptop, smartphone, or tablet. Space is limited and reservations are required (sign up at the Information Desk or call 415-355-5770). This is part of the Tech Time program series designed to help people explore current technology and navigate the digital world.

events.title: Kids Craft Hour
events.description: Kids Craft Hour, 2pm
events.event_detail: Kids Craft Hour is a free weekly craft event held at Albany Library where children can get creative and make a new project every week. The event takes place on Wednesdays from 2:00 PM to 3:00 PM, running from March through June 2026. Children under 8 years old must be accompanied by an adult. Library staff may take photos or videos at the event. Participants can expect to engage in hands-on crafting activities with provided materials. The program is held in the meeting room at Albany Library, located at 1247 Marin Avenue in Albany, California. No registration is required to attend this free event.

events.title: Workshop: Write Your Own Obituary
events.event_detail: Workshop: Write Your Own Obituary - A free virtual event hosted by San Francisco Public Library's Magazines and Newspapers Center on Wednesday, June 3, 2026 from 2:00 to 3:00 PM. Participants will learn the basics of obituary informational content and style from expert librarians who handle dozens of obituary requests monthly. The workshop covers how obituaries (also called death notices, funeral announcements, or life tributes) traditionally work, including their purpose in communicating a person's birth, life, and death details, listing close relatives, and sharing biographical impact. Obituaries require a fee for publication whether in newspapers, memorial websites, or through mortuary services. The session emphasizes the importance of including obituaries in legacy planning as they serve both contemporary mourners and future genealogists. Registration is required via Zoom. A related Legacy Planning Workshop precedes this event.

events.title: Fish Feeding Viewing
events.description: Fish Feeding Viewing, 3pm-3:30pm
events.event_detail: Fish Feeding Viewing is a free family-friendly event at Crab Cove Visitor Center in Alameda where attendees can learn about Bay creatures and observe crabs, flounder, perch, pipefish and more during feeding time. The experience is described as "like a dive in the Bay without getting wet." The event runs approximately 30 minutes and is a drop-in activity with no registration required. Multiple dates are available in May and June 2026, with sessions typically starting at 3:00 pm. The event is suitable for toddlers, preschoolers, grade schoolers, and families. Contact: East Bay Regional Park District at (510) 544-3187.

events.title: Activity: DIY Candy Lei
events.event_detail: DIY Candy Lei is a craft program at San Francisco Public Library's Sunset branch. Held on Wednesday, June 3, 2026 from 3:00 to 4:00 PM in the Sunset Program Room, participants ages 8-18 create sweet candy leis perfect for gifting at graduations. All materials are provided by the library. This drop-in program requires no registration and is part of the Make + Do craft series sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library.

items.name: Small bag for carrying finished lei

events.title: Workshop: Career Coaching
events.event_detail: Workshop: Career Coaching at the San Francisco Public Library (Main Branch). Scheduled for Wednesday, June 3, 2026, from 3:00-5:00 PM. This in-person workshop offers free half-hour career coaching sessions by appointment with a career coach to help with job searches or career changes. Coaching covers self-inquiry, self-assessment, encouragement, guidance on best practices, structure, and homework to stay on track. Library staff also provide information about free library and local resources for practical skill-building. Appointments can be made up to 15 days in advance. Participants are limited to 2 appointments per person. IMPORTANT: Attendees must bring a copy of their resume. Participants who miss appointments without notice may lose the ability to book future sessions. Location: Sycip Family Conference Room, 4th Floor, Main Library at 100 Larkin Street, San Francisco, CA 94102. In partnership with the Friends of the San Francisco Public Library.

events.title: Workshop: Mandarin for Beginners
events.event_detail: Workshop: Mandarin for Beginners at San Francisco Public Library's Main Library, Chinese Center Exhibit Space - 3rd Floor. A partnership with Taipei Economic and Cultural Office in San Francisco. This beginner-friendly class explores basic vocabulary, everyday phrases, simple conversations, and Chinese culture through interactive activities. Held on Wednesdays starting 6/3/2026 from 3:00 - 5:00 PM. Eight sessions total: 6/3, 6/10, 6/17, 6/24, 7/1, 7/8, 7/15, 7/22. Space limited, reservation required: (415) 557-4430 or register online. Provided by Taipei Economic and Cultural Office Education Division, St. Anne Chinese School, and Chinese Center of SFPL. Program is part of Summer Stride reading program. Conducted in English.

events.title: Workshop: Rainbow Breakfast Bowls with The Breakfast Project
events.event_detail: Workshop: Rainbow Breakfast Bowls with The Breakfast Project at San Francisco Public Library Park Branch. Celebrates Pride season with a hands-on cooking workshop where children and their caregivers make nutritious rainbow chia porridge breakfast bowls. Takes place Wednesday, June 3, 2026 from 3:00-4:00 PM in the Park Meeting Room (1833 Page Street, San Francisco). Space is limited and reservations are required by calling 415-355-5656 or emailing parevent@sfpl.org starting May 3. This is a family-friendly food program sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library as part of the Summer Stride reading program. Participants will learn to prepare a healthy, colorful breakfast dish while celebrating diversity and community.

events.title: Workshop: Healthier Living Chronic Disease Self-Management
events.event_detail: Healthier Living Chronic Disease Self-Management workshop presented by OnLok in partnership with San Francisco Department of Disability and Aging Services. This is a six-week workshop for older adults (60+) where participants learn to better manage chronic health conditions through symptom management skills and activities. Classes run from 5/13/26-6/17/26. The specific session takes place on Wednesday, June 3, 2026, from 3:00 PM to 5:00 PM at Glen Park Meeting Room, located at 2825 Diamond Street, San Francisco, CA 94131. This is a drop-in program with no registration required. Participants can expect to learn practical skills for managing chronic diseases, connecting with peers, and improving their overall wellness.

events.title: Tutorial: Basic Tech Help
events.event_detail: Tutorial: Basic Tech Help is a free library program offering one-on-one tech assistance with SFPL librarians. The event takes place on Wednesday, June 3, 2026 from 3:00 to 3:30 PM at the Excelsior branch library located at 4400 Mission Street in San Francisco. Sessions cover basic computer skills, email setup, Google Docs, Microsoft Office, and eResources. Each session is 30 minutes long and conducted in English. Space is limited and reservations are required by calling 415-355-2868. This is part of the Tech Time program series designed to help community members explore current technology and navigate the digital world. Participants can expect personalized help from librarians in a quiet library setting.

events.title: LEGO Club! For ages 5-12
events.description: Join us first and third Wednesdays for LEGO Club! Kids ages 5-12 are invited to explore, build, create, and have fun.
events.event_detail: LEGO Club is a free library program for kids ages 5-12 held on the first and third Wednesdays from 3:30 PM to 4:30 PM at the Corte Madera branch of the Marin County Free Library. Children are invited to explore, build, create, and have fun with LEGO bricks. This is a crafts and making event where kids can use their imagination to construct various creations. No registration is required, and all materials are provided by the library. Parents or guardians should accompany younger children as needed.

events.title: Social: Gaming Hour
events.event_detail: Social: Gaming Hour is a drop-in gaming event at the San Francisco Public Library where participants can test their skills on Nintendo Switch and a variety of board games to see if they'll be victorious. The event takes place on Wednesday, June 3, 2026 from 3:30 to 4:30 PM at the Excelsior Meeting Room (located at the Excelsior branch, 4400 Mission Street, San Francisco, CA 94112). This program is designed for ages 8 and older and is sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library. Attendees can enjoy competitive and casual gaming in a social setting with others in the community. No registration is required.

events.title: Workshop: DIY Boondoggle
events.event_detail: Workshop: DIY Boondoggle at San Francisco Public Library Anza Branch. This hands-on workshop teaches the art and science of lacing with plastic, where participants learn to twist, weave, and knot to create their own personalized vibrant keychains or accessories. Takes place on Wednesday, June 3, 2026 from 4:00 to 5:00 PM in the Anza General Floor Area. The event is perfect for all skill levels and is designed for children ages 8 and older. All materials are provided by the library as part of the Make + Do program. Drop-in attendance, no registration required. Part of the Summer Stride reading program. Program sponsored by Friends of the San Francisco Public Library.
